items.title: Govt raises petrol price by Rs1.20 per litre, reduces high-speed diesel rate by Re0.17
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · " style="width: 100%; min-height: 50px; max-height: 30000px; border: none; overflow: hidden; display: block;" scrolling="no"> The government on Wednesday raised the price of petrol by Rs1.20 per litre, but reduced that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.17 per litre. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs393.86 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs396.65 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 15 (Thursday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months. On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Achakzai warns governor's rule will next be imposed in Sindh, over water and mines
items.description: Opposition Leader in the National Assembly Mehmood Khan Achakzai warned on Wednesday that governor’s rule would be imposed next in Sindh over the “occupation of water, mines and streams”, urging the Centre to give provinces their rights and resources. He was speaking in the National Assembly, where a resolution endorsing the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Sunday was passed . The federal government cited the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism as the reason for imposing governor’s rule in KP. In days preceding the development, political tensions between the federal government and the opposition, mainly the PTI, had remained high after the party announced a long march to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. However, the march, initially planned for Islamabad, remained confined to KP until it fizzled out with the imposition of governor’s rule in the province. In his address, Achakzai said KP’s “mistake is that it saved itself with the help of its people”. He also drew a comparison between the current situation with regards to KP and the one witnessed at the time of the creation of Bangladesh. He also assailed the government for depriving the PTI of its election symbol ahead of the 2024 general elections. “And the mistake of his (Imran’s) party’s workers was that they contested the elections on 200 different symbols and turned your own game around on you. You are meting out the punishment for that? You are punishing 240 million people of Pakistan for that?” The opposition leader also pointed out that Sohail Afridi, who has become non-functional as the chief minister after the imposition of governor’s rule and had been leading the PTI’s march, had not resorted to violence or using expletives in his call for the protest. He went on to say, “When you try to snatch our right to self-determination, our right to vote, we all will stand against you. All of us, all provinces.” Noting the participation of the PPP, which is in power in Sindh, Achakzai said it pained him. He then warned that governor’s rule would next be imposed in Sindh over the “occupation of water, mines and streams”. “And then you will recall your mistake,” he said, noting however that there was still time to rectify mistakes. “Reverse these decisions,” Achakzai said, urging that Parliament be made the centre of power. “And Pakistan will be saved.” He warned that when the “state turns against its own people, they are compelled to look elsewhere”. The opposition also criticised the government over the country’s economic situation. “You are looting this country’s resources […] Have some mercy on this country. […] This country is drowning because of our mistakes. There is only one way to save it: through its Constitution and Parliament and by having a democratic system,” he asserted. Achakzai also lamented the fact the Parliament was not taken into confidence over decisions related to foreign affairs, and that Pakistan had strained ties with most of its neighbours. On Imran, who has not been allowed meetings with his family and associates for a long time, Achakzai said: “Which provision of the Constitution … places a restriction on meetings with the most popular leader of the country?” He assured that if meetings were arranged with Imran, “we will just try to assess his health condition and will try to resolve matter between you. We promise we will meet him and not tell anyone. […] Have some sense. Negotiate.” He concluded his address by declaring that the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP was wrong.

items.title: Omani FM meets PM Shehbaz, commends Pakistan's 'sustained diplomatic efforts' for regional peace
items.description: Omani Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr Albusaidi called on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday and appreciated Pakistan’s “sustained diplomatic efforts” for de-escalation and peaceful solutions to regional challenges, a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said. Both Pakistan and Oman have been engaged in efforts for de-escalation after US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February resulted in a conflict that has now expanded further into the Middle East. Albusaidi’s meeting with PM Shehbaz was held on the second day of his two-day trip to Pakistan, during which he also attended the eighth session of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC) and held a meeting with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar. In his meeting with the Omani foreign minister, PM Shehbaz “highlighted that the strong bond of shared faith, geography, history, culture, and centuries of people-to-people exchanges between Pakistan and Oman provided a strong fraternal foundation to the bilateral relationship”, the PMO statement said. The premier underscored that Pakistan considered Oman a brotherly country, an important maritime neighbour and a valuable partner in a critically important region, it added. “The prime minister expressed satisfaction over the successful convening of the 8th Session of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission. “He hoped that the meeting would provide a strong foundation for further expanding mutually beneficial cooperation and deepening engagement between the two brotherly countries,” the statement said. It further stated that PM Shehbaz “noted with deep satisfaction the unanimity of views between Pakistan and Oman on all regional and global issues”. He appreciated Oman’s “principled stance” of dialogue and diplomacy in resolving disputes, the statement said. For his part, Albusaidi thanked the government of Pakistan for the hospitality extended to him and his delegation and “expressed satisfaction on successful holding of the 8th JMC session”, the PMO statement said. It added that the Omani foreign minister “agreed that it (JMC session) would pave the way for enhanced bilateral collaboration in diverse sectors for mutual benefit”. “The Omani foreign minister also appreciated Pakistan’s sustained diplomatic efforts towards de-escalating tensions and advancing peaceful solutions to regional challenges,” the statement read. It added that PM Shehbaz also witnessed the signing of the Protocol of the 8th session of the Pakistan-Oman JMC, as well as agreements and memoranda of understanding for bilateral cooperation between the two sides in the areas of media cooperation, news and information exchange, historical documentation and archives management, communication and information technology and facilitation of diplomatic and official exchanges. ‘Totally unacceptable’ Earlier in the day, Albusaidi held a joint press conference with Deputy PM Dar, during which the latter said that Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia were “totally unacceptable”. At the outset of the press conference, Dar said that the two sides would sign a protocol relating to the commission. He said that this reflected “a shared resolve to further strengthen and expand bilateral cooperation in areas of mutual interest”. He said that the two sides would also sign an agreement for mutual visa exemption for holders of diplomatic and official passports. “Pakistan-Oman friendship remains strong and forward-looking,” he told the media. He added that the two ministers had also agreed to hold a business-to-business investment forum in Pakistan. The ministers discussed the situation in the Gulf as well, he said, adding that “Pakistan remained committed to contributing constructively to diplomatic efforts aimed at promoting peace and stability in the region”. Dar said that the two sides also exchanged views on recent Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. He said that he conveyed Pakistan’s condemnation of the attacks. “I underscored that attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure are totally unacceptable. My brother [Albusaidi] actually fully endorses this. Violations of international law pose a serious threat to regional peace and security,” he said. “I reaffirmed Pakistan’s full solidarity with Saudi Arabia and our unwavering commitment to the kingdom’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security in accordance with the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement,” he said. They also “emphasised the urgent need for unhindered delivery of humanitarian assistance to the people of Gaza”, Dar said. DPM Dar also stressed that India’s unilateral abeyance of the Indus Water Treaty was “a material breach of international law”. “This action threatens the water, food and energy security of Pakistan’s 250 million people,” Dar said. Speaking at the occasion, Albusaidi said the JMC had “provided an important opportunity to review the state of bilateral relations”. He said that two sides “reaffirmed the strength of the longstanding ties” between the two countries. “Both Oman and Pakistan attach great importance to dialogue and diplomacy as essential means of addressing regional challenges, easing tensions and promoting peace and stability,” Albusaidi said. He also appreciated Pakistan’s diplomatic role in the US-Iran war . He reaffirmed the two countries’ “shared commitment to further deepening our bilateral partnership and broadening cooperation across centres of mutual benefit”. The two countries agreed that dialogue and diplomacy were “the only way forward” to resolve regional conflicts, Dar said in response to a reporter’s question. “We are both on the same page,” he said. Meanwhile, Dar told reporters that a free trade agreement between Pakistan and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) would help expand business activities, adding that he was told that barring one, all countries had consented to the agreement. Responding to a question about the gaps in bilateral talks between the two countries, Dar said Albusaidi’s visit was previously delayed because Pakistan had been involved in mediation efforts between the US and Iran. Albusaidi added that discussions had continued “behind the scenes”. Responding to a question about the Strait of Hormuz, Albusaidi said that Oman was committed to “unhindered navigation” through the strait “because of its vitality to the global economy and the region”. JMC session The meeting of the commission was co-chaired by Dar and Albusaidi. The two sides “reaffirmed their close fraternal ties and commitment to expanding bilateral cooperation, particularly in trade and investment, maritime and logistics connectivity, agriculture, industry, energy, workforce mobility, human resource development, education, IT, media and climate change, among other areas”, the Foreign Office (FO) said. Both ministers emphasised the importance of strengthening people-to-people ties, facilitating workforce mobility, and promoting exchanges of business delegations from both countries to unlock new opportunities for trade, investment and institutional collaboration. FM Dar stressed the need for “timely implementation of agreed outcomes through close institutional coordination and sustained engagement between joint working group meetings”, the statement added. According to FO, the Oman FM thanked Pakistan for its warm hospitality, appreciated Pakistan’s efforts for regional peace and security, and reaffirmed Muscat’s commitment to further strengthening the longstanding partnership between the two countries. Dar commends Albusaidi’s efforts towards regional peace Speaking at the outset of the JMC session, Dar said the two had “worked out” certain areas of bilateral interest and discussed global issues in detail, including the US-Iran war, the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, Bab al-Mandab and Gaza in their restricted meeting. Dar said the two sides had also discussed Jammu and Kashmir and other pressing regional issues. He commended Albusaidi’s leadership and efforts towards regional peace in the Middle East. “I personally greatly admire your efforts. I know how much hard work you have put in,” he said, noting that Pakistan’s position on the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) was “very unique”. “We are members of both the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) and, obviously, the United Nations and other multilateral bodies,” Dar said. He stressed, “There should not be any long gaps between bilateral engagements,” noting potential in the areas of trade, economic activities and investment opportunities. Dar said he had promised to visit Oman in 2027 to hold the next session of the commission there. He added that both sides had identified areas of mutual interest and discussed possible meetings. He said Pakistan and Oman cooperated closely and cordially, adding that although their diplomatic relations had completed 55 years, their ties went back “centuries”. Dar said the two countries shared a history of “love and affection”, particularly in relation to Balochistan and Gwadar. Referring to discussions on Bab al-Mandab and recent developments involving the Houthis and Saudi Arabia, Dar said both sides shared similar views on resolving regional issues. He said the impact of regional tensions was also visible in Pakistan, where energy supply chains had been affected, and fuel prices had skyrocketed, adding that the “common man could not afford the resulting burden.” Speaking on the occasion, Albusaidi said Oman was committed to further strengthening bilateral engagement and cooperation in various fields that could bring greater benefits to the people of both countries. “I am delighted to be here with my delegation in Islamabad this morning, in this very warm, friendly and brotherly country, Pakistan, with which, as you have rightly said, we share bonds of history, culture, tradition and unity,” he said. He said the Pakistan-Oman JMC was one of the mechanisms for exploring further avenues of collaboration, adding that the two countries also had a business council and a political consultation mechanism between their foreign ministers. “We can do much more, and as we made a joint commitment this morning to make this meeting a success, I believe the more we do, the more we can deliver on the promise and the aspiration of our leaderships and our people,” Albusaidi said. He also commended Pakistan’s role in supporting dialogue and diplomacy in the region. “Your efforts to encourage engagement, understanding, respect and recognition are commendable, and I salute you for all your efforts,” he said, adding that Oman greatly appreciated Pakistan’s role in providing space for dialogue between Iran and the US. Albusaidi said there was significant potential for economic cooperation between Oman and Pakistan, particularly in trade, logistics, port connectivity, energy and food security. “The potential exists, and our task is to remove any obstacles and create the conditions that allow businesses to thrive so that we can fully benefit from this potential,” he said. He also called for greater cooperation in tourism, academic and technological fields, as well as more regular exchanges between the people of the two countries. “Once again, I appreciate the efforts of our private sector and industrial partners,” Albusaidi said, adding that he looked forward to further discussions on strengthening bilateral cooperation. According to a joint statement, the two sides agreed to hold the ninth session of the JMC next year. After the session concluded, Albusaidi posted on that he had a “constructive day” in Islamabad co-chairing JMC session with Dar. “We reviewed practical ways to deepen our longstanding partnership in trade, investment, energy, logistics and other priority areas, and agreed on closer follow-up to turn opportunities into results,” he said, expressing gratitude for the “warm hospitality and the shared commitment to cooperation and regional dialogue”. Dar, Omani FM call for sustained bilateral engagement Earlier in the day, Dar also held a bilateral meeting with Albusaidi ahead of the JMC session, FO said. The visiting dignitary had arrived in Pakistan on Tuesday on a two-day visit. The two ministers reaffirmed the close, fraternal ties between Pakistan and Oman and underscored the importance of sustained high-level engagement to deepen cooperation in areas of mutual interest, particularly trade, investment and people-to-people contacts, according to FO. “The two sides also exchanged views on regional developments and emphasised the importance of dialogue and diplomacy in advancing lasting peace and stability,” FO said. Albusaidi commended Pakistan’s efforts to promote regional peace and security, while Dar acknowledged and appreciated Oman’s constructive role and shared aspirations for regional peace and stability, the statement added. A day earlier, FO said the JMC session would review the entire spectrum of Pakistan-Oman bilateral relations and strengthen cooperation. The visit “reflects the longstanding fraternal relations between Pakistan and Oman and is expected to further deepen mutually beneficial cooperation”.

items.title: Couverture santé: place à l’accès réel aux soins
items.description: Avec 88 % de la population couverte par l’Assurance maladie obligatoire (AMO), contre 42 % auparavant, le Maroc a franchi un cap décisif. Réunis ce mercredi 14 octobre à Marrakech à l’invitation du Conseil de la concurrence, régulateurs, institutions et acteurs économiques ont défini la suite : transformer ce droit en soins accessibles, de qualité et durables, grâce à l’investissement, à une concurrence saine et à l’innovation. Étendre la couverture médicale n’était que la première moitié du chantier. L’autre, plus ingrate, consiste à convertir ce droit nouveau en soins réellement accessibles, de bonne qualité et finançables dans la durée. C’est sur ce terrain que s’est ouverte, ce mercredi 14 octobre au Palais des Congrès de Marrakech, la conférence internationale que le Conseil de la concurrence consacre à la politique de santé, sous l’angle de la concurrence, de la régulation et de la gouvernance. Le passage à une couverture quasi universelle redistribue en effet les rôles. Prestataires de soins, établissements hospitaliers, industriels du médicament, distributeurs et organismes de remboursement évoluent désormais dans un système où la dépense médicale repose davantage sur la solidarité collective. Le secteur privé y gagne une place centrale, avec ses promesses d’investissement et ses risques de concentration. L’édifice, lui, s’expose à un coût difficile à tenir et à une répartition inégale entre grandes villes et territoires reculés. Quatre voix ont ouvert la séance, chacune éclairant une facette de ce défi. Investir sans verrouiller le marché Le président du Conseil de la concurrence, Ahmed Rahhou, a plaidé pour un secteur de la santé plus attractif, capable de drainer les investissements et de créer de la valeur ajoutée. Il y voit la condition d’une concurrence saine, respectueuse de la loi et de l’éthique, soucieuse de la qualité des prestations comme de la soutenabilité de leur coût. Le secteur privé, qui occupe une place importante dans l’écosystème, est à ses yeux un maillon essentiel pour concrétiser le chantier royal de généralisation de la protection sociale. L’appel à investir s’accompagne d’une mise en garde. Ahmed Rahhou ne conteste pas les vertus des regroupements d’opérateurs, qui permettent de mutualiser les équipements, d’étoffer les plateaux techniques et de mieux organiser la permanence des soins. Il refuse toutefois que ces opérations dressent des barrières devant de nouveaux venus, installent des rentes de situation ou faussent l’équilibre entre l’offre et la demande. Sa conception de la régulation fait de la transparence des règles et de leur application équitable à tous un principe cardinal, sans écarter la coopération et l’échange d’informations entre opérateurs lorsqu’ils servent la continuité des soins. Le Conseil, a-t-il rappelé, a déjà consacré plusieurs travaux au secteur, notamment sur le circuit de distribution des médicaments et sur la fixation de leurs prix. Autre front, celui des ressources humaines et des territoires. Le président du Conseil de la concurrence a relevé une répartition déséquilibrée des professionnels de santé entre secteurs public et privé, mais aussi entre des centres urbains, où la demande est forte et le pouvoir d’achat plus élevé, et des zones éloignées qui en manquent. Il appelle à assouplir les frontières entre les deux secteurs pour mieux mobiliser compétences et équipements, et à régionaliser la formation médicale afin de retenir les praticiens hors des régions les plus attractives. À défaut, a-t-il averti, les écarts géographiques et sociaux risquent de se muer en obstacles à l’accès aux soins. La technologie lui paraît le levier le plus prometteur pour résorber ces écarts. Télémédecine, intelligence artificielle appliquée au diagnostic et robotique pourraient élargir l’accès aux spécialités sans imposer systématiquement des déplacements aux patients ou aux praticiens. Ahmed Rahhou en a livré la formule : l’avenir de la médecine ne consiste pas forcément à envoyer les médecins vers les gens, mais à « amener la médecine chez les gens ». Ces outils, a-t-il précisé, doivent seconder les soignants et non les remplacer. Tous les acteurs sont appelés à conjuguer leurs efforts, et le Conseil se dit prêt à y prendre sa part, dans l’intérêt du citoyen et dans le cadre des hautes instructions royales. Mesurer l’accès, non les inscrits Le président du Conseil économique, social et environnemental, Abdelkader Amara, a, quant à lui, salué une avancée considérable : 88 % de la population bénéficie désormais d’une couverture sanitaire, un chantier auquel le roi Mohammed VI accorde une attention particulière. L’indicateur, a-t-il aussitôt nuancé, ne dit pas tout. La réussite de la réforme ne se mesure pas au nombre d’assurés inscrits, mais à leur capacité d’accéder réellement aux soins, au moment où ils en ont besoin, avec la qualité requise et dans des délais raisonnables. La protection inscrite dans la loi doit devenir une protection effective, adossée à la continuité des droits et à l’équilibre financier du système, y compris pour les bénéficiaires de l’AMO Tadamon. Cet accès réel suppose, selon Abdelkader Amara, un hôpital public plus attractif pour les professionnels et de meilleures conditions de travail. La cherté des soins dans le privé rend indispensable un secteur public capable de servir des prestations de qualité, en particulier aux populations les plus vulnérables. Quant à la concurrence, il la juge utile à condition de ne pas en faire une fin en soi : la santé n’étant pas un secteur comme les autres, elle doit servir à améliorer les services, à stimuler l’innovation et à orienter l’investissement vers les besoins réels et les zones sous-dotées. Il propose de juger la gouvernance à l’aune d’indicateurs concrets, tels que le délai pour décrocher un rendez-vous ou consulter un spécialiste, et réclame un meilleur encadrement des prix des médicaments. Tenir la dépense pour pérenniser le droit De son côté, le directeur général de la Caisse nationale de sécurité sociale, Hassan Boubrik, a rappelé l’ampleur prise par l’assurance maladie obligatoire, qui a couvert près de 25 millions de bénéficiaires en 2025 grâce à l’élargissement de la base et à la simplification de l’accès, notamment par la numérisation. Cette montée en charge pèse désormais sur les équilibres : les prestations servies par la CNSS au titre de l’AMO ont atteint 23 milliards de dirhams en 2025, en hausse de 17 % sur un an. Hassan Boubrik appelle donc à chercher des ressources supplémentaires et à mieux maîtriser les dépenses, sans que le niveau des cotisations ne freine l’adhésion. Un secteur public fort, articulé avec le privé, demeure à ses yeux la condition d’une couverture universelle durable. La régulation est son second chantier. Hassan Boubrik estime que la santé n’est pas un marché ordinaire et préconise le recours accru aux génériques et aux biosimilaires, la maîtrise des prix des médicaments, l’actualisation des tarifs de référence et des listes de médicaments remboursables, ainsi que la prévention et la coordination des parcours de soins. Il plaide pour un durcissement des contrôles contre la surfacturation, les actes injustifiés et la fraude, et pour que la Haute Autorité de santé reçoive les moyens de sa mission. Il demande aussi plus de transparence et de célérité dans l’évaluation des médicaments innovants, afin que tous les patients y accèdent sans discrimination. Des règles, fait-il valoir, ne valent que si des mécanismes d’application, des compétences et des moyens humains et techniques leur donnent vie. Bâtir l’offre au rythme de la demande Le président de la Confédération générale des entreprises du Maroc, Mehdi Tazi, a, pour sa part, déplacé le débat vers l’autre versant de la réforme : l’offre. Les bénéficiaires de l’AMO sont passés de 42 % à 88 % de la population, soit plus de 32 millions de Marocains, et la demande de soins s’en trouve démultipliée. « Il faut maintenant que l’offre de santé grandisse au même rythme que la demande », a résumé Mehdi Tazi. Le secteur privé est appelé à y prendre toute sa part. Il compte aujourd’hui 475 cliniques totalisant plus de 20 000 lits, 280 centres d’hémodialyse, 850 laboratoires d’analyses et plus de 15 000 cabinets médicaux, mais les besoins demeurent immenses dans les territoires sous-équipés. La CGEM veut qu’un citoyen de Guelmim, de Béni Mellal ou de Casablanca accède à des soins de même qualité, ce qui suppose de lever les freins que citent les opérateurs : pénurie de ressources humaines qualifiées, rareté du foncier, lourdeur des procédures et délais d’autorisation. La concurrence qu’il appelle de ses vœux ne doit pas se limiter à une bataille sur les prix, mais se jouer sur la qualité, l’investissement et l’expérience du patient. Elle doit également favoriser l’arrivée de nouveaux entrants sur le marché, plutôt que de se cantonner à la surveillance des acteurs déjà installés. Reste la question des tarifs. La tarification nationale de référence, qui fonde les remboursements de l’AMO, date encore de 2006 pour nombre d’actes : une consultation de médecine générale demeure calculée sur 80 dirhams, celle d’un spécialiste sur 150. Vingt ans plus tard, l’écart avec le coût réel des soins retombe souvent sur les patients, d’où l’urgence de la révision en cours, jugée indispensable par les professionnels. L’équation financière se tend d’autant plus qu’entre 2022 et 2024, les dépenses de l’AMO ont progressé de 83 % quand les ressources n’augmentaient que de 36 %. Pour Mehdi Tazi, la sortie passe aussi par l’innovation : télémédecine, intelligence artificielle et partage sécurisé des données médicales pourraient réduire les inégalités territoriales, affiner les diagnostics et fluidifier les parcours de soins, à condition d’un cadre clair qui protège les patients et garantisse un usage responsable des données. The post Couverture santé: place à l’accès réel aux soins appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Pakistani, Chinese armies begin joint training exercise in Xinjiang
items.description: GILGIT: A joint training exercise of Pakistani and Chinese armies, “Karakoram 2026”, began in the Xinjiang province of China on Wednesday. The opening ceremony of Karakoram 2026 was held at a training base in Korla city, according to the China Military Bugle, the official media account of Beijing’s armed forces. The two sides exchanged counter-terrorism experience and Pakistani troops observed some Chinese weapons and equipment. Before the drill commenced, Colonel Chen Xi, the press secretary of China’s defence ministry, said last week that the exercise would help the two sides deepen exchanges and cooperation and enhance their ability to jointly respond to the threat of terrorism. He said the training would focus on “joint anti-terrorism clearance operations at high altitudes”. The press secretary added that the drills would involve drone operation, on-the-move target search and firing, and long-range sniping, and would cover “joint command and live-force exercises”, according to China’s Xinhua news agency. Pakistan and China share a longstanding strategic partnership. In September, the two countries held a joint patrolling exercise at Mantika Pass, at an altitude of approximately 4,700 metres, near Khunjerab top situated in the upper area of GB’s Hunza. In May, they reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral military cooperation and strategic coordination. Additional input from Anadolu Agency

items.title: Pope out of bed, progress ‘normal’ after cancer operation
items.description: Pope Leo XIV is out of bed, walking and eating after doctors removed a cancerous tumour from his lung, while post-surgery tests show his progress is “normal”, his doctors said Wednesday. Part of the pope’s right lung was removed in Tuesday’s operation at Rome’s Gemelli hospital and the leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics is now awaiting the results of a biopsy to determine if the cancer has spread. Blood tests and a chest X-ray meanwhile “confirm a normal post-operative course”, doctors Luigi Carbone and Stefano Margaritora said in a statement released by the Vatican. “The values are within the expected range for the type of procedure performed,” they said. The discovery on Tuesday that a nodule detected in Leo’s lung was cancerous has plunged the Catholic Church into a period of uncertainty. “It’s a shock for everyone. We’re in ‘wait-and-see’ mode,” a Vatican source told AFP. Doctors said his recovery was “proceeding as expected” and the pontiff had eaten both breakfast and lunch, been walking about his room, and had done some respiratory physiotherapy. Another Vatican source said the pope had even celebrated a mass on Wednesday in a specially prepared room on the 10th floor of the hospital, where is staying. The papal suite on the same floor is where popes are usually treated. It has a private chapel but is currently being refurbished. – ‘Show my spiritual support’ – The sporty 71-year-old, elected as the first pope from the United States only last year, made the surprise announcement that he would be undergoing surgery after Sunday prayers. Messages of support flooded in from around the world, including from Britain’s King Charles III, who is also being treated for an undisclosed cancer. A banner flying outside the hospital read “Long live the pope!” and a handful of people recited prayers for the hospitalised pontiff. Nearby, nun Angele Bilegue said she had come to pray for Leo. “I’m not worried. I came to express my closeness, to show my spiritual support, because I also came for Pope Francis,” she told AFP. Leo’s predecessor, the Argentine Francis, spent five weeks last year being treated for double pneumonia at the same hospital, before his death at the Vatican on April 21, 2025. Experts said much would depend on how advanced Leo’s cancer was, and whether it had spread, but the Vatican has said it had been detected early and was localised. Before the operation, the Vatican said the pope’s recovery should take around a week. All his audiences have been cancelled until October 20. “If we are dealing with stage I or II disease, and recovery is good… the patient can resume a normal life and usual activities within a few weeks,” Alain Gelibter, an oncologist at Rome’s Policlinico Umberto I hospital, told AFP. The Chicago-born Leo had entered the hospital smiling and waving on Tuesday. In the hospital chapel, dozens of faithful prayed for the pope’s health during the operation. – New uncertainty – The shock news of the tennis-playing pope’s illness has rattled the Catholic Church. Expert Marco Politi, who has spent decades covering the Vatican, told AFP: “The Church is now in a state of uncertainty. When Leo was elected everyone foresaw a long papacy.” Hendro Munsterman, a theologian and expert for Dutch newspaper Nederlands Dagblad, told AFP “we have a pope whom everyone described as young, active and athletic. Now, we have a pope who also has his own vulnerabilities, which will change his image.” His health issues may prompt him to speed up personnel appointments, Munsterman said. Politi said Leo had been working on “repairing” rifts between various wings of the Church, and many will want him “to continue with this important mission as soon as possible”. Filipino Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle, newly nominated to the influential role of dean of the College of Cardinals, celebrated mass on St Peter’s Square on Wednesday instead of Leo. The surgery has raised questions about whether Leo will go ahead with a lengthy visit next month to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, where he worked as a missionary for two decades. items.title: Barcola scores hat-trick as Liverpool thrash LASK 6-3 in Champions League
items.description: Bradley Barcola silenced his critics as the Liverpool forward ended his goal drought with a hat-trick in a chaotic 6-3 win against LASK in the Champions League on Wednesday. Barcola had come under fire for some lacklustre performances since his blockbuster £123 million ($161 million) move from Paris Saint-Germain in August. But the France forward finally started to live up to his hefty price tag with his first goals for Liverpool in his seventh appearance. Barcola struck twice before the interval at the Raiffeisen Arena after Ronald Araujo put Liverpool ahead in the first half with his maiden goal for the club. Jeremie Frimpong netted the fourth after the break against the Austrian champions before Barcola completed his treble. There was still time for Lewis Koumas to score his first Champions League goal as Liverpool maintained their 100 percent record in this season’s tournament after beating Atletico Madrid in their opening game. It was a welcome boost for Iraola following his first defeat in eight games as Liverpool manager when Premier League leaders Manchester City won 3-0 at Anfield on Sunday. Iraola this week said he has “100 per cent” trust in Barcola and Florian Wirtz, who has struggled mightily since joining from Bayer Leverkusen last year. Injuries to Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai, who all missed the trip to Austria, increased the pressure on Wirtz and Barcola to carry the Liverpool attack. The pair repaid Iraola’s faith with a much-needed display of their undoubted qualities. Now Iraola will demand they produce that level of intensity and quality on a regular basis. The trip to Linz was the second of six games in 18 days for Liverpool, forcing Iraola to make changes in a bid to save his players from burnout. Reds captain Virgil van Dijk, Milos Kerkez, Alexis Mac Allister and Victor Munoz were all rested as Frimpong, Kostas Tsimikas, Trey Nyoni and Rio Ngumoha came in. – Clinical Barcola – After some disjointed displays at the start of Iraola’s reign, this was an indication of what they can become under the former Bournemouth boss, although he will still be concerned about their defensive issues. Araujo put Liverpool ahead in the 22nd minute, rising highest to meet Tsimikas’s corner with a thumping header past LASK keeper Lukas Jungwirth. The on-loan Barcelona defender’s goal was swiftly followed by one for Barcola 96 seconds later. Ngumoha was the catalyst with an incisive run into the LASK area and Barcola applied the finishing touch as he guided a clinical finish beyond Jungwirth. Iraola’s men were running riot and Barcola scored their third in the 37th minute. It was a riposte to the criticism of Wirtz and Barcola as the pair combined to cut through the LASK defence. Barcola picked out Wirtz and the German played a pinpoint return pass that allowed the 24-year-old to fire past Jungwirth. Frimpong has also frustrated Liverpool fans since signing last year, making his goal in the 51st minute a welcome tonic for the Dutch right-back. Tsimikas got to the byline and lofted a cross towards Frimpong, who belied his diminutive stature with a towering header into the bottom corner. Robert Ljubicic reduced the deficit in the 63rd minute with a composed finish from Yvan Dibango’s pass. But Barcola sealed his treble with a nimble finish from Frimpong’s pass in the 66th minute. Teed up by Frimpong, Koumas hit Liverpool’s sixth with a searing strike in the 72nd minute. Despite the introduction of Van Dijk and fellow defender Joe Gomez, Liverpool lost control in the closing stages. Florian Flecker’s diving header two minutes later punished slack Liverpool defending. Flecker struck again with a close-range finish in the 77th minute, but nothing could spoil Barcola’s big night. items.title: La Fiscalía abre la puerta a que la Audiencia Nacional investigue a Julio Iglesias por agresión sexual
items.description: La Fiscalía ha cambiado de criterio sobre la denuncia presentada contra el cantante Julio Iglesias por presunta agresión sexual a dos extrabajadoras y, según confirman fuentes del ministerio público, se ha posicionado ahora a favor de que la Audiencia Nacional pueda llevar a cabo una investigación . El fiscal Vicente González Mota ya ha enviado un escrito al juez instructor Antonio Piña para comunicarle que, según su opinión, tiene competencia para abrir una causa contra el artista tras recibir una nueva querella contra el músico por supuestos delitos cometidos “en 2021 en propiedades de Iglesias ubicadas en las Bahamas y en la República Dominicana”. El magistrado deberá decidir en los próximos días si inicia unas pesquisas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Mahdia | Décès d’un jeune de 28 ans après l’incendie d’un dépôt de carburant de contrebande
items.description: Un jeune homme de 28 ans a succombé à ses blessures ce mercredi 14 octobre au matin à l'hôpital universitaire Taïeb Sfar de Mahdia, des suites de graves brûlures. Le drame s'était produit le dimanche 11 octobre 2026, lorsqu'un violent incendie s'est déclaré dans un dépôt clandestin de carburant de contrebande. Touchée sur l'ensemble du corps, la victime avait subi des brûlures du troisième degré. Malgré sa prise en charge rapide en soins intensifs, le jeune homme n'a pas survécu à ses blessures. Les unités de la Protection civile étaient intervenues sur les lieux dès le déclenchement du sinistre pour circonscrire les flammes et évacuer les victimes. Y. N. items.title: GRA submits preliminary report on drug shipment case to Mahama – Commissioner-General
items.description: The Commissioner-General of the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA), Anthony Kwasi Sarpong, has disclosed that a preliminary investigation report into the recent drug shipment case involving containers that left Ghana has been submitted to President John Dramani Mahama. He said the Authority was also working with the relevant security agencies to establish the full details of the incident and support efforts to address the concerns surrounding the shipment. Mr Sarpong made the disclosure when he appeared before Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee (PAC), in response to concerns about the reputational damage the drug-related cases could cause Ghana. The question was raised by the Member of Parliament for Mpraeso and Vice-Chairperson of the Committee, Davis Ansah Opoku, who sought clarity on measures being taken to address the situation. Mr Sarpong described drug trafficking as a serious concern for the GRA and called for collective efforts to prevent the country from being used as a transit point for narcotics. He also revealed that the Authority regularly intercepts drugs and arrests suspected traffickers at the country’s entry and exit points, although such operations are not always made public. According to him, publicising every interception could alert drug traffickers and allow them to devise new methods to evade detection. Meanwhile, the GRA has urged taxpayers to take advantage of tax reliefs available under the law, saying many eligible individuals are missing out because of limited awareness. Mr Sarpong said the Authority was intensifying public education to ensure taxpayers understood the reliefs available to them under the Revenue Administration framework and the relevant tax laws, including the Income Tax Act, 2015 (Act 896). He said the GRA was committed to helping eligible taxpayers access the benefits provided by law and was working to improve awareness of the applicable requirements. The Commissioner-General also addressed issues relating to online cross-border transactions and attempts by some financial institutions to impose additional percentage charges on products. He explained that consumers were already paying the applicable 20 per cent charge but were not always aware of it, adding that the Authority was seeking to formalise the arrangement.

items.title: Man United line up three-man shortlist as sack looms for Michael Carrick
items.description: Manchester United are reportedly considering Brighton and Hove Albion manager Fabian Hurzeler, former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte as potential replacements for Michael Carrick if the club decides to part ways with its current manager. According to talkSPORT, the three managers have attracted interest from different figures within the Old Trafford hierarchy as pressure mounts on Carrick following a difficult run of results. United’s reported interest comes after their 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday, which extended their winless run to five matches across all competitions. The result also followed a 1-1 draw against Tottenham Hotspur, a run of form that has raised concerns about the team’s performances and Carrick’s tactical decisions. The defeat to Atletico also prompted defender Lisandro Martinez to criticise technical director Jason Wilcox over what he reportedly viewed as insufficient squad strengthening. United will look to end their poor run when they face historic rivals Leeds United in the Premier League on Sunday. Speaking on talkSPORT Breakfast, the station’s chief live football anchor, Adrian Durham, suggested Carrick’s position could become increasingly difficult if the team fails to improve. “Does it feel like an inevitability? Absolutely, that Michael Carrick will go,” Durham said. He added that Carrick would need to turn around the team’s results to improve his chances of remaining in the job. Durham also expressed concerns about Carrick’s tactical decisions in the Atletico Madrid match, arguing that some of the changes made during the game contributed to United’s defeat. Among the three reported candidates, Nagelsmann and Conte are said to be available for an immediate appointment. Conte left Napoli by mutual consent in May, while Nagelsmann reportedly departed his position as Germany coach following the country’s elimination by Paraguay in the round of 32 at the World Cup. The report said United’s director of recruitment, Christopher Vivell, was advocating for Nagelsmann internally as a potential successor should the club decide to dismiss Carrick. Hurzeler, meanwhile, remains under contract with Brighton until 2029 after signing an extension in May. The German coach is reportedly favoured by Wilcox and has overseen a strong start to the Premier League season, with Brighton winning four of their opening six matches to sit third in the standings. Hurzeler has also guided Brighton to victory over Manchester United in the third round of the EFL Cup in September, adding to his credentials as a potential candidate. However, Manchester United have not been reported to have made a formal appointment decision, and Carrick’s immediate future could depend on the team’s results in the coming matches. The post Man United line up three-man shortlist as sack looms for Michael Carrick appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Sammy Gyamfi using ‘procedural roadblocks’ to dodge defamation case? – Afenyo-Markin’s lawyers
items.description: Lawyers for Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin have accused Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi of using procedural tactics to avoid responding to their client’s GH¢15 million defamation suit. The accusation comes after the High Court in Accra set aside the suit on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, ruling that the writ of summons did not sufficiently specify the statements alleged to be defamatory. In a statement, Mr Afenyo-Markin’s legal team questioned why Mr Gyamfi had allegedly focused on procedural issues instead of filing a defence to the allegations. The lawyers said Mr Gyamfi’s legal representatives, Ayine & Partners, had written to the court on August 26 confirming their authority to accept service of the writ on his behalf. They said the court bailiff subsequently served the documents on the law firm, but the lawyers returned them to the court registry the following day, indicating that their client had changed his mind. According to Mr Afenyo-Markin’s lawyers, a subsequent attempt to serve the documents personally on Mr Gyamfi at his office was unsuccessful, with the GoldBod CEO allegedly refusing to accept them. The legal team argued that under the High Court (Civil Procedure) Rules, 2004 (C.I. 47), service should be considered complete once a lawyer has undertaken in writing to accept court documents on behalf of a client. However, the High Court, presided over by Justice Akwasi Agyenim Boateng, ruled that the writ was defective because it failed to sufficiently particularise the alleged defamatory statements, as required under Order 57, Rule 2 of C.I. 47. The ruling addressed the procedural requirements for filing a defamation case and did not determine whether Mr Gyamfi’s comments were defamatory. Mr Afenyo-Markin’s lawyers have criticised the decision, arguing that procedural irregularities should not be allowed to undermine substantive justice. They said they were yet to receive a copy of the court’s ruling as of 4:00 p.m. on Wednesday and would determine their next steps after reviewing it. The lawyers added that they had instructions from their client to pursue the matter to its logical conclusion. The dispute followed comments made by Mr Gyamfi on JoyNews’ Newsfile programme in August 2026, during which he described Mr Afenyo-Markin as an “extortionist” amid a public debate over the Bank of Ghana’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme. Mr Afenyo-Markin subsequently sued Mr Gyamfi and Multimedia Group Limited, the parent company of JoyNews, seeking GH¢15 million in damages, a retraction, an apology and a permanent injunction against further publication of the alleged defamatory statements.

items.title: 15-Octobre : « Au Mémorial Thomas Sankara, nous voulons que chaque visiteur reparte enrichi et marqué par son histoire », souligne Pengdwendé Kima, guide
items.description: Trente-neuf ans après l'assassinat de Thomas Sankara et de ses douze compagnons, leur mémoire continue de nourrir la conscience historique de nombreux Burkinabè et admirateurs à travers le monde. Au Mémorial Thomas Sankara, chaque statue, chaque tombe et chaque vestige raconte une page de cette histoire. Guide sur le site, Pengdwendé Kima décrypte la portée de ce lieu emblématique et lance un appel à la connaissance, à la transmission et à l'appropriation de l'héritage sankariste. Lefaso.net : Pouvez-vous nous présenter le Mémorial Thomas Sankara ? Pengdwendé Kima : Le Mémorial Thomas Sankara est un projet né de la réflexion d'un certain nombre d'acteurs qui souhaitaient préserver la mémoire de Thomas Sankara afin qu'elle ne tombe pas dans l'oubli de l'histoire. Nous savons tous qui était cet homme et ce qu'il a voulu pour le Burkina Faso, mais aussi pour le continent africain et, au-delà, pour toute l'humanité. Le combat de Thomas Sankara consistait à faire en sorte que le monde vive dans la paix, la quiétude et l'égalité, et que personne ne soit victime de violences ou de discriminations en raison de sa couleur de peau, de sa condition sociale ou de sa situation. Je pense que telle était la vision de ce grand homme. C'est au regard de sa contribution à l'humanité que des acteurs ont décidé, à un moment donné, de mettre en place un mémorial destiné à préserver ses idéaux et à transmettre l'héritage national et international qu'il nous a laissé. L'objectif est de faire vivre cet héritage et d'empêcher qu'il ne disparaisse avec le temps. Voilà, en substance, l'idée qui a présidé à la création du Mémorial Thomas-Sankara. Quelle est la vocation du mémorial et que découvrent les visiteurs au cours de la visite ? Au sein du mémorial, nous, les guides, travaillons à faire en sorte que les visiteurs repartent enrichis par ce qu'ils ont appris et soient profondément marqués par l'histoire de Thomas Sankara. Lorsque les visiteurs arrivent, nous leur présentons d'abord les douze compagnons qui ont été assassinés avec lui, notamment à travers les statues qui leur rendent hommage. Nous expliquons également le rôle que chacun jouait pendant la révolution. Nous leur présentons ensuite le Conseil de l'Entente et expliquons pourquoi cet espace occupe une place importante dans l'histoire de la révolution. C'est ici que Thomas Sankara avait établi son quartier général pour mener son combat politique. Après cette présentation historique, nous conduisons les visiteurs sur le lieu où Thomas Sankara a été assassiné, puis nous leur faisons découvrir le bâtiment dans lequel il travaillait. C'est dans ce bâtiment que Sankara a développé et porté de nombreuses idées qui ont contribué à faire connaître le Burkina Faso sur la scène internationale. On peut le considérer comme le lieu d'où ont jailli une grande partie des idées qui ont marqué sa révolution et son engagement en faveur du peuple. Nous faisons également découvrir aux visiteurs son bureau, qui témoigne de la simplicité et de l'humilité de l'homme. Thomas Sankara n'était pas un adepte du luxe. Le luxe ostentatoire ne faisait pas partie de ses habitudes, alors même qu'il aurait pu choisir un autre mode de vie. À travers cette visite, nous voulons montrer que ses idéaux se reflétaient aussi dans sa manière de vivre. Quels sont les autres éléments historiques et symboliques que les visiteurs découvrent au mémorial ? Après la présentation du bureau de Thomas Sankara, nous abordons également l'histoire de sa dépouille et les circonstances de son inhumation. Après son assassinat, ses adversaires ne se sont pas contentés de lui ôter la vie. Sa tombe a été profanée et son corps aurait été enterré dans une fosse très peu profonde, qui aurait mesuré à peine 40 centimètres. Il a fallu attendre plusieurs années avant que des travaux d'aménagement puissent être envisagés sur le site. En 2015, la tombe de Thomas Sankara a été exhumée dans le cadre d'une procédure judiciaire, afin de procéder à des examens d'identification. Les résultats ont confirmé son identité. Cependant, de nombreuses controverses ont entouré la question du lieu où il devait être inhumé. Certains estimaient qu'il devait reposer à Dagnoën, tandis que d'autres évoquaient différents lieux, notamment le jardin de l'Amitié. Ces débats ont longtemps marqué les discussions autour de sa mémoire et de son lieu de repos. Finalement, le 23 février 2023, Thomas Sankara et ses compagnons ont été réinhumés dans la dignité et l'honneur. Nous poursuivons ensuite la visite en présentant les tombes avant de terminer par la voiture militaire de Thomas Sankara, qui se trouve derrière moi. Nous expliquons aux visiteurs ce que représente ce véhicule et comment il témoigne de l'humilité de l'homme. Sankara aurait pu s'offrir des voitures de luxe, mais il n'a jamais voulu mener une vie fastueuse pendant que son peuple vivait dans la misère. Nous évoquons également son mariage avec son épouse, Mariam Sankara, dont nous saluons la combativité et le courage. Elle a contribué à préserver la mémoire de son mari afin que son héritage ne soit pas jeté dans l'oubli. C'est une grande dame qui a marqué son époque et qui continue de marquer les esprits. Voilà, de manière générale, ce que nous transmettons aux visiteurs sur les plans historique et intellectuel à travers l'héritage de Thomas Sankara. Il faut également souligner la dimension éducative du mémorial. Nous organisons notamment des visites thématiques destinées aux jeunes. Au cours de ces visites, nous expliquons les citations de Thomas Sankara ainsi que les enseignements, les idéaux et la vision qu'il défendait. Nous aidons ainsi les visiteurs à mieux comprendre la portée historique et idéologique de ses paroles. Nous présentons enfin l'histoire du Conseil de l'Entente, créé dans un contexte marqué par les enjeux politiques de l'époque et les débats autour de l'unité africaine. Selon notre analyse, cette organisation s'inscrivait dans un contexte de rivalités politiques et d'influences extérieures, alors que plusieurs initiatives visaient à fédérer les pays africains. Thomas Sankara avait compris que les divisions du continent constituaient un obstacle à son émancipation. C'est notamment pour cette raison qu'il avait choisi d'installer son quartier général dans cet espace, afin d'y mener son combat politique et idéologique. Quelle est la symbolique architecturale du mausolée de Thomas Sankara et de ses douze compagnons ? Le mausolée que vous voyez ici abrite les tombes de Thomas Sankara et de ses compagnons. Comme je l'ai indiqué, ils ont été réinhumés ici le 23 février 2023. Il faut souligner que cette architecture n'est ni chinoise, ni française, ni américaine, ni japonaise. C'est une architecture profondément burkinabè, qui met en valeur le savoir-faire local. De son vivant, Thomas Sankara a toujours encouragé l'expertise endogène. C'est dans cet esprit qu'il invitait les Burkinabè à oser pour inventer l'avenir. Ce joyau architectural est l'œuvre de Francis Kéré, architecte burkinabè de renommée internationale et lauréat du prix Pritzker d'architecture en 2022. L'architecture du mausolée porte également une dimension symbolique. Elle rappelle les différentes réalisations de la révolution de Thomas Sankara. Même si tous les projets n'ont pas pu être achevés de son vivant, il nous appartient aujourd'hui de poursuivre le combat et de faire vivre ses idéaux. Comme il l'avait lui-même affirmé, nous devons oser. Il nous appartient donc de continuer la lutte, malgré les difficultés et les risques qu'elle peut comporter. Je pense que le président Ibrahim Traoré a également choisi de s'inscrire dans cet héritage politique et symbolique. Il reprend certains codes associés à Thomas Sankara, notamment à travers sa tenue militaire, son béret et son engagement affiché en faveur de la souveraineté du Burkina Faso. Aujourd'hui, l'intérêt pour Thomas Sankara demeure important, aussi bien au niveau national qu'international. Si vous observez le mausolée, vous remarquerez également des ouvertures qui symbolisent le vide laissé par les treize hommes assassinés. Chacun avait une épouse, des enfants, des parents et des proches. Leur disparition a donc laissé un vide immense dans leurs familles et dans la société. Les tombes sont également orientées vers le sud. Selon l'explication symbolique que nous transmettons aux visiteurs, cette orientation représente le fait que Thomas Sankara et ses compagnons sont morts dans la force de l'âge, sans avoir eu la possibilité de vieillir. En Afrique, le parcours du soleil peut être associé aux différentes étapes de la vie humaine. Le soleil se lève à l'est, atteint son zénith, puis poursuit sa course vers l'ouest. De la même manière, l'être humain naît, grandit, atteint la plénitude de sa vie, puis vieillit. Thomas Sankara et ses compagnons étaient encore dans la force de l'âge lorsqu'ils ont été assassinés. Ils n'ont malheureusement pas eu la possibilité de parvenir à la vieillesse. La nature nous enseigne également que, dans la forêt, ce sont généralement les arbres les plus anciens qui tombent et laissent la place aux plus jeunes, permettant ainsi le renouvellement de la végétation. La mort prématurée de ces hommes représente donc une rupture dans le cycle naturel de la vie. Une autre particularité du mausolée concerne la lumière. Au-dessus de chaque tombe, des ouvertures permettent aux rayons du soleil de pénétrer dans l'espace. Lorsque le soleil atteint son zénith, ses rayons peuvent éclairer simultanément les tombes. Selon l'interprétation symbolique de l'artiste, cette lumière évoque la période où ces hommes étaient encore en vie. Lorsque le soleil décline vers l'ouest, la lumière disparaît progressivement, symbolisant leur absence. Enfin, vue d'en haut, la structure du mausolée évoque un œil. Celui-ci représente la vision de Thomas Sankara : sa vision politique, idéologique et globale pour le Burkina Faso, mais aussi pour l'ensemble du continent africain. Voilà, dans les grandes lignes, la symbolique architecturale du mausolée de Thomas Sankara et de ses compagnons. Quels sont les différents profils de visiteurs que vous accueillez au mémorial ? Nous accueillons plusieurs catégories de visiteurs. Parmi eux figurent des personnalités politiques, notamment des présidents et des ministres. Nous recevons également des visiteurs internationaux venus de différents pays, notamment de Chine, des États-Unis et du Japon. Des personnes venues de différents continents ont déjà foulé le sol du Mémorial Thomas-Sankara. Pour ce qui concerne le continent africain, nous recevons également des visiteurs de nombreux pays. Au niveau national, les profils sont tout aussi variés. Nous accueillons des élèves, des étudiants, des commerçants, des agriculteurs, des fonctionnaires et des personnes exerçant différentes activités professionnelles. En somme, le mémorial reçoit des personnes issues de toutes les catégories sociales. Lorsque les visiteurs repartent, ils emportent avec eux de nouvelles connaissances sur la vision de Thomas Sankara. Cette vision devait permettre aux Burkinabè de sortir de l'ornière, de prendre leur destin en main et d'assumer leur place dans l'histoire sans aucun complexe, comme il l'avait lui-même défendu. Peut-on dire que le public burkinabè s'intéresse de plus en plus à l'histoire de Thomas Sankara ? Oui, évidemment. Il faut saluer le peuple burkinabè et sa résilience. Malgré la crise sécuritaire et les difficultés économiques auxquelles le pays est confronté, de nombreuses personnes trouvent les moyens de venir visiter le mémorial en famille. Même lorsque les ressources financières sont limitées, certaines familles font l'effort de consacrer 1 000 ou 2 000 francs CFA à cette visite. Lorsqu'elles arrivent, nous constatons un enthousiasme remarquable. Les visiteurs manifestent un intérêt grandissant pour l'histoire de Thomas Sankara et pour la vision qu'il portait pour le Burkina Faso. Beaucoup sont profondément émus lorsqu'ils découvrent les circonstances de sa mort et prennent conscience de l'ampleur de ses ambitions pour le pays. Certains ont même du mal à retenir leurs larmes, ce qui témoigne de leur attachement à sa personne et à ses idéaux. Je pense donc que les Burkinabè s'intéressent de plus en plus à leur histoire. Il ne s'agit pas uniquement de l'histoire de Thomas Sankara, mais aussi de celle du Burkina Faso et de l'ensemble du continent africain. Les citoyens veulent comprendre d'où nous venons, où nous en sommes et vers quelle destination nous souhaitons aller. Il faut également saluer l'intérêt grandissant de la population pour les questions géopolitiques. Aujourd'hui, même des personnes qui ne sont pas allées à l'école s'intéressent à l'actualité internationale et cherchent à comprendre les événements qui se déroulent à Washington, en Chine, en Russie ou ailleurs, ainsi que leurs conséquences pour nos pays. À mon avis, cette évolution témoigne d'une volonté croissante d'émancipation et de compréhension des enjeux internationaux. Je pense également que les appels à la connaissance et à la culture historique ont trouvé un écho auprès d'une partie importante de la population. Un révolutionnaire doit connaître ses origines et comprendre les épreuves traversées par ses ancêtres. Un révolutionnaire qui ne s'intéresse ni à l'histoire ni à la culture générale ne peut pas véritablement comprendre les enjeux de son époque. L'histoire nous aide à comprendre notre passé et à mieux préparer notre avenir. Aujourd'hui, de plus en plus de personnes cherchent donc à comprendre d'où nous venons. C'est cette connaissance qui, selon moi, nous permettra d'avancer vers les objectifs que nous nous sommes fixés. En tant que guide, combien de visiteurs accueillez-vous en moyenne par jour ? Je ne suis pas en mesure de répondre de manière exhaustive à cette question, car les données officielles relèvent plutôt de l'administration du mémorial. Toutefois, je peux vous donner une estimation à partir de ce que nous observons sur le terrain. Certaines périodes sont particulièrement difficiles en matière de fréquentation. Pendant la rentrée scolaire, par exemple, nous constatons parfois une baisse du nombre de visiteurs. Cela peut notamment s'expliquer par les dépenses auxquelles les familles doivent faire face, même si cela reste une hypothèse. Durant ces périodes creuses, nous pouvons accueillir environ 100 à 200 visiteurs par jour. En revanche, pendant les périodes de congés et certains trimestres de l'année, la fréquentation peut atteindre 500 à 600 visiteurs par jour, voire davantage. Je rappelle qu'au cours d'une journée particulièrement fréquentée, un samedi du mois d'avril, nous avons enregistré plus de 7 200 visiteurs. Nous avons également connu des journées où la fréquentation a atteint environ 5 000 visiteurs, voire plus de 7 000. Ces chiffres illustrent l'importance de la fréquentation du site et l'intérêt que suscite l'héritage de Thomas Sankara auprès des populations du Burkina Faso, du continent africain et du reste du monde. À l'occasion du 15 octobre, date de commémoration de l'assassinat de Thomas Sankara et de ses douze compagnons, quel message adressez-vous aux Burkinabè et à toutes les personnes qui s'identifient à son héritage, notamment à celles qui hésitent encore à visiter le mémorial ? Mon message s'adresse à tous les Burkinabè, à l'ensemble du continent africain, notamment aux pays de l'Alliance des États du Sahel (AES), ainsi qu'au reste du monde. J'invite chacun à venir célébrer la mémoire de Thomas Sankara et de ses compagnons. Là où il se trouve, Sankara n'a plus besoin que nous pleurions sa disparition. Pleurer n'est pas une solution. Ce qu'il attend de nous, symboliquement, c'est que chacun s'approprie son histoire, son idéologie et son héritage. Nous devons célébrer Sankara, car la transmission de ses idéaux constitue une victoire sur l'oubli. Je le dis souvent, Thomas Sankara n'est jamais mort, il vit à travers ses idées et les personnes qui poursuivent son combat. J'invite donc toutes les personnes qui se trouvent à Ouagadougou, ainsi que celles qui viennent d'ailleurs, à visiter le mémorial. C'est un lieu où nous pouvons honorer nos héros et mieux comprendre les combats qu'ils ont menés. Sankara ne se battait pas uniquement pour lui-même ni pour sa famille. Il se battait pour un monde plus juste et plus équilibré, dans lequel personne ne serait humilié ou violenté en raison de sa condition ou de sa position sociale. Il se battait pour toute l'humanité, pour que les orphelins puissent se nourrir convenablement, en quantité et en qualité, et pour que chacun ait accès à l'eau potable. C'est dans cet esprit qu'il défendait l'idée qu'il fallait choisir entre le champagne pour quelques-uns et l'eau potable pour tous. Il accordait une importance particulière à l'accès à l'eau, comme en témoignent les initiatives en faveur des forages et des barrages, ainsi que le développement de la culture de contre-saison. J'invite donc tout le monde à sortir, à venir découvrir le mémorial et à prendre part à la célébration de nos héros. La mobilisation que nous observons chaque jour sur le site, même si les chiffres que j'ai évoqués ne sont pas exhaustifs, montre que Thomas Sankara continue de vivre dans la mémoire collective. Il y a une phrase que j'aime rappeler qui est que tous les morts ne sont pas au cimetière. Certains marchent, bien habillés, en costume et en cravate ; ils mangent et respirent, mais ils sont morts intérieurement. On les appelle des « cadavres ambulants ». Par cette image, je veux dire que la mort physique n'est pas la seule forme de disparition. On peut être vivant biologiquement, mais avoir perdu ses idéaux, ses convictions et son sens du combat. C'est pourquoi j'invite les Burkinabè, les Africains et toutes les personnes qui se reconnaissent dans les idéaux de Thomas Sankara à venir au mémorial, à s'instruire et à faire vivre son héritage. Thomas Sankara vit toujours à travers les idées qu'il nous a léguées et le combat pour un monde plus juste. Hanifa Koussoubé Anita Zongo Lefaso.net

items.title: You’re not Abraham Lincoln — Shettima berates Atiku for ‘disrespecting’ Tinubu
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Vice-President Kashim Shettima has criticised former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar over what he described as disrespectful comments about President Bola Tinubu, saying anyone seeking the presidency must show discipline and respect for public institutions. Shettima spoke on Wednesday at the inauguration of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council for the 2027 election. In his remarks, Shettima said Atiku’s repeated presidential bids and recent policy proposals did not, in his view, excuse language he considered disrespectful toward the sitting president. He also questioned how Atiku’s proposed production subsidies would be funded. “Those who want equity must come with clean hands. You can call him Bola. If you like, you can call him Adekunle. But the truth is that he is the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. “Your Excellencies, distinguished ladies and gentlemen, Atiku Abubakar. I will still respect him and call him his former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar. “I will not follow suit with the maverick Babachir Lawal and call him Kachalla, no. But believe me, Atiku Abubakar, who has contested for the presidency of this country for the eighth time, is no Abraham Lincoln. He is more of Oginga Odinga.” Shettima framed his criticism as an argument about the conduct expected of presidential contenders, saying the higher the office sought, the greater the responsibility candidates bear in their words and dealings with public institutions. “The presidency of the Federal Republic of Nigeria is not an ordinary political prize. It is the highest expression of constitutional authority in our country. And those who aspire to occupy it must demonstrate, even before they get there, the qualities they will expect of themselves, if entrusted with the responsibility of leading more than 200 million Nigerians. “Political ambition is not merely the desire to occupy public office. It is a test of character, cerebral strength, intellectual maturity, and responsibility. The higher the office a person seeks, the greater the discipline expected in his words, conduct, and relationship with public institutions,” he added. Turning to Atiku’s proposal on production subsidies, Shettima questioned the cost and the competing priorities that might be affected. “Distinguished ladies and gentlemen, this political season has become a masterclass in cinematic comedy. Vice President Atiku Abubakar’s proposal for production subsidies raises questions that some changes cannot answer. Who pays? Who benefits? And which competing priorities must surrender their funding? A change in ideological wardrobe cannot balance a national budget.” The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council inauguration, held at the Banquet Hall of the Presidential Villa in Abuja, formally brought the expanded campaign structure into focus as the ruling party prepared for the 2027 general election. The post You’re not Abraham Lincoln — Shettima berates Atiku for ‘disrespecting’ Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: The illusion of a good deal: Why some everyday money-saving habits may be costing you more
items.description: At a busy filling station somewhere in Accra, an attendant rests the pump nozzle inside a sedan’s fuel tank. Seconds after a sharp metallic click signals the tank is full, the attendant glances at the driver and asks a routine question: “Master, should I round it up?” With a nod from the driver, the attendant squeezes the lever again, forcing several more liters into the tank. Across Ghana’s consumer marketplace, from fuel stations and Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) refill depots to auto parts hubs like Abossey Okai, a collection of deeply ingrained urban myths dictates everyday commercial choices. Driven by a desire to maximize value or outsmart perceived commercial inefficiencies, consumers routinely embrace practices that promise more for less. Yet, an examination of these widespread consumer habits reveals a stark economic reality: the short-term illusion of getting extra value almost always ends in severe long-term financial loss, safety risks, and market inefficiency. The True Cost of ‘Topping Off’: LPG Cylinders and Fuel Tanks The practice of topping off isn’t confined to gasoline. At residential LPG stations, consumers frequently request that gas cylinders be filled to ‘full’—demanding that attendants bypass manufacturer safety thresholds to cram in maximum volume. The technical risks of overfilling liquefied gas and liquid fuel are well-documented. Examining the true cost of topping off highlights significant hidden long-term consequences associated with common consumer actions. For instance, forcing fuel past the first click floods the EVAP charcoal canister with liquid fuel, ultimately triggering expensive engine repairs. Similarly, overfilling domestic LPG cylinders beyond specification eliminates the twenty percent thermal expansion buffer, substantially increasing the risk of catastrophic valve failure. The ‘Tested’ Illusion: Second-Hand Parts vs. New Imports When it comes to cars and home appliances, many people truly believe that “home-used” or imported second-hand items are automatically better than brand-new ones. In places like Accra and Kumasi, mechanics almost always advise car owners to buy used original parts taken from old imported cars rather than new spare parts. Their reason? They say the used part is “tested and proven.” While original parts are usually better than cheap knockoffs, buying someone else’s discarded junk comes with serious hidden risks. First, hidden wear and tear presents a major issue: a used shock absorber or brake part might look fine on the outside, but it could easily have invisible cracks or worn-out internal rubber from old accidents, age, or weather exposure. Second, there is a distinct lack of guarantees or warranties, as second-hand items almost never come with a real warranty compared to brand-new parts. If a used alternator dies three weeks after installation, the consumer must pay for another part and pay the mechanic all over again. Finally, high power bills pose a major financial strain; sellers of used fridges and appliances often argue that older imported models are built stronger than new ones, yet these old motors consume far more electricity, rapidly eating up any upfront savings through sky-high monthly power bills. Transit Chaos: The Economics of the Pre-Stop The psychological compulsion to gain a brief advantage extends to public transportation. Drivers of trotros—the commercial minibuses that form the backbone of urban transport—frequently drop off or pick up passengers dozens of meters before designated bus stops. While drivers view early stops as a quick tactic to beat competing minibuses to the curb, the aggregate economic impact is negative. This premature stopping leads to micro-congestion, as trailing vehicles are forced to brake unexpectedly or maneuver around stationary buses, creating severe bottleneck gridlock along key corridors like the George Walker Bush Highway. Consequently, commuters suffer a substantial loss of productive hours, losing cumulative time weekly in artificially created traffic jams that diminish urban productivity across commercial centers. Furthermore, pedestrian risks escalate drastically when disembarking passengers outside designated zones are forced to navigate active traffic lanes. An Imperative for Behavioral Change Ghana’s consumer practices are rooted in an understandable attempt to manage costs within a demanding economic landscape. However, the reliance on informal heuristics over technical specifications creates systemic waste. Moving toward a more efficient market requires deliberate shifts in both policy and consumer behavior. To achieve this, consumers must respect manufacturer protocols by treating equipment limits—whether fuel nozzle clicks or LPG weight markers, as engineered safety limits rather than arbitrary guidelines. In addition, vehicle and appliance owners should prioritize total cost of ownership, evaluating purchases by their full lifecycle costs, including energy efficiency, durability, and warranty protections, rather than initial purchase price alone. Finally, municipal assemblies and driver unions must enforce transit discipline, prioritizing organized boarding at designated stops to protect city mobility and safety. True consumer value is not found in pushing equipment past its engineered limits or opting for worn-out hardware. Recognizing the hidden economic costs of these popular myths is the first step toward building a safer, more sustainable marketplace. About the author; William Wallace Tamakloe is an Associate PR Director at Touchpoint Magna Carta.
