items.title: AES-CEDEAO: les experts de la Task force préparent la participation de l’AES au prochain round des négociations
items.description: (Ouagadougou, le 14 octobre 2026) En prélude à la prochaine rencontre de négociations entre la Confédération des Etats du Sahel (AES) et la Commission économique des Etats de l’Afrique de l’Ouest (CEDEAO) qui se tiendra dans les jours à venir à Dakar au Sénégal, les hauts fonctionnaires réunis au sein de la Task force confédérale, se sont réunis ce 14 octobre dans la capitale burkinabè, pour préparer la participation des ministres des Affaires étrangères de l’espace confédéral à ce cadre de dialogue. Les membres de la Task force réunissant les experts du Mali, du Niger et du Burkina Faso vont, au cours de cette réunion, identifier les axes et questions prioritaires consacrant la position des pays membres de l’AES lors des négociations. Les conclusions de leur travaux seront examinées par les ministres en charge des Affaires étrangères de la Confédération AES, et serviront de boussole aux négociations avec la CEDEAO, selon le chef de la délégation malienne, l’Ambassadeur Amadou MAÏGA. « Les domaines tels que la libre circulation des personnes et des biens, le commerce, l'intégration des peuples et les questions diplomatiques et institutionnelles, sont entre autres points qui devront faire l’objet d’échanges à cette réunion préliminaire à la rencontre des Chefs de la diplomatie de l’AES », a-t-il indiqué. Félicitant l’AES et la CEDEAO, animées selon lui, d’un même esprit, celui de la préservation de l’intérêt des populations de l’Afrique de l’Ouest, le chef de la délégation du Niger l’Ambassadeur Ousmane ALHASSANE, a salué la mise en place effective de la Task force qui va œuvrer à l’harmonisation de la feuille de route des consultations et des négociations de Dakar. « Ce rendez-vous engage l'avenir des relations entre deux espaces que l'histoire, la géographie, les échanges et les peuples continuent de relier. Notre responsabilité est donc de préparer une position rigoureuse, cohérente et pleinement conforme aux orientations du Collège des Chefs d'État de notre Confédération », précise le chef de la délégation burkinabè, l’Ambassadeur Yirigouin Hermann TOE, par ailleurs Secrétaire général du ministère des Affaires étrangères. Pour lui, l’enjeu de ces échanges est de mutualiser les forces qui permettront à terme de construire une intégration adaptée aux aspirations des peuples des deux espaces sous régionales. Présidant la cérémonie d’ouverture, le chef de la délégation du Burkina Faso a appelé les experts à des échanges fructueux, favorisant une lecture et une compréhension mutuelles des enjeux et de tous les contours des dispositions qui seront soumises à la négociation. Avant l’étape de Dakar, les ministres des Affaires étrangères du Mali, du Niger et du Burkina Faso, vont se réunir à leur tour, ce vendredi 16 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, pour examiner les conclusions et les recommandations de cette réunion des experts de la Task force de négociations. DCRP/MAE L’article AES-CEDEAO: les experts de la Task force préparent la participation de l’AES au prochain round des négociations est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Family seeks autopsy, police investigation into death of student 12 days after Abomosu SHS enrolment
items.description: The family of a 14-year-old student who died 12 days after enrolling at Abomosu STEM Senior High School in the Eastern Region is demanding a thorough police investigation into the circumstances surrounding his death. Daniel Boateng Mintah died on September 30, 2026, less than two weeks after leaving home to begin senior high school. The family says conflicting accounts of the events leading to his death, questions about medication found among his belongings and concerns over the condition of his body at the mortuary have raised questions that require urgent investigation. According to the family, Daniel’s mother, Joyce Mintah, spoke to him earlier on the day he died before they received a call informing them that he was unwell and needed an injection for suspected malaria. The family says they were asked to send GH¢50 for the injection and provide his National Health Insurance Scheme details. However, subsequent attempts to obtain updates on his condition were unsuccessful for several hours, leaving them without clear information about his situation. At about 3:10 p.m., a caller who identified himself as the school’s headmaster asked Daniel’s parents to report to the school urgently. They immediately set off but were later redirected to Kwabeng Hospital, where they were informed that their son had been brought in dead. Daniel’s father, David Mintah, said a doctor informed the family that the boy had died before arriving at the hospital and recommended a post-mortem examination to establish the cause of death. The family’s concerns have since extended to the condition of Daniel’s body. Mr Mintah claims he found the body bleeding when he visited the Tafo mortuary on October 6. The body had been transferred from Kwabeng Hospital to the mortuary on October 1 at the family’s request. The family is also seeking clarification over reports that Daniel left the school’s orientation area to urinate but failed to return. They want investigators to establish the events between his last reported activities at school and the circumstances under which he was taken to the hospital. Daniel’s elder sister, Vivian Mintah, a nurse, has separately raised questions about psychiatric medication reportedly found among his belongings handed over by the school. She is seeking an explanation from the school regarding the medication, including how it came to be among his possessions and whether it had been prescribed to him. The family has appealed to the Inspector-General of Police, Christian Tetteh Yohuno, and the Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu, to intervene and ensure a comprehensive investigation into the matter. It is also calling for Daniel’s body to be transferred to the Police Hospital in Accra to facilitate further investigations and help establish the cause of death. The family says it wants answers to the questions surrounding the teenager’s death and clarity on the events leading to the loss of their son.

items.title: Sudan, Egypt to pursue joint border security, as public tensions flare after deadly mine bombing
items.description: In the aftermath of the bombing of a mine in the Halayeb Triangle that left scores of Sudanese miners dead, Egypt and Sudan are discussing a new security framework along the countries’ shared eastern border. That framework would provide for joint coordination to pursue what both sides regard as security risks arising from organized crime, Sudanese and Egyptian officials told Mada Masr. The push toward closer coordination comes amid public outcry in Sudan and diplomatic concern in international quarters over the killing of scores of artisanal miners in the disputed Halayeb Triangle on Saturday. That public outcry was accentuated on Monday when a gunman killed two Egyptians in a main market in southern Khartoum in what Sudanese security officials involved in the investigations told Mada Masr was a retaliatory attack. The shooting took place at around 2 pm near the Export Development Bank in the Local Market , a security source in Khartoum State police told Mada Masr. Three Egyptians were targeted in the market’s commercial area. Two died at the scene, while the third was taken to the Omdurman Medical Corps Hospital for treatment. Ali al-Laouta, a vegetable seller at the market, witnessed Monday’s shooting. He told Mada Masr that he noticed a man wearing a military uniform bearing the badge of the joint force of military-allied armed movements buying some items in the market. He then suddenly pointed his weapon at the three Egyptians shopping nearby, opened fire and fled the scene, Laouta adds. Police patrols and security units responded to the scene and tracked down the suspect, a source in the Khartoum police’s criminal investigations department told Mada Masr. The suspect initially resisted arrest, opening fire on security forces, but officers eventually subdued him, seized the weapon used in the attack and took him into custody, the source said. One member of the arrest unit was shot in the leg during the exchange of fire, a security officer involved in the operation said. The injured officer was hospitalized and is in stable condition, he added. The suspect is a member of the “support forces” — a wide range of armed formations that fight alongside the Sudanese military in the current war — a source informed of the preliminary investigation told Mada Masr. Sudan’s military-led government adopted a wartime policy that put the joint force, its main battlefield ally, in charge of protecting state institutions and supporting security operations in cities under military control. That has left the alliance with a heavy presence in urban areas. But a string of violent incidents involving joint force members in recent months has stoked public concerns and prompted authorities to review the policy and seek to curb the allied group’s urban presence. The source informed of the preliminary investigation told Mada Masr that the suspect was subjected to intensive questioning about his military affiliation and how he had obtained the weapon used in the attack. The interrogating officer told Mada Masr that, in his initial statement, the suspect said he had shot the Egyptian men in retaliation for his brother’s death in Saturday’s strikes. The shooting comes amid a wave of polarization in Sudanese public opinion following the deadly airstrike near the Sudanese-Egyptian border that killed scores of Sudanese people. The shooting adds more complexity to an already charged public sphere. Sudanese lawyer Oweis Salah Eddin al-Iraqi urged authorities to disclose the facts related to the miners’ deaths directly to the public, saying the case had become a matter of public concern and that any mishandling could provoke backlash. Many in the public and political arena are viewing the shooting in the context of wider accountability for the miners’ deaths. Viewing the market shooting in isolation from the attack on the miners would offer an incomplete assessment of the situation, said Adel Ibrahim Hamad, the head of Sudan’s Ashigga Party. The party was re-established by former members of the Democratic Unionist Party, drawing inspiration from an earlier party of the same name that called for union with Egypt. The revived party focuses on national issues, paying particular attention to Sudanese-Egyptian relations. Discussion of Monday’s shooting, Hamad argued, must begin with the original incident, saying Egypt’s response was disproportionate to the violation, “if any.” “Approaching the discussion from any other angle, such as platitudes about the strategic relationship [between the two countries] and the need to prevent an isolated incident from affecting it, would distract from a recurring Egyptian failing in handling Sudanese issues,” he said. For journalist Majed Mohamed Ali, Sudanese authorities have seriously underestimated the political and security consequences, at an especially complex and sensitive geopolitical moment, in their handling of the miners’ deaths. While he insisted that Monday’s shootings came down to the actions of an individual, Ali warned Khartoum and Cairo against allowing their opponents further opportunities to exploit the miners’ deaths. “The matter should be closed by clarifying the facts, identifying who is responsible and holding them accountable,” he said. “The Sudanese government must also take responsibility for securing the borders and regulating miners’ activity in accordance with the law.” Two days after the strike, the Transitional Sovereignty Council issued its first comment on the incident, announcing the formation of a fact-finding committee to investigate the deaths of the Sudanese miners. While the statement said Egyptian and Sudanese leaders had remained in contact since the attack to establish the facts, Egypt’s military announced later that evening that it had launched the third phase of its campaign against illegal gold mining in the Eastern Desert, citing the protection of national resources and the imposition of Egypt’s “full sovereignty” over its territories, without acknowledgement of the incident. According to a senior Sudanese diplomat, TSC Chair Abdel Fattah al-Burhan is paying close attention to the matter amid mounting public pressure to uncover the circumstances surrounding the attack and identify those responsible. That level of attention reflects heightened public concern in Sudan and the need to manage the strikes’ repercussions through state institutions and official channels, while safeguarding Sudanese citizens’ rights and ensuring the incident is treated seriously, the source said. The diplomatic steps are intended to convey Khartoum’s position to Cairo clearly and facilitate cooperation between the relevant authorities to complete the investigation and address questions raised by the incident, the diplomat added. Sudan has put forward a proposal for a joint security matrix to govern how incidents and activities in border areas are handled, define the responsibilities of relevant agencies and establish coordination mechanisms, according to the diplomat. The proposal also calls for the activation of surveillance and field monitoring procedures in areas prone to such incidents, he added. The matrix could include direct communication channels between relevant agencies in both countries, clear procedures for reporting and verifying incidents and mechanisms for sharing information on movements and activities requiring security intervention. It could also prompt a review of how authorities respond when incidents affect citizens or people working in border areas, the diplomat said. The proposal’s significance lies in the shift from responding to each incident separately toward an institutional mechanism for managing border risks and preventing the recurrence of similar incidents, the source added. Activating surveillance mechanisms would require practical coordination between the relevant Sudanese and Egyptian agencies, potentially through a new joint committee similar to the long established bodies overseeing other aspects of Sudanese-Egyptian affairs. This would necessitates clearly defined administrative and security responsibilities and a mechanism for exchanging information and verifying reports, the source said. All adopted measures would need to respect the sovereignty of both countries and the rules governing activities in border areas, the source added. An Egyptian official briefed on Egyptian-Sudanese relations confirmed that Cairo is considering establishing a joint security presence on the border alongside the Sudanese military to ensure border security. Egypt has pointed to the plan in discussions with African Union officials, during which Saturday’s strikes were criticized. items.title: Trade Minister urges employers to leverage industrial opportunities to create jobs
items.description: The Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, has urged employers to take advantage of the government’s industrial policies and investment opportunities to expand businesses, boost productivity and create jobs. She said economic stabilisation measures, alongside targeted industrial policies and investments in energy, digital trade systems and export development, were creating an enabling environment for businesses to grow and compete in domestic and international markets. Madam Ofosu-Adjare made the call when she addressed the 66th Annual General Meeting of the Ghana Employers’ Association (GEA) in Accra on Wednesday, October 14, 2026. She outlined the government’s strategies to move Ghana from economic stabilisation towards production-led growth, emphasising the role of the private sector in driving investment, industrial expansion and employment creation. The Minister congratulated the leadership and members of the Association on the milestone, describing the GEA as a critical partner in national development and an important voice in shaping policies that affect businesses and employment. “Through every political turn and every economic cycle, your association has remained a steady backbone, never ceasing to advocate for employers, the people who create the bulk of the jobs. We salute you for this,” she said. The meeting was held under the theme, “Macroeconomic Stability, Policy Predictability and Employment Creation in Ghana.” Meanwhile, the President-elect of the Association, Nana Dr Emmanuel Adu-Sarkodee, in a speech read on his behalf, commended stakeholders for renewing their mandate and pledged a stronger commitment to serving the employer community. He also proposed the institutionalisation of a Policy Predictability Compact (PPC) between the government and the private sector to promote a more predictable policy environment for businesses.

items.title: Burkina/Passeport biométrique: la fin des longues distances pour les citoyens des régions
items.description: Le Camarade ministre de la Sécurité, Mahamadou SANA, a procédé au lancement officiel de l'extension du service d'enrôlement des passeports à l'ensemble des régions du Burkina Faso, ce mardi 13 octobre 2026 à Ziniaré, dans la région d'Oubri. La cérémonie s'est déroulée en présence de la Gouverneure de la région d'Oubri, la Camarade Sy Assétou BARRY/TRAORÉ, ainsi que des corps constitués. Pour le ministre SANA, cette initiative traduit une exigence fondamentale de l'action publique : faire du service public un droit accessible à tous, et non une contrainte imposée par la distance. Il a, à cet effet, exhorté l'ensemble des acteurs concernés à faire de cette réforme une réussite, en garantissant un accueil de qualité et des procédures d'enrôlement et de délivrance des passeports plus accessibles, diligentes, transparentes et sécurisées. « Au-delà de l'enrôlement des passeports, cette initiative porte une ambition claire : rapprocher durablement l'administration des citoyens et rendre le service public plus accessible partout au Burkina Faso », a-t-il souligné, en insistant sur la nécessité d'assurer le bon fonctionnement du dispositif dans toutes les régions.» La Gouverneure de la région d'Oubri, la Camarade Sy Assétou BARRY/TRAORÉ, a salué le choix de sa région pour accueillir le lancement de cette réforme. Elle a, par ailleurs, invité l'ensemble des corps constitués à accompagner son déploiement afin d'en garantir le succès. Cette extension marque ainsi une étape importante dans le rapprochement de l’administration des populations et la facilitation des démarches liées à l’obtention du passeport biométrique sur l'ensemble du territoire national. DCRP/MSECU L’article Burkina/Passeport biométrique: la fin des longues distances pour les citoyens des régions est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Reps order halt to disputed land development in Imo
items.description: By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja The House of Representatives Committee on Public Petitions has ordered a halt to further development on a disputed parcel of land in Umundoche community, Ngor Okpala Local Government Area of Imo State, pending the resolution of a petition alleging illegal land acquisition and intimidation of residents. The committee also directed that armed men allegedly operating in the community be disarmed following claims that villagers had been threatened with firearms amid the dispute. The directives were issued on Wednesday during a hearing on Petition No. 901 of 2026, filed by J.U. Okoye Chambers against Prince Charles Amadi, also known as Chavon; Chikadibia Anyanwu; and Chidubem Nwosu. The petition alleges the illegal acquisition of more than 2,500 hectares of land, shooting and attempted murder of villagers, the invasion of the community by armed men, desecration of a corpse, abuse of police powers and breach of a memorandum of understanding. The petition also names HRH Eze Lambert Unuoha, traditional ruler of Nma 1 of Obioma Autonomous Community in Ngor Okpala, as a respondent. Addressing the parties, the committee chairman, who was represented by his deputy, Rep. Matthew Nwogu, directed that no further activity should take place on the disputed land until the matter was resolved through the committee or other appropriate means. “There are orders that no more actions on this land until this matter is resolved,” the chairman said. “Either through this place, or through which other means you want to resolve it. That’s the first order. No more putting up caterpillars or bulldozers in that land.” He said the committee had contacted the Department of State Services (DSS) and the police, which, according to him, denied supplying firearms to the men allegedly operating in the community. “All the boys that are armed in that village should be disarmed. Because we have made contact with the DSS. They said they didn’t give them the gun. The police said they didn’t,” he said. The chairman said the directives were intended to prevent further escalation while the committee examined the allegations. The hearing featured disagreements among lawyers representing the parties over the status of a pending court case and whether the committee should continue considering the petition. Counsel to Charles Farms Limited, identified during the proceedings as one of the parties involved in the dispute, told the committee that his clients had legally acquired the land and paid the relevant parties. He rejected the allegations in the petition and disclosed that his clients had instituted legal proceedings against the petitioners. According to him, he wrote to the committee on September 28, 2026, explaining his clients’ position and providing details of the court proceedings. He, however, acknowledged that he had not brought the supporting court documents to the hearing. The committee chairman said a letter and oral explanations were insufficient, demanding certified documentary evidence to establish the status of the case. The lawyer subsequently undertook to organise the documents he had received, certify the necessary papers and submit them to the committee. A committee member, intervening in the exchange, cautioned against allowing the existence of a court case to automatically terminate the legislative investigation. He said the committee had a constitutional responsibility to consider petitions submitted to it, adding that the scope of the court proceedings would have to be examined before determining whether they covered all the issues raised in the petition. “That a matter is in court does not immediately stop us from doing our duty. This is a constitutional committee. One of the very few committees written into the Nigerian constitution,” the lawmaker said. He urged the parties to respect the committee’s procedures and allow the petitioners an opportunity to present their grievances. “Tomorrow he might be the one petitioning this National Assembly over an issue. So let us respect processes, respect our constitution. And then respect the will of the people who have come here to seek justice,” he added. The lawmaker also urged the committee to give the respondents time to file formal responses, noting that the proceedings would benefit from documentary evidence from both sides. Petitioners allege intimidation of villagers Counsel to the petitioners, Dr Julius Onyemi, told the committee that efforts had been made to resolve the dispute before the matter was brought before the House. He said the first petition was submitted on July 17, 2026, followed by another on August 14 and a subsequent petition later that month. Onyemi alleged that he had made several attempts to contact the respondents to resolve the dispute with the community but was unsuccessful. He further alleged that the court action was initiated after the petitions had been submitted to the House and suggested that it was intended to frustrate the committee’s proceedings. The lawyer also accused the respondents of using security personnel and armed men to intimidate residents and prevent them from accessing their community. He urged the committee to ensure that the alleged intimidation stopped while the petition was being considered. Onyemi questioned the circumstances surrounding the land acquisition and called on the parties to demonstrate compliance with customary land acquisition procedures. He also raised concerns about the environmental implications of the proposed development, asking whether an environmental impact assessment had been conducted and made available to the community. The lawyer argued that residents had a right to be consulted over activities that could affect their land and environment. The respondents’ representatives disputed the allegations, maintaining that the land had been legally acquired. The claims remain subject to the committee’s investigation. Committee demands video evidence During the hearing, one of the respondents’ representatives challenged claims that armed men had visited the community and threatened residents. He said he had been in the area since Monday and disputed claims that he was present at the location where the alleged incident occurred. He offered to provide his flight itinerary and hotel booking details to support his account. The chairman subsequently asked the parties to provide any available video or photographic evidence to establish what happened. He said the committee was interested in examining the available evidence rather than relying solely on conflicting oral accounts. The chairman reiterated that further development on the disputed land must stop and that armed men allegedly involved in intimidating residents must be disarmed. The committee adjourned the matter until November 2026 to allow the respondents to study the petition, prepare their formal responses and submit the necessary documentary evidence. The hearing formed part of the committee’s consideration of the petition seeking intervention over the disputed land in Umundoche community, Imo State. The allegations have not been established as findings of fact. The respondents maintain that the land was legally acquired, while the committee is yet to conclude its investigation. The post Reps order halt to disputed land development in Imo appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kankan : le double message de Djénabou Touré aux autorités locales et aux citoyens
items.description: « Le président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, ne peut pas rester à Conakry et voir tout ce qui se passe en Guinée ou dans les villages. Tout ce qui se gâte, on dit son nom, pourtant nous sommes censés faire le travail. Nous avons notre responsabilité là-dedans » À Kankan, la ministre de l’Administration du Territoire et de la Décentralisation, Djénabou Touré, appelle à un respect mutuel entre les autorités et les citoyens. Lors d’une rencontre tenue ce mercredi 14 octobre 2026 à la Maison des jeunes de Kankan, elle a exhorté les populations à respecter les autorités établies, tout en rappelant aux responsables locaux leur obligation de répondre aux préoccupations des citoyens. Elle a également insisté sur le rôle des chefs de quartier dans la lutte contre le banditisme et l’amélioration des conditions de vie des habitants. Évoquant les critiques relatives au manque de respect envers les chefs traditionnels et les autorités en Haute-Guinée, la ministre a invité les citoyens à abandonner les comportements qu’elle juge contraires aux valeurs de respect de l’autorité. « On dit que quand on vient chez nous en Haute-Guinée, c’est ici qu’il y a le non-respect des chefs. Il faut qu’on abandonne cela, ce n’est pas bon. Respectons nos chefs… », a-t-elle déclaré, rappelant l’importance du respect des lois et des institutions pour le bon fonctionnement de l’administration. Pour Djénabou Touré, les sous-préfets, les préfets, les gouverneurs et les maires occupent des fonctions qui leur confèrent des responsabilités précises dans la gestion des affaires publiques. Le respect dû à ces autorités doit, selon elle, contribuer au fonctionnement harmonieux de l’État. Mais la ministre a également tenu à rappeler que l’autorité ne saurait se résumer à un statut ou à une fonction. Les responsables locaux doivent, en retour, faire preuve d’écoute et se préoccuper des difficultés quotidiennes des populations. L’accès à l’eau potable, aux soins de santé, à l’éducation, à la sécurité ainsi que la bonne gestion des espaces publics figurent parmi les préoccupations qu’elle a mises en avant. Elle a ainsi appelé chaque responsable à s’investir davantage dans la recherche de solutions concrètes aux problèmes des citoyens. Dans cette dynamique, Djénabou Touré a souligné que le développement du pays ne saurait reposer uniquement sur le président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya. Elle a invité les responsables à assumer pleinement leur part de responsabilité dans la gestion des affaires publiques. « Le président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, ne peut pas rester à Conakry et voir tout ce qui se passe en Guinée ou dans les villages. Tout ce qui se gâte, on dit son nom, pourtant nous sommes censés faire le travail. Nous avons notre responsabilité là-dedans », a-t-elle souligné. À travers cette déclaration, la ministre a appelé les responsables administratifs et locaux à prendre leurs responsabilités et à s’impliquer davantage dans la résolution des problèmes auxquels les populations sont confrontées. La lutte contre le banditisme a également occupé une place importante dans son intervention. Djénabou Touré a notamment exhorté les chefs de quartier à renforcer leur collaboration avec les services de sécurité afin de mieux prévenir les actes criminels. Elle leur a demandé de signaler aux autorités compétentes les zones sensibles de leurs quartiers et de contribuer activement à la sécurisation de leurs communautés. Cette démarche vise à renforcer le rôle des responsables de proximité dans la prévention de l’insécurité et la protection des citoyens. Au terme de cette rencontre, la ministre a mis en avant une double exigence : le respect des autorités légalement établies et le devoir de celles-ci de servir les populations avec responsabilité. Pour Djénabou Touré, l’amélioration des conditions de vie et le développement de la Guinée nécessitent l’engagement de tous les acteurs, des responsables administratifs aux citoyens. Chacun est ainsi appelé à jouer pleinement son rôle, dans le respect des lois et des responsabilités qui lui incombent.

items.title: 2027: Accreditation, collation won’t be fully automated – INEC
items.description: …Says Nigerians, not AI, will determine election outcomes By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has assured Nigerians that voter accreditation and result collation will not be fully automated in the 2027 general elections, insisting that citizens, not Artificial Intelligence AI, will determine the outcome. Chairman of the Commission, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN said on Wednesday that “Algorithms will not, and must never, decide the 2027 vote.” INEC in its Wednesday Bulletin said Amupitan spoke in Abuja while delivering the keynote address at the Artificial Intelligence and Democracy Forum 2026, held in collaboration with Yiaga Africa. Amupitan said, as a foundational policy, no critical electoral decision, result collation, voter accreditation or candidate qualification would ever be fully automated or delegated to an autonomous system. “Human accountability, statutory oversight and judicial review will remain paramount at every stage of the electoral chain,” he said. Responding to the forum’s opening question, “Will Algorithms Decide the 2027 Vote?”, he said the answer was an unequivocal no. According to him, the choice of who leads Nigeria belongs exclusively to the Nigerian people. The chairman said the forum was taking place 92 days before the general elections, in a digital landscape that had shifted significantly since 2023. He warned that the Commission was no longer dealing only with the “analogue” challenges of logistics but with a world in which AI can influence what a voter sees, how the voter thinks and how the voter trusts. “The greatest threat we face is not the hacking of a ballot box, but the hacking of the voter’s mind,” Amupitan stated. He said generative AI had reduced to near zero the cost of producing convincing deepfakes, including videos of candidates saying things they never said and of INEC officials giving false instructions. “If a voter cannot distinguish between truth and a synthetic lie, the foundation of informed consent crumbles,” he said. The INEC chairman warned that a well-timed deepfake video or cloned audio recording of a candidate, an election official or a security chief could announce a false candidate withdrawal, a postponement of the election or inflammatory ethnoreligious statements, and spread virally within minutes. He added that malicious actors could also impersonate the INEC Chairman, Resident Electoral Commissioners RECs and other officials to issue fake guidelines, declare unauthorised results or instruct voters to stay home. On the Commission’s response, Amupitan disclosed that INEC had created an AI Unit within its Information and Communication Technology ICT Directorate, equipped with real-time digital monitoring tools, deepfake detection software and data analytics expertise. He said any AI tool or automated system deployed by the Commission for logistics, database management or operational support must undergo rigorous audits to guarantee explainability, fairness and security before deployment. The Commission, he added, was working on a Digital Strategy to audit the information environment and partnering with technology platforms for the rapid debunking and labelling of AI-generated content touching on electoral processes. Amupitan called on technology companies, including Meta, X, Google, TikTok and Telegram, to rapidly restrict unlabelled synthetic media impersonating election officials, candidates or security personnel. He also asked them to enforce disclaimers on political advertisements and restrict micro-targeting based on ethnicity, religion or local origin. He urged political parties and candidates to sign an Ethical AI Code of Conduct, committing to refrain from deploying deepfakes, synthetic impersonation, dark ads or automated botnets. The INEC chairman stressed that the Commission does not view AI only through the prism of risk. He described it as a powerful force multiplier for administrative precision, predictive planning and institutional integrity. He said while human collation remained the statutory standard for declaring results, AI could run parallel statistical audits on polling unit result sheets uploaded through the eEC8A, flagging mathematical inconsistencies, atypical entry patterns and image quality defects for administrative review. On logistics, he said AI-driven geospatial analytics could help INEC deploy ad-hoc staff, vehicles, boats and sensitive materials to 176,846 polling units before 7:30 a.m. on election day. Amupitan said the 2027 General Election would be the largest democratic exercise on the African continent, involving over 103 million registered voters across 774 Local Government Areas LGAs. He said 10 of the 14 major operational milestones under the Electoral Act 2026 had been successfully executed. The two-day forum was attended by the Chairperson of the Economic Community of West African States Network of Electoral Commissions ECONEC and Chairman of the Senegal Electoral Commission, Mr Abdoulaye Sylla, along with National Commissioners, RECs, political party leaders, civil society organisations, security agencies, technology firms and the media. Amupitan said algorithms had no moral compass, no civic duty and no constitutional oath. “They do not have a conscience, they do not have a country, and they do not have a vote. INEC’s job is to ensure that the voice of the people is heard clearly, above the noise of the machines. “On election day in 2027, it will be the thumbprint of the Nigerian citizen, guided by their own will and their own hopes, that decides our future,” Amupitan said. The post 2027: Accreditation, collation won’t be fully automated – INEC appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Cancer : le gouvernement actualise son plan national avant le 31 décembre
items.description: Derrière chaque diagnostic de cancer, il y a une bataille qui ne se limite pas au traitement médical. Il faut pouvoir accéder à un spécialiste, réaliser les examens nécessaires, trouver les médicaments prescrits et financer un parcours de soins parfois long. Pour de nombreuses familles, ces contraintes peuvent s’ajouter à l’épreuve de la maladie. C’est dans ce contexte que le Premier ministre Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed LO a annoncé, lors du Conseil des ministres du 13 octobre, l’actualisation du Plan national de lutte contre le cancer 2025-2029, au plus tard le 31 décembre 2026. Le Gouvernement prévoit également de sécuriser la disponibilité des médicaments anticancéreux et de faciliter l’enrôlement des malades démunis dans les dispositifs de prise en charge de l’Agence de la Couverture sanitaire universelle. 14 358 cas en 2024 : l’ampleur du défi Les chiffres disponibles donnent la mesure du défi. Selon les estimations de GLOBOCAN 2024, publiées par le Centre international de recherche sur le cancer, une agence de l’Organisation mondiale de la santé, le Sénégal a enregistré environ 14 358 nouveaux cas de cancer et 9 659 décès cette année-là. Les femmes représentaient 8 670 des nouveaux cas estimés. Les cancers du col de l’utérus et du sein étaient les plus fréquents chez elles, avec respectivement 2 280 et 2 220 cas estimés. Ces données sont des estimations modélisées et non un décompte exhaustif de chaque diagnostic. Elles montrent néanmoins le poids de la maladie et l’importance d’une stratégie qui ne se limite pas aux soins hospitaliers. Pour les cancers du col de l’utérus et du sein, l’information, le dépistage et l’orientation rapide vers des services adaptés sont des maillons essentiels. Plus une maladie est repérée tôt, plus les équipes médicales disposent de possibilités pour organiser la prise en charge. L’actualisation du plan national doit donc permettre de préciser les priorités, les responsabilités et les moyens. Elle gagnerait à s’appuyer sur des objectifs mesurables : améliorer l’accès au dépistage, réduire les délais avant le diagnostic, renforcer la disponibilité des traitements et suivre les patients tout au long de leur parcours. La coordination entre les structures sanitaires, les professionnels, les associations et les collectivités est tout aussi importante pour atteindre les personnes qui consultent tardivement ou vivent loin des services spécialisés. Médicaments, couverture sanitaire : de l’annonce à l’accès La question des médicaments est tout aussi déterminante. Une prescription ne suffit pas si le produit n’est pas disponible ou reste financièrement inaccessible. Le communiqué ne précise ni la liste des médicaments concernés ni les moyens prévus pour en sécuriser l’approvisionnement. Ces éléments devront être clarifiés pour apprécier la portée concrète de la mesure annoncée. Le soutien aux patients les plus démunis constitue un autre enjeu. L’enrôlement dans les dispositifs de couverture sanitaire peut alléger une partie des dépenses, mais son efficacité dépendra des critères d’éligibilité, de la simplicité des démarches et de la couverture réelle des prestations. Il faudra notamment préciser les examens, les traitements et les frais pris en charge, ainsi que les modalités d’accès aux structures spécialisées. La date du 31 décembre 2026 fixe une échéance pour l’actualisation du plan. Le défi commencera ensuite : transformer les orientations en services accessibles, avec des ressources identifiées et un suivi public des résultats. Pour les malades, l’efficacité de la politique se mesurera moins au nombre de documents adoptés qu’à la possibilité d’être diagnostiqué à temps, de recevoir le traitement prescrit et de poursuivre les soins sans basculer dans la précarité. Cheikh Gora DIOP

items.title: ADC accuses APC of coercing opposition governors into campaign council
items.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of coercing opposition governors into its presidential campaign council, alleging that the ruling party is undermining Nigeria’s multiparty democracy ahead of the 2027 general election. The ADC Presidential Campaign Council’s Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, made the allegation in a statement reacting to the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja on Wednesday. Ologbondiyan accused the ruling party of using state power to pressure opposition governors into its fold or include them in its campaign structure despite their continued membership of other political parties. “What we are witnessing is not politics but political abduction. You cannot claim to be a democrat while using state power to force opposition governors into your party and then drafting them into your campaign council. This is political banditry,” he said. The ADC spokesman also alleged that the APC was pursuing a political agenda aimed at concentrating power in the hands of one individual, claiming that national institutions, security agencies and the judiciary were being deployed to weaken opposition forces. He urged Nigerians to resist what he described as an attempt to establish an immoral political order driven by the desire to retain power at the expense of citizens’ welfare. Ologbondiyan further accused the ruling party of neglecting the economic hardship, hunger and insecurity confronting Nigerians while focusing on its political interests. “These particular sets of leaders don’t care about the current conditions of the people but how best to remain in power at a time when average Nigerians find it difficult to eat and be secure,” he said. He also alleged that the country’s democratic space was shrinking, citing what he described as the suppression of dissenting voices, harassment of opposition figures and the weakening of democratic institutions for partisan purposes. “Never in our democratic journey have we witnessed this level of intolerance and desperation. The APC government has weaponised poverty, hunger and insecurity to subjugate Nigerians and cripple the opposition,” Ologbondiyan said. He added that the situation was inconsistent with the democratic ideals for which late politician Moshood Abiola and other pro-democracy figures fought. The ADC spokesman also promoted the party’s presidential ticket of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi, describing them as having the experience and democratic credentials to address the country’s challenges. “Atiku Abubakar is a democrat to the core. He has the national spread, the capacity and the will to reunite Nigeria and restore our battered democracy,” he said. The ADC Presidential Campaign Council called on Nigerians, media organisations, civil society groups and the international community to oppose what it described as the APC’s anti-democratic agenda and support efforts to protect multiparty democracy. items.title: Chambre des représentants : Majorité et Opposition se partagent le Bureau et les commissions
items.description: La recomposition des instances dirigeantes de la Chambre des représentants est désormais achevée. Au lendemain de l'élection d'Ahmed Touizi à la présidence de la première Chambre, la carte des responsabilités a été finalisée ce mercredi 14 octobre 2026, marquant la structuration complète du Bureau ainsi que la répartition de la présidence des neuf commissions parlementaires permanentes entre les différentes forces politiques de la Majorité et de l'Opposition pour la 12e législature. Cette étape consacre la mise en place de la nouvelle gouvernance de l'institution législative, au lendemain du vote ayant porté Ahmed Touizi à la tête de la première Chambre. Lors de son allocution investie d'enjeux institutionnels, le nouveau président avait fixé le cap de cette étape en appelant à une synergie accrue entre les composantes parlementaires et à un renforcement de la qualité législative et du contrôle de l'action gouvernementale. La composition du nouveau Bureau s'inscrit dans cette dynamique de représentativité, équilibrant la présence des partis de la majorité exécutive et des formations de l'opposition. Au sein du Bureau de la Chambre, le poste de premier vice-président revient à Mustapha Baitas (Rassemblement National des Indépendants), tandis que Khalid Chennak (Parti de l'Istiqlal) occupe la deuxième vice-présidence et Abdellah Bouanou (Parti de la Justice et du Développement) la troisième. Les autres postes de vice-présidents sont attribués à Mohamed Ouzzine (Mouvement Populaire) pour la quatrième vice-présidence, Mohamed Mellal (Union Socialiste des Forces Populaires) pour la cinquième, Mohamed Joudar pour la sixième, Meryem Ouhssan pour la septième et Adel El Bitar pour la huitième vice-présidence. La gestion administrative et financière du Bureau est confiée à Amina Maelainine (PJD) et Houda El Maghari (PAM) en qualité de questeures, alors que les fonctions de secrétaires sont assurées par Fatima Zohra El Basraoui (RNI), Mbarek Hamia (Istiqlal) et Aziza Beddad (PAM). Parallèlement, la présidence des neuf commissions permanentes, organes stratégiques d'examen des textes et de suivi des politiques publiques, a fait l'objet d'une répartition globale reflétant la diversité du paysage parlementaire : La Commission des Affaires étrangères, de la défense nationale et des Marocains résidant à l'étranger est présidée par Mohamed El Gharras (Groupe Constitutionnel Démocratique et Social). La Commission de l'Intérieur, des collectivités territoriales, de la ville et de la politique de la ville revient à Monsef El Tob (Groupe Istiqlalien de l'Unité et de l'Égalitarisme). La Commission de la Justice, de la législation et des droits de l'Homme est attribuée à Mohamed Ghiat (Rassemblement National des Indépendants), tandis que la Commission des Finances et du développement économique est confiée au député El Mhajri (Parti Authenticité et Modernité). Dans les secteurs sociaux et économiques, la présidence de la Commission des Secteurs sociaux est confiée à Mustapha El Ibrahimi (Parti de la Justice et du Développement), tandis que Mohamed Laaraj (Mouvement Populaire) prend la tête de la Commission des Secteurs productifs. La Commission des Infrastructures, de l'énergie, des mines et de l'environnement est dirigée par Abdelhak Amghar (Union Socialiste des Forces Populaires), et la Commission de l'Enseignement, de la culture et de la communication revient à Hassan Derhem (Parti du Progrès et du Socialisme). Enfin, la présidence de la Commission de Contrôle des finances publiques est attribuée à Hanane El Massi (Parti Authenticité et Modernité). The post Chambre des représentants : Majorité et Opposition se partagent le Bureau et les commissions appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Asantehene plants trees to commence Jimi Watercourse Rehabilitation destroyed by galamsey
items.description: The Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, has planted trees at the Jimi River near Obuasi to launch a major effort to reclaim lands and restore the river destroyed by illegal mining. He visited Lot 1 of the Jimi Land Reclamation and River Watercourse Rehabilitation Project, a 153-hectare pilot under the Green Ashanti Initiative, to inspect ongoing works and symbolically plant trees to mark the restoration. The site, which holds a major water source for the Adansi enclave, has been heavily degraded by galamsey, with vegetation stripped, soils contaminated and open pits left behind. The pollution threatens the Jimi River and the Jimi Dam downstream, which treats water for over 200,000 people in Obuasi and the Adansi area. At Tasliman, illegal miners have diverted the course of the river with heaps of sand, causing heavy siltation and rising turbidity. Aside from the rising turbidity levels, which has increased the cost of water treatment, the dam’s volume is decreasing, hence resulting in rationing of water to the communities. Director of Engineering at AngloGold Ashanti, Ing. Eric Broni, says the impact is already hitting water supply. “There is a possibility that this year, water abstraction will decrease. When the water level drops, abstraction decreases, but our cost increases. Last year we spent about $584,000 to treat water despite treating less. It is becoming a worry because we have to ration water to other communities,” he said. The Jimi project, led by the Ashanti Green Initiative under the leadership of Oheneba Nana Kwaku Duah, with Manhyia Palace providing vision and patronage, is piloting a six-step restoration model: backfilling pits, re-grading spoil heaps and terracing slopes, containing heavy metal contamination, installing drainage and erosion controls, restoring topsoil, and replanting with kenaf. Kenaf, a fast-growing fibre crop for sacks, ropes and eco-composites and other uses, has been chosen over food crops due to residual contamination risk and to provide alternative livelihoods for local farmers. The Jimi River and its buffer zones will also be cleaned and replanted under EPA guidance. The Asantehene was joined by partners, including AngloGold Ashanti, which is providing technical and operational support. The Managing Director, Samuel Boakye Pobee, said, “We are proud to be partners in the fight against land degradation and elated by the government’s support. The Jimi remains important to Obuasi. It provides water to many people outside the mine, more than those in the mine.” Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, disclosed that about 8,000 hectares of 188 forest reserves have been impacted by galamsey, with only 150 hectares reclaimed so far. “Government can only succeed with partnership. 80% of water comes from forest reserves, and this goes to the core of human survival. Government is committed to this partnership. The Asantehene’s commitment is a model for all chiefs,” he said. Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, described the project as a national crusade. “What you are doing is the launching of a national crusade for traditional leaders to partner with civil society, mining companies and government to lead the way to restore degraded lands,” he said. Organisers say the Green Ashanti tree planting at Jimi is more than symbolic. It marks the start of a replicable model to restore Ghana’s degraded lands, protect clean water, and restore livelihoods. The Asantehene was briefed at AngloGold Ashanti in Obuasi before moving to Lot 1 for the tree planting and inspection of the reclamation site and later, the Jimi Dam.

items.title: Justice pénale : le Parlement adopte une réforme clé du travail d’intérêt général
items.description: Réunis en séance plénière le mercredi 14 octobre 2026, sous la présidence du chef du Parlement, le camarade Dr Ousmane BOUGOUMA, les 71 députés votants ont adopté à l’unanimité le projet de loi révisé portant administration du travail d’intérêt général (TIG) au Burkina Faso. Bien qu’ayant enregistré des résultats encourageants, la loi n°035-2024/ALT du 8 novembre 2024 portant administration du travail d’intérêt général présentait plusieurs insuffisances qui ont rendu nécessaire sa révision. Le nouveau texte vise à renforcer la réinsertion sociale des personnes condamnées et à contribuer au désengorgement des établissements pénitentiaires. Parmi les principales innovations figurent le prononcé d’office du TIG pour certaines infractions mineures, l’élargissement des activités éligibles aux prestations intellectuelles et l’instauration d’un régime permanent de commutation des peines d’emprisonnement en travail d’intérêt général. À travers cette adoption, l’Assemblée législative du peuple (ALP) contribue à l’évolution du dispositif pénal en faveur d’une justice qui privilégie la responsabilisation des personnes condamnées, leur réinsertion sociale et l’utilité collective. items.title: 15 arrested, 6 trucks impounded over sandwinning activities on Kumasi-Accra Expressway
items.description: The National Security in the Ashanti region has arrested fifteen individuals for their alleged involvement in sandwinning activities on the Kumasi–Accra Expressway project. The suspects, all males, were apprehended in the Sewua–Donyina–Appiadu enclave during a swoop by some officers of the National Security on Wednesday, October 14. Six trucks, including a wheel loader, were also impounded during the raid in the enclave. An Assistant Liaison Officer, Ivan Bilson Yeboah, says the suspects have been transported to the national office in Accra for custody and further investigations. “They are on their way to Accra for our officers at the headquarters to carry out further investigations,” he said. A viral video indicated the individuals have been excavating and removing white sand from the Accra-Kumasi Expressway for commercial purposes. This raised concerns about the potential destruction of the right of way, which is crucial to the planned road infrastructure. Mr. Yeboah described the illegal activity as unacceptable, advising the public to desist from such practices, which impede national development. “We have seen a considerable damage being done to the road. It’s bad that resources of the state will be channeled to such a beautiful national activity, but people who want to loot and do whatever they did. This is unacceptable. Mr. Bilson Yeboah further noted that the regional security council is expected to meet to deliberate on means to heighten patrols along the portion of the expressway in the region. “REGSEC will be meeting on Thursday to look at how to sustain surveillance on the stretch to nip some of these activities in the bud,” he noted. However, some suspects remain at large as the security force intensifies the manhunt for their whereabouts. Bosomtwe District Chief Executive, Ing. Abdullah Hamidu, disclosed exclusively to JoyNews that preliminary investigations by the Assembly suggested the sand winners claimed to have obtained authorization from the Ejisu Municipality Assembly to undertake the excavation. They, however, failed to produce a copy of the said permit. “When they were directed to my office, they told me they had obtained a permit from Ejisu, but they could not provide a copy. I ordered them to stop the operation and referred the matter to the police for further investigations,” he said.

items.title: Senate urges FERMA to repair failed Anambra-Rivers highway
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The Senate has urged the Federal Road Maintenance Agency (FERMA) to undertake emergency repairs on failed sections of the Onitsha–Ogbaru–Ndoni–Rivers Federal Highway pending its comprehensive rehabilitation and reconstruction. The Senate said the immediate intervention would reduce the hardship faced by motorists and communities along the route. Following a motion sponsored by Senator Tony Nwoye, representing Anambra North, the Senate also proposed that the Federal Government mandate the South East Development Commission (SEDC) or the Federal Ministry of Works to carry out the remedial work. The Senate recommended that the comprehensive rehabilitation and reconstruction be executed through a special intervention programme or another appropriate funding arrangement, given the road’s strategic importance as a major link between the South-East and South-South geopolitical zones. It mandated the Senate Committee on Works to conduct an on-the-spot assessment of the highway, engage relevant stakeholders and report back within four weeks with appropriate recommendations. It also urged the Senate committees on Works and Appropriations to ensure adequate budgetary provision for the road’s comprehensive rehabilitation and reconstruction. The Senate noted that the highway was partially constructed in the late 1980s but had suffered decades of neglect without any major rehabilitation. It said the prolonged abandonment, ageing infrastructure, increasing traffic volume and lack of routine maintenance had left the road in a deplorable condition, characterised by extensive pavement failures, deep potholes and severe erosion. According to the Senate, the condition of the highway posed a serious threat to the lives and property of commuters and other road users. It further observed that the deterioration had significantly increased travel time, with a journey of approximately 70 kilometres from Onitsha through Ogbaru to Ndoni, which would ordinarily take about one hour, now taking nearly two hours. The Senate said the situation had resulted in higher transportation costs, loss of productive man-hours and disruption of commercial activities. It added that the failed sections frequently caused vehicles to break down and remain stranded for extended periods, exposing commuters to road accidents and heightened security risks. The Senate also noted that the highway served as a vital economic corridor, supporting significant oil and gas exploration and production activities in the Ogbaru oil belt and contributing to Nigeria’s economy. It expressed concern that continued neglect of the federal highway had affected interstate commerce, agricultural value chains, regional integration and investment, undermining efforts to promote economic development, national connectivity and safe transportation. The Senate warned that without urgent intervention, further deterioration would endanger lives and property, impede economic activities, increase transportation costs and affect oil exploration and production along the Ogbaru corridor. It added that the situation would worsen the hardship faced by residents of Anambra and Rivers states and negatively affect businesses that depend on the transport corridor. items.title: La réouverture de la route 463 aux colons menace d’isoler Ramallah
items.description: L'armee israelienne s'apprete a rouvrir aux colons la route 463, un axe de dix kilometres traversant le nord de Ramallah et d'el-Bireh. Cette mesure, selon plusieurs sources, menacerait d'isoler huit villages palestiniens et deux grands quartiers residentiels, tout en separant le nord et le sud du gouvernorat. Une route au cœur de la fragmentation Construite au milieu des annees 1990 pour relier les colonies de Beit El et de Dolev, la route 463 avait ete fermee apres le declenchement de la seconde Intifada. Sa reouverture s'inscrit dans un budget d'infrastructures de 1,075 milliard de shekels (environ 355 millions de dollars) destine aux colonies, illegales au regard du droit international. Le gouvernement israelien souhaite accelerer le processus avant les elections du 27 octobre . La Commission de resistance a la colonisation et au mur, affiliee a l'OLP, denonce une « politique systematique visant a demanteler la contiguïte geographique et demographique palestinienne ». Des dizaines de milliers d'habitants seraient contraints d'emprunter une route alternative deja saturee pres du camp de Jalazone. Les villages de Surda, at-Tira, Ein Qiniya, Ras Karkar, Deir Ibzi ou Ein Arik seraient particulierement touches. Jamal Juma, coordinateur de la Campagne populaire de resistance au mur et aux colonies, estime que la reouverture « encerclerait completement la partie ouest de Ramallah ». Sur X, l'Association France Palestine Solidarite avait deja alerte le 1er octobre en soulignant que « l'armee et les colons israeliens collaborent pour rouvrir la route 463 reservee aux colons et rompre la continuite territoriale ». L'armée et les colons israéliens collaborent pour rouvrir la route 463 réservée aux colons et rompre la continuité territoriale. Selon Jamal Jumaa de @stopthewall, elle divisera Ramallah en coupant les universités dont Birzeit du reste de la ville. https://t.co/Icp4rZ426c — Association France Palestine Solidarité (@AFPSOfficiel) October 1, 2026 Munif Treish, maire d'El-Bireh, rappelle que 95 % du trace se situe en zone B, placee sous administration civile palestinienne selon les accords d'Oslo II. Il y voit une « violation flagrante » des engagements pris avec l'OLP et une « menace existentielle » pour 250 000 Palestiniens. La municipalite promet de mobiliser tous les moyens legaux pour s'y opposer tandis que la mobilisation internationale, notamment au sein de l'UE, ne semble pour l'heure pas produire d'effets .
