items.title: MTN Ghana to spend $1.1bn in 3 years, build 500 new sites as MoMo hits 44% Growth
items.description: Telecom giant MTN Ghana is investing US$1.1 billion over the next three years to expand its network, including the deployment of 500 new cell sites this year, as it marks 30 years in Ghana. At a stakeholder forum in Wa, the company’s Chief Risk and Compliance Officer, Joseph Dogbe, announced the investment. Speaking before media partners, stakeholders and MTN staff, Mr Dogbe traced the company’s journey from luxury to lifeline — from connecting people to creating opportunities, and from building cell sites to building trust. He then outlined the figures behind the investment. Mr Dogbe said MTN Ghana connects more than 32 million subscribers. To keep that connection alive, the company is investing US$1.1 billion over the next three years, including approximately US$380 million in 2026, to enhance network capacity and resilience. As part of the investment, the telecommunications company is deploying 500 new cell sites nationwide this year. The MTN Chief Risk and Compliance Officer said the company’s 30-year journey had not always been smooth, adding that gratitude that remembers only the easy years is not complete gratitude. Mr Dogbe, however, stressed that connectivity alone was not enough. “One of the most powerful examples of shared value is Mobile Money. In the first half of this year, MoMo transaction value grew by 44.4% year-on-year, with active MoMo users up 3.1% and transaction volumes up 23.3%,” he said. “For many, MoMo has become more than a payment platform. It is a gateway to economic participation,” he added. He said MTN’s extensive reach came with responsibility, emphasising that cybersecurity and data privacy were fundamental to building trust. On financial performance, MTN Ghana recorded strong growth in the first half of 2026, with service revenue increasing by 32.3% to GH¢15.0 billion, earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) rising by 47.1% to GH¢9.3 billion, and profit after tax growing by 46.8% to GH¢5.1 billion. “We share these numbers not to boast, but because they matter to you directly: a financially strong MTN Ghana is a Ghana that can keep investing,” Mr Dogbe stated. On its contribution to national revenue, MTN paid GH¢5.6 billion in direct and indirect taxes, as well as GH¢384.7 million in fees and levies, in just six months. Beyond its core business, Mr Dogbe highlighted interventions by the MTN Ghana Foundation, including the MTN Skills Academy, which targets 100,000 young people with digital skills, and the Bright Scholarship Scheme, which has supported more than 1,200 students with fees, hostel accommodation, stipends and laptops. The company has also revamped its Heroes of Change initiative, increasing the overall winner’s prize from GH¢100,000 to GH¢400,000. Category winners will receive GH¢200,000 each, while every finalist will receive GH¢100,000. New award categories for sustainability and digital innovation have also been introduced. In the Upper West Region, Wa Catholic Primary School benefited from the company’s water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) programme during MTN’s 21 Days of Y’ello Care initiative. Mr Dogbe also highlighted DigiFest 2026, an artificial intelligence capacity-building programme for media practitioners and civil society organisations (CSOs), as well as digital skills programmes for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and partnerships with festivals such as Dumba and Kobine. As part of its 30th anniversary celebrations, MTN has extended Customer Service Week into a month-long engagement dubbed Customer Service Month. On sustainability, he said MTN’s environmental, social and governance (ESG) pillars — Doing for People, Doing It Right, Doing for Growth and Doing for Planet — were not activities undertaken alongside its business but were central to how the company operates. The stakeholder engagement also featured a four-member panel discussion involving senior MTN officials: Simon Amoh, Augustine Kontoma, David Nana Addai and Aseye Kwame Akude, who represented the company’s management, network engineering, Mobile Money and retail enterprise functions, respectively.

items.title: I have no regrets joining Assemblies of God – Mahama
items.description: The Executive Committee of the World Assemblies of God Fellowship has paid a courtesy call on President John Dramani Mahama ahead of the church’s World Congress, which opens in Accra today, Tuesday, October 13. The delegation was led by the Global Chairman, Reverend Dominic Yeo, and the host, General Superintendent Reverend Stephen Wengam. Reverend Wengam said all was set for the World Congress, which is taking place on African soil for the first time in the 115-year history of the Assemblies of God worldwide. He commended President Mahama and the government for supporting the organisation of the event. Reverend Wengam explained that the change of venue for the morning conference, from Independence Square to the Grand Arena of the Accra International Conference Centre, was due to technical hitches, adding that the new venue is more conducive. The Global Chairman of the Assemblies of God Fellowship, Reverend Yeo, congratulated Ghana on being the first country in Africa to host the World Congress, just as it was the first in sub-Saharan Africa to gain political independence. He expressed the gratitude of the Executive Committee to President Mahama and the Government of Ghana for their diverse assistance to ensure the success of the World Congress. The Global Chairman commended the President for his visionary and transformational leadership, which he said is reflected in economic stability and massive road development. He urged the President to continue to represent Christ well in politics and to remain steadfast in his faith. President Mahama welcomed the delegation to Ghana and assured them of the government’s continued support to ensure that the event is peaceful, successful and impactful. He recounted how he joined the Assemblies of God, saying, “I have no regrets.” He commended the current leadership of the church for its visible growth and transformation. Reverend Yeo presented Congress souvenirs to President Mahama and led the delegation to pray for him and for the prosperity of the nation.

items.title: Racheté par l’égyptien Beltone, le groupe panafricain Baobab ouvre un nouveau chapitre et veut accélérer au Mali
items.description: © Baobab Mali Depuis janvier 2026, le groupe de microfinance Baobab est détenu à 100 % par le groupe égyptien Beltone. Au Mali, où il est implanté depuis 2013, Baobab compte près de 100 000 clients, 352 salariés et un encours de crédit de près de 42 milliards de FCFA. Son directeur général, Mor Talla Diop Tine, explique ce que ce nouvel actionnariat change concrètement pour les commerçants, producteurs et entrepreneurs maliens, et détaille ses priorités pour les prochaines années. Le groupe Baobab a été racheté par le groupe égyptien Beltone en Janvier 2026. En quoi cette opération doit permettre d’accélérer ? Baobab est aujourd’hui un groupe panafricain, détenu à 100 % par un actionnaire égyptien, Beltone. Nous sommes présents dans sept pays : Mali, Burkina Faso, Sénégal, Côte d’Ivoire, Nigeria, République démocratique du Congo et Madagascar. Ce rapprochement représente une étape importante pour le développement de Baobab. Beltone est l’un des grands groupes de services financiers en Égypte, avec une expertise très diversifiée dans le financement des entreprises et des particuliers, la microfinance, la gestion d’actifs et les nouvelles technologies financières. Ce qui est particulièrement intéressant pour nous, c’est que Beltone possède également une solide expérience dans des métiers très proches des nôtres. À travers sa filiale Cash for Microfinance, le groupe est notamment très présent en Haute-Égypte, une région largement rurale, où il accompagne de nombreux petits entrepreneurs, commerçants et artisans, ainsi que des activités liées à l’agriculture. Il existe de vraies similitudes entre les besoins de financement de ces populations et ceux de nos clients au Mali. Les contextes économiques ne sont évidemment pas identiques, mais les défis sont souvent les mêmes : faciliter l’accès au crédit, accompagner les petites activités économiques et permettre aux entrepreneurs de développer leurs affaires. Nous avons donc beaucoup à apprendre de l’expérience acquise par Beltone en Égypte, notamment dans le développement de produits adaptés à ces clientèles, l’utilisation des nouvelles technologies et l’amélioration de nos processus de crédit. J’ai d’ailleurs eu l’occasion de me rendre au Caire avec les directeurs de nos autres filiales pour rencontrer les équipes de Beltone. Nous avons été particulièrement impressionnés par l’étendue de leurs activités, leur expertise et leur capacité d’innovation. Pour Baobab Mali, c’est une formidable opportunité d’accélérer notre développement en nous appuyant sur les moyens financiers, les compétences et l’expérience de notre nouvel actionnaire egyptien. Et cette complémentarité fonctionne dans les deux sens. Baobab apporte sa connaissance approfondie des marchés africains et des réalités locales. Nos équipes maliennes restent au cœur de notre activité et des décisions de crédit, car ce sont elles qui connaissent le mieux nos clients. Notre ambition est de réunir le meilleur des deux groupes : l’expertise et la capacité d’innovation de Beltone, associées à la proximité et à la connaissance du terrain qui font la force de Baobab. Treize ans après votre arrivée à Bamako, que pèse Baobab dans l’économie malienne ? Lorsque nous avons ouvert notre première agence à Bamako, en septembre 2013, nous avons fait le pari du marché malien et de ses entrepreneurs. Le dynamisme des entrepreneurs maliens et leur capacité à toujours s’adapter aux défis économiques ont renforcé notre confiance dans ce marché et notre volonté d’y investir durablement. Aujourd’hui, nous comptons 18 agences, dont neuf en dehors de Bamako, et nous servons près de 100 000 clients, parmi lesquels environ 36 000 emprunteurs. Notre portefeuille de crédits atteint près de 42 milliards de FCFA. Ces financements permettent à des commerçants, des entrepreneurs et des producteurs de renouveler leurs stocks, d’acquérir du matériel ou de développer leur activité. En se développant, notre activité a également généré des recettes pour le pays. Par exemple, sur l’année 2025, la contribution de Baobab Mali aux recettes de l’État s’est élevée à 3,5 milliards de FCFA. Ces résultats reposent sur une confiance réciproque : nous avons cru au potentiel de l’économie malienne, et les clients nous ont accordé leur confiance. C’est cette relation construite dans la durée qui nous permet de continuer à nous développer au Mali. Votre développement s’est-il aussi traduit par plus d’emplois et de responsabilités pour les cadres maliens ? Tout à fait, nous comptons aujourd’hui 352 collaborateurs. Nos équipes sont jeunes, avec une moyenne d’âge de 30 ans, et beaucoup nous ont rejoints directement à la sortie de l’université pour leur première expérience professionnelle. Nous formons nos jeunes collaborateurs en interne et les accompagnons dans l’apprentissage du métier. Une gestionnaire de portefeuille, par exemple, suit les clients et leurs crédits. Elle apprend à comprendre une activité, à examiner un besoin de financement et à suivre les remboursements. Cette expérience du terrain peut ensuite lui permettre d’accéder à des responsabilités d’encadrement. De nombreux chefs d’agence ont suivi ce parcours. Notre directeur administratif et financier actuel et notre responsable marketing actuels sont tous les deux entrés comme stagiaires en 2017. La promotion interne est centrale pour nous. Elle permet aux jeunes de construire une carrière et à l’institution de s’appuyer sur des responsables qui connaissent les clients et les réalités du pays. Pour les petites activités, obtenir un crédit reste une préoccupation. Comment répondez-vous à leurs besoins ? Nous partons du fonctionnement de l’activité. Un commerçant a besoin de financer ses achats et de faire tourner son stock. Un producteur agricole doit composer avec un calendrier de production et des revenus qui arrivent à certaines périodes. Le montant du crédit et ses échéances doivent tenir compte de ces différences. Nous avons aussi développé des offres spécifiques. Le Crédit Muso, destiné aux femmes, propose des financements de 100 000 à 1 million de FCFA sur dix mois, sans frais d’ouverture ni frais de demande, afin de réduire les coûts d’accès au crédit et de tenir compte des obstacles particuliers qu’elles rencontrent pour financer leur activité. Cette proximité avec nos clients nous aide à adapter nos offres. Elle compte également lorsqu’ils rencontrent des difficultés : il faut qu’ils puissent parler à leur gestionnaire, expliquer leur situation et être accompagnés dans la recherche de solutions. Quelles sont maintenant vos priorités pour le marché malien ? Nous allons investir fortement dans la digitalisation au cours des deux prochaines années. L’application My Baobab permet déjà de consulter son compte et d’effectuer des transferts. Grâce au dispositif d’interopérabilité de la BCEAO, nos clients peuvent également transférer de l'argent instantanément, gratuitement et de manière 100 % sécurisée entre n'importe quel compte bancaire ou compte de monnaie électronique (Mobile Money) au sein de la zone UEMOA. Pour un commerçant qui doit régler un fournisseur, cela simplifie les opérations. Pour un client éloigné d’une agence, cela réduit les déplacements. Nous voulons développer ces usages tout en conservant l’accompagnement de nos équipes. Nous poursuivrons également nos financements en faveur des femmes entrepreneures et de l’agriculture. Nous étudions enfin les besoins des petites entreprises et des populations dans les zones minières. Notre ambition est de toucher davantage d’activités et de permettre aux entrepreneurs maliens de financer leurs prochaines étapes de développement.

items.title: Starlink restrictions in Ukraine war linked to political situation, Zelensky aide says
items.description: New restrictions on the speed at which some of Ukraine’s weapons can travel and stay connected to the Starlink internet network have disrupted Ukraine’s battlefield “missions”, President Volodymyr Zelensky’s adviser has warned. Serhiy Beskrestnov said Ukraine had not been told about speed limits set overnight at 100mph (160km/h) by Elon Musk’s SpaceX company. Starlink is a vital tool allowing Kyiv to effectively guide drones to Russian targets and also protect Ukrainian skies. Beskrestnov said SpaceX’s move “cannot be a coincidence and is related to the current political situation”. The firm has not commented. In Wednesday’s post on Telegram, Beskrestnov said that SpaceX had “implemented overnight a speed limit on Starlink terminals” and this had already resulted in “the disruption of a number of missions”. In a follow-up post, the adviser stressed that Starlink was the most effective tool for enabling interceptors to shoot down Russia’s newly developed jet-propelled drones. It comes as at least 600,000 people across Ukraine were left without electricity after deadly overnight Russian missile and drone strikes, Zelensky said. Pictures from Kyiv showed residents, some dressed in their pajamas, with bloodied faces. He added that “critical” energy infrastructure had been hit in Kyiv and the capital region, and in the north-eastern city of Kharkiv – despite US President Donald Trump’s claim on Sunday that an “energy ceasefire” was in place between Russia and Ukraine. Three people were killed in Kyiv, local officials reported. Russia said its “massive” strikes had hit communications and energy facilities used by Ukraine’s military. Later on Wednesday, at least six people were killed in a Russian drone strike on a warehouse in the north-western city of Lutsk, local officials said. Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and Moscow currently controls about 20% of Ukrainian territory. A source in the Ukrainian defence ministry later told the BBC: “Last night, we detected restrictions affecting Starlink connectivity at speeds above 160 km/h.” The source added that the “root cause” of the issue was being investigated. Defence ministry sources later explained that “once a vehicle or asset exceeds this [160km/h] threshold speed, the terminal loses its connection”. They told the BBC that this made it more difficult to carry out drone operations, “specifically interceptors and middle-strike drones”, and also degraded “capabilities for front line logistics, reconnaissance, and signal relaying”. In February, Musk’s decision to deny Russian forces access to Starlink blunted Moscow’s advance in Ukraine and caused confusion among Russian commanders. Musk’s SpaceX has not commented on the reported speed restrictions. Zelensky has said that the US threatened to restrict intelligence sharing if he did not sign up to Trump’s energy ceasefire. On Tuesday, Trump denied that Washington was withholding intelligence. Ukraine relies on US satellite systems to track Russian missiles in order to issue alerts and to try to shoot them down. But over the past two nights, missiles have struck targets in the Ukrainian capital without any warning, before air raid sirens could be sounded. According to Ukraine’s air force, Russia launched 39 ballistic and cruise missiles and 128 drones overnight. Four of those missiles and 115 drones were shot down, it said. It was the second night in a row that Kyiv was hit by Russian missiles, and came as Zelensky prepared to meet UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham at Downing Street on Wednesday to discuss accelerating air defence supplies to Kyiv. Meanwhile, the Russian defence ministry said 902 Ukrainian drones had been shot down overnight over a number of Russian regions, including the capital Moscow and Crimea – Ukraine’s southern peninsula annexed by Russia in 2014. On Sunday, Trump wrote on Truth Social: “Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!” Zelensky has since repeatedly said that Ukraine is ready to halt its strikes on Russian oil refineries and other energy facilities if Moscow does the same. But Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov has said Ukraine does not deserve the “respite” a ceasefire would bring. Under any truce, he added, Europe would be able to “pump [Ukraine] with new weapons”, enabling it to continue the war. For residents of Kyiv, the past two nights have been frightening. Tetiana Storozhyk, 54, said a late night blast on Tuesday at her apartment block blew her from the kitchen into the hallway. The sirens sounded just as the missile hit the building, giving her no time to evacuate. “It all happened in a fraction of a second. In that moment I lost everything” she said. Storozhyk told the BBC that Ukraine needs weapons to protect its people, “but from the other side we need peace”. Without peace Ukraine is reliant on its air defences, but this wrecked neighbourhood is evidence of how ineffective they are without the right data.

items.title: Furniture boost for Techiman North schools as MP donates to 20 institutions
items.description: In a significant boost to education in the Techiman North District, the Member of Parliament (MP) and Minister for Trade, Agribusiness, and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, has donated a large consignment of furniture to twenty schools across the constituency. The donation, which spans from Kindergarten (KG) to Senior High School (SHS) levels, aims to create a more conducive environment for teaching and learning. The items presented included: 50 KG sets, 300 mono desks, 150 dual desks, 50 dining tables and chairs, and 50 teachers’ tables and chairs. The beneficiary list includes a mix of basic and second-cycle institutions, such as Bridigeso KG, Kondiase D/A Primary, Offuman Ramzier JHS, Guakro Effah SHS, Akumfi Ameyaw SHS, St. Francis Seminary SHS, and Tuobodom Senior High Technical School, among others. The distribution was strategically tailored to the needs of each school level. KG schools received between 10 and 12 sets each, while primary schools received the bulk of the dual desks, with some receiving up to 90. Junior High and Senior High Schools received mono desks ranging from 30 to 100, with Senior High Schools also receiving dining hall furniture. Speaking at a brief presentation ceremony in Tuobodom, Madam Ofosu-Adjare explained that the gesture was prompted by the urgent needs observed during her visits to schools in the constituency. “I realized that during my visits, the major concern raised by teachers and pupils was the lack of furniture,” she said. “This gesture is aimed at creating an enabling environment for children to learn in dignity and comfort.” The MP assured constituents that this is the beginning of a sustained effort. She pledged to return next month with another batch of furniture, stating she will continue until the furniture needs of all schools in the district are fully addressed. District Director of Education, Ahmed Nasir Ibrahim, received the items and commended the government and the MP for their continuous support of education in the area. He noted that furniture shortage has been a persistent challenge, particularly affecting the youngest learners. “In some cases, KG pupils have to sit on the floor to learn,” Mr. Ibrahim said, adding that the donation would significantly alleviate these challenges. A teacher at Mesidan D/A KG, Joseph Mahama, who spoke on behalf of the headteachers of the beneficiary schools, described the support as “timely.” He said that the lack of furniture had forced many pupils to endure uncomfortable learning conditions. “With this donation, some schools will for the first time have proper furniture, which will enhance teaching and learning,” he stated. The donation is expected to ease congestion in classrooms and improve the overall quality of education delivery in the Techiman North District.

items.title: Assemblies of God to loan 10,000-seater dome for Ghana@70 celebrations
items.description: The Assemblies of God, Ghana, will loan its newly arrived 10,000-seater dome to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for activities marking Ghana’s 70th anniversary celebrations. The church’s General Superintendent, Rev. Dr Stephen Yenusom Wengnam, disclosed this at the opening of the 10th World Assemblies of God Congress on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Accra International Conference Centre Dome. He explained that technical difficulties delayed the arrival of the structure from Dubai, preventing the church from using it for the congress as originally planned. According to him, although the dome has arrived at the port, it requires about 10 days to assemble, making it unsuitable for the ongoing event. “Originally, we were to meet at the Independence Square. We had ordered a 10,000-seater dome from Dubai, but technical challenges made it impossible for it to arrive on time. Even though, as I speak, it has arrived at the port, we need 10 days to fix it,” he said. Rev. Dr Wengnam said the church had decided to put the structure to another use by moving it to the Assemblies of God Centenary City land before making it available to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for the national celebrations. “Nevertheless, it will serve another purpose. We are moving it to the Assemblies of God Centenary City land, and then we’ll loan it to Foreign Affairs for the Ghana at 70 events,” he added. Meanwhile, the 10th World Assemblies of God Congress will continue with evening revival rallies at the Accra Sports Stadium from 5 p.m. daily, from Wednesday, October 14, to Friday, October 16, 2026.

items.title: Government to audit 2,016 community network sites – Communications Minister
items.description: The government will conduct an audit of 2,016 community network sites inherited under an existing contract to determine their completion status and establish how many are currently operational. Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovation, Samuel Nartey George, announced the planned exercise during a visit to the Sekyere Afram Plains District in the Ashanti Region, where he commissioned four community network sites. He said the audit would provide a clear picture of the work completed by the contractor, identify outstanding tasks and help the government determine the condition of the facilities. Mr George explained that it would be impractical for him to visit all 2,016 sites personally, making an independent assessment necessary. “Next week, we are going to have a meeting with the contractor to evaluate the work that is done. We inherited the contract; 2,016 sites, we want to do a status update. I am unable to visit all the sites myself, so we are commissioning an audit to ascertain the status of the sites,” he said. The Minister also reaffirmed the government’s commitment to extending internet access to underserved communities, stressing the need to ensure that residents are not excluded from digital services because of where they live. The four facilities commissioned during the visit serve Nyameama No. 1, Nyameama No. 2, Dawia and Abenua. According to Mr George, some of the beneficiary communities do not have electricity, but the government is using solar-powered infrastructure to provide internet connectivity. He, however, called for the facilities to be upgraded from 3G to 4G technology to improve network performance and give residents a better digital experience.

items.title: Lutte contre le cancer du sein : L’hôpital Saint-Camille sensibilise et s’équipe d’une nouvelle IRM à Ouagadougou
items.description: Briser le silence autour du cancer du sein et encourager le dépistage précoce. C’est l’ambition des responsables de l’hôpital Saint-Camille. Ce 14 octobre 2026, à Ouagadougou, ils ont organisé une séance de sensibilisation consacrée à cette maladie. La rencontre a également été marquée par la bénédiction d’un nouvel appareil d’imagerie par résonance magnétique (IRM). le cancer du sein, selon les estimations de l’Organisation mondiale de la santé (OMS), a causé environ 694 000 décès dans le monde en 2024. Face à ce lourd bilan, l’établissement entend mieux informer les populations sur la maladie. Les échanges ont notamment porté sur ses signes d’alerte, sa détection et l’importance du dépistage. Souvent confrontées à un manque d’information ou à une prise de conscience tardive, certaines femmes consultent alors que la maladie est déjà à un stade avancé. À travers cette initiative, l’hôpital Saint-Camille entend contribuer à lever les tabous et à encourager un recours plus précoce aux services de santé. Des experts mobilisés autour des cancers féminins Plusieurs thématiques liées au cancer du sein et à celui du col de l’utérus ont été abordées au cours des échanges, animés par des experts de la santé. Les discussions ont permis d’éclairer les participants sur ces maladies, leur détection et les enjeux de leur prise en charge. La rencontre a enregistré une bonne mobilisation. Cette initiative, à en croire le père docteur Lucien Kaboré, directeur général de l’hôpital Saint-Camille, vise à renforcer l’information des femmes sur le dépistage et la prise en charge des cancers. Il a également annoncé la pérennisation de ce rendez-vous, organisé pour la deuxième fois après deux ans. « Nous prenons l’engagement que ce panel se tienne chaque année à l’occasion du mois d’Octobre rose », a-t-il assuré. Il a, par ailleurs, invité les populations à s’informer sur les dispositifs publics de prise en charge, notamment les cliniques mobiles et les subventions. Un nouvel appareil d’IRM pour renforcer le diagnostic En marge de la sensibilisation, la bénédiction du nouvel appareil d’imagerie par résonance magnétique (IRM) a constitué un autre temps fort de la rencontre. Selon le directeur général, cet équipement de dernière génération présente des capacités diagnostiques élargies. Il permet notamment de réaliser des examens cardiaques et des analyses plus poussées de certaines lésions suspectes. « Avec ce nouvel appareil, on pourra faire des examens qui contribueront davantage au diagnostic précoce, à la prise en charge et au suivi des différents cancers » , a expliqué le père docteur Lucien Kaboré. Si la sensibilisation constitue un premier pas, pour les initiateurs, l’enjeu reste désormais d’amener davantage de femmes à franchir le cap du dépistage. Un défi qui appelle une mobilisation continue des acteurs de santé et une meilleure accessibilité aux services de diagnostic et de prise en charge. Éléonore Savadogo Faso7 L’article Lutte contre le cancer du sein : L’hôpital Saint-Camille sensibilise et s'équipe d'une nouvelle IRM à Ouagadougou est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: 2027: APC coalition headed for rocks, Makinde campaign says
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The Makinde/Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has described the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council as a “Nebuchadnezzar Coalition” headed for political defeat in the 2027 general elections. The organisation accused the ruling party of relying on influential politicians to mask what it described as the failures of the President Bola Tinubu-led administration. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Ihediwa, the campaign organisation said the expanded APC campaign council could not win public acceptance for an administration it accused of presiding over economic hardship, insecurity, unemployment and declining living standards. It argued that Nigerians would judge the ruling party by the prevailing realities of their lives rather than the size of its campaign council or the political influence of its members. “This ‘Nebuchadnezzar Coalition’ is headed for the rocks as it cannot whitewash the failures of the APC administration, nor rewrite the painful realities confronting citizens,” Ihediwa said. The organisation challenged the APC to explain what it described as widespread poverty and deprivation, citing figures it attributed to the World Bank and the Federal Government. It claimed that 140 million Nigerians, representing 63 per cent of the population, were experiencing multidimensional poverty, while 113 million suffered deprivation in health, education and other basic needs. The campaign organisation also cited a reported government disclosure that 70 per cent of Nigerian children under 10 could not read and understand a simple sentence, arguing that the figures reflected the scale of the country’s social and economic challenges. “What explanation will the APC-led ‘Nebuchadnezzar Coalition’ offer millions of families who go to bed every night on empty stomach and our teeming hardworking youths whose destinies have been fractured by pervasive unemployment worsened by the APC’s anti-people policies?” it asked. The MDPCO further accused the administration of worsening hardship while surrounding itself with political allies whom it alleged lacked the popular support needed to translate political influence into electoral success. It dismissed the size of the APC campaign council as no guarantee of victory in 2027, insisting that voters would assess the government’s record rather than the political affiliations of those mobilised to campaign for it. “Elections are not won by the size of a campaign council or the number of powerful figures gathered. They are won by the confidence of citizens who must ultimately decide whether their lives have improved under the government seeking their votes,” the statement said. The organisation maintained that neither incumbency nor an expanded political alliance could shield the APC from voters’ verdict, adding that Nigerians had the constitutional right to demand accountability and change through the ballot box. It expressed confidence in the prospects of Seyi Makinde, whom it identified as its presidential candidate under the Allied People’s Movement (APM), saying his RESET NIGERIA agenda offered an alternative focused on accountability, productivity, dignity and prosperity. The campaign organisation said the 2027 elections would test whether the APC’s political machinery could overcome public dissatisfaction or whether voters would reject the ruling party. items.title: Pauvreté multidimensionnelle: plus d’un milliard de personnes en paient le prix
items.description: Pour la première fois depuis la création de l’Indice mondial de pauvreté multidimensionnelle en 2010, le nombre de personnes confrontées à des privations simultanées en matière de santé, d’éducation et de conditions de vie est en hausse. Selon un rapport du Programme des Nations unies pour le développement (PNUD) et de l’Initiative Oxford Pauvreté et Développement Humain (OPHI), publié le lundi 12 octobre 2026, 1,2 milliard de personnes vivent désormais dans une pauvreté multidimensionnelle aiguë, soit 51,5 millions de plus que lors de la précédente mise à jour comparable. La lutte contre la pauvreté mondiale connaît un revers préoccupant. L’édition 2026 de l’Indice mondial de pauvreté multidimensionnelle (IPM), élaborée par le PNUD et l’OPHI, rattachée à l’Université d’Oxford, révèle une augmentation inédite du nombre de personnes confrontées à plusieurs privations essentielles depuis la création de cet indicateur, en 2010. Sur les 1,2 milliard de personnes concernées, 617 millions sont des enfants, tandis que 83 % vivent en milieu rural. Ces chiffres mettent en évidence la vulnérabilité de millions de personnes, confrontées notamment aux difficultés d’accès à une alimentation suffisante, à l’éducation, à l’eau potable et à l’électricité. Pour Alexander De Croo, administrateur du PNUD, cette évolution doit alerter la communauté internationale. «La hausse de la pauvreté devrait être un signal d’alarme pour le monde entier», a-t-il déclaré, soulignant que ces statistiques traduisent des difficultés qui se cumulent et aggravent les conditions de vie des populations touchées. Le responsable insiste néanmoins sur la possibilité d’inverser cette tendance. «Cette situation est inacceptable. Mais elle n’est pas une fatalité. Nous savons que des progrès sont possibles», a-t-il affirmé, plaidant pour des réponses coordonnées aux différentes dimensions de la pauvreté. Une hausse aux causes multiples L’augmentation de 51,5 millions de personnes par rapport à la précédente mise à jour comparable s’explique en partie par la croissance démographique et l’actualisation des estimations. Dans 95 pays, aucune nouvelle enquête sur la pauvreté n’était disponible pour cette édition. La mise à jour des données démographiques y a entraîné une hausse estimée à 15,8 millions du nombre de personnes considérées comme pauvres. La variation restante reflète notamment les évolutions démographiques, les changements dans l’incidence de la pauvreté et les différences de couverture des indicateurs entre les enquêtes. Dans les 13 pays dont les estimations ont été actualisées, les résultats sont contrastés. L’Égypte, le Népal et le Tadjikistan ont enregistré une baisse significative à la fois de la proportion de personnes vivant dans la pauvreté multidimensionnelle et de leur nombre total. En Angola et en Zambie, la proportion de personnes pauvres a également diminué. Toutefois, la croissance démographique, plus rapide que le recul de la pauvreté, a entraîné une augmentation du nombre total de personnes concernées. Le Nigeria illustre, pour sa part, la fragilité des progrès réalisés. Après un recul significatif de la pauvreté multidimensionnelle au cours des années 2010, le pays a connu un retournement de tendance dans les années 2020, avec une hausse du taux de pauvreté et du nombre de personnes touchées. Des réussites qui montrent la voie Malgré cette tendance mondiale préoccupante, le rapport met en avant des progrès significatifs. Parmi les 89 pays disposant de données permettant de suivre l’évolution de leur indice, 33 ont réduit de moitié la valeur de leur IPM en moins de 15 ans, dont six en Afrique subsaharienne. L’Eswatini figure parmi les exemples marquants. En 15 ans, la proportion de sa population vivant dans la pauvreté multidimensionnelle est passée de 38,7 % à 8 %. La Chine a enregistré la baisse la plus rapide parmi les pays étudiés, réduisant de moitié la valeur de son indice en seulement quatre ans. Entre 2010 et 2014, la proportion de personnes vivant dans la pauvreté multidimensionnelle y est passée de 9,5 % à 4,2 %. Le Vietnam a également réduit de moitié la valeur de son indice en sept ans. Ces expériences montrent que des progrès rapides sont possibles lorsque les politiques publiques s’attaquent aux différentes formes de privation. Elles soulignent également l’importance d’inscrire les efforts de lutte contre la pauvreté dans la durée. L’objectif de 2030 sous pression L’édition 2026 de l’IPM rappelle l’ampleur du défi auquel les pays sont confrontés pour atteindre la cible 1.2 des Objectifs de développement durable (ODD), qui prévoit de réduire de moitié, d’ici à 2030, la proportion d’hommes, de femmes et d’enfants vivant dans la pauvreté sous toutes ses formes. À quatre ans de cette échéance, la hausse mondiale constitue un signal préoccupant. Toutefois, les résultats obtenus dans plusieurs pays montrent que l’objectif n’est pas hors de portée. Le rapport souligne la nécessité d’agir simultanément sur la santé, l’éducation et les conditions de vie, en accordant une attention particulière aux enfants et aux populations rurales. Entre aggravation mondiale et réussites nationales, le rapport du PNUD et de l’OPHI livre un constat sans appel: la pauvreté multidimensionnelle reste un défi majeur, mais son recul est possible. À l’approche de 2030, l’enjeu est désormais d’accélérer les efforts et de tirer les leçons des expériences réussies pour inverser durablement la tendance. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Pauvreté multidimensionnelle: plus d’un milliard de personnes en paient le prix est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Nigeria, Ghana in spotlight as Meta removes 3.7m accounts in scam crackdown
items.description: By Juliet Umeh Nigeria and Ghana have come under the spotlight after an international operation against online fraud networks in West Africa led Meta to remove more than 3.7 million accounts, Pages and Groups from Facebook and Instagram. The operation involved law enforcement agencies from 10 countries and 15 technology companies. It resulted in 28 arrests, the identification of more than 30 suspected scam centres and the rescue of 117 human trafficking victims in Ghana. Hosted by the United Kingdom’s National Crime Agency, NCA, in partnership with the United States Department of Justice, DOJ, and the Federal Bureau of Investigation, FBI, the exercise targeted criminal networks operating across West Africa. Meta described it as the first coordinated effort to broadly target scam networks in the region. Most of the removed accounts reportedly targeted victims in the United States and the United Kingdom, using profiles that impersonated American and British users. The networks also reached victims in Germany, Brazil, Japan, India, South Africa, Turkey and Nigeria. Technology partners included Google, Microsoft, OpenAI, Coinbase, Adobe and Starlink. According to the DOJ, Nigerian authorities arrested nine people and seized 53 electronic devices during the operation. In Ghana, authorities arrested 19 people in Sasaabi, near Accra, and seized 303 electronic devices. They also identified 117 people allegedly held against their will and forced to work in scam operations. The DOJ said the victims were awaiting repatriation to Nigeria. Authorities also identified 89 people allegedly defrauded, with estimated losses of about $8.3 million. The reported cases highlight the human cost of online fraud, including the alleged coercion of trafficking victims into criminal activity. The operation targeted several schemes, including cryptocurrency investment scams, fraudulent job offers, romance scams, online sales fraud and the impersonation of law enforcement officers and military personnel. Investigators also focused on recovery scams, in which fraudsters demand upfront payments from previous victims while promising to recover money they have lost. Microsoft suspended accounts suspected of involvement in the activities, while cybersecurity firm Silent Push mapped more than 35,000 malicious domains and nearly 700 communication channels linked to suspected scam centres. Coinbase said it identified more than 65 active scam victims and prevented potential losses exceeding $415,000. The DOJ said private-sector partners had identified more than $11 million in funds that could potentially be frozen. Meta’s Vice President and Deputy General Counsel, Chris Sonderby, said the operation showed why countries and technology companies needed to work together. “Scams are a global threat that demand a global response,” he said. Sonderby said leads on more than 30 suspected scam centres had contributed to arrests, victim rescues and cryptocurrency seizures. The NCA’s Deputy Director of Fraud, Nick Sharp, said international partnerships were essential because fraudsters could operate in one country while targeting victims in another. Sharp pledged continued cooperation with law enforcement and private-sector partners to disrupt criminal networks and the infrastructure supporting their activities. items.title: A Melilla, Felipe VI plaide pour le "bon voisinage" et la "bonne foi" avec le Maroc
items.description: Le Roi d'Espagne Felipe VI a plaidé, mercredi depuis le préside occupé de Melilla, pour une relation avec le Maroc fondée sur « la confiance » et « la bonne foi ». « L'Espagne et le Maroc doivent veiller en permanence à construire et préserver une relation de bon voisinage » , a dit Felipe VI dans un discours qui a clôturé un voyage de deux jours dans les enclaves de Sebta et Melilla. Le souverain espagnol a dit vouloir avec Rabat une relation bilatérale « tournée vers un avenir au bénéfice mutuel, à travers la paix, la sécurité, la stabilité et la coopération. Cela exige de la confiance et de la responsabilité fondée sur la bonne foi ». « Je crois que c'est possible et souhaitable », a-t-il poursuivi, appelant à « tous s'y engager ». C'est la première fois depuis son accession au trône en 2014 que Felipe VI se rend à Sebta et Melilla, les deux territoires dont les frontières terrestres sont les seules entre l'Union européenne et l'Afrique. La dernière visite d'un souverain espagnol à ces enclaves remontait à 2007 : Juan Carlos, le père de Felipe VI, s'y était alors rendu, provoquant une crise diplomatique avec le Maroc. Toutefois, cette invitation intervient au lendemain de la visite du roi Felipe VI à Sebta, au cours de laquelle le souverain espagnol a réaffirmé une « souveraineté espagnole non négociable » sur Sebta et Melilla, qu’il a présentées comme des territoires faisant partie intégrante de l’Espagne. Une position qui demeure en contradiction avec la position marocaine historique réclamant la fin de la présence espagnole dans les deux présides occupés. La visite royale a par ailleurs suscité des réactions dans certains milieux civils marocains, qui y ont vu un geste à forte portée politique, dépassant le cadre protocolaire, ainsi qu’une manière de consacrer une situation que le Maroc continue de contester. A cet égard, l'Alliance de la gauche, qui regroupe la Fédération de la gauche démocratique et le Parti socialiste unifié (PSU), a vivement condamné la visite du Roi d’Espagne , Felipe VI, à Sebta et à Melilla, deux villes revendiquées par le Maroc. Qualifiant cette initiative de « provocatrice », elle dénonce une tentative de légitimation de la présence espagnole et déplore l’absence de réaction officielle de Rabat. Dans un communiqué consulté par Hespress FR, l'Alliance estime que le déplacement du souverain espagnol vise à consacrer une « légitimité fallacieuse » à l’occupation espagnole des deux villes marocaines, en contradiction flagrante avec le droit et les usages internationaux. Cette visite constitue, selon elle, une nouvelle escalade à l’encontre du Maroc, de son Etat et de son peuple. L'Alliance affirme que la lutte pour la libération et l’unification de l’ensemble du territoire national se poursuivra, quelles que soient les pressions et les manœuvres. Au-delà de la condamnation de la démarche, l'Alliance de la gauche établit un lien entre le respect de la souveraineté marocaine et l’avenir des relations avec les partenaires européens. Elle estime que la coopération avec les pays de l’Union européenne, en particulier avec l’Espagne, suppose la prise en compte des revendications marocaines, notamment la récupération des territoires occupés et l’achèvement de l’intégrité territoriale du royaume. Dans ce contexte, l’appel à la confiance et au bon voisinage prend une dimension particulière. Pour être pleinement crédible, ce message ne peut être dissocié, selon ces voix, des questions historiques et de souveraineté qui continuent de peser sur la relation entre Rabat et Madrid, notamment autour de Sebta et Melilla. The post A Melilla, Felipe VI plaide pour le "bon voisinage" et la "bonne foi" avec le Maroc appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Ligue 1 : Gessime Yassine récompensé pour son geste technique du mois de septembre
items.description: Gessime Yassine a remporté le prix « Top Skills » de septembre, qui récompense le plus beau geste technique du mois en Ligue 1. L’ailier du Racing Club de Strasbourg a été distingué pour un enchaînement spectaculaire réalisé face à Troyes, lors de la troisième journée du championnat. Gessime Yassine continue de se faire remarquer en Ligue 1. À seulement 20 ans, le jeune Lion de l’Atlas vient de décrocher le prix « Top Skills » du mois de septembre, récompensant le plus beau geste technique du championnat français. Cette distinction lui a été attribuée à la suite de sa prestation face à l’ESTAC Troyes, le 6 septembre dernier, lors de la troisième journée de Ligue 1. Au cours de cette rencontre remportée par Strasbourg sur le score de 6-2, l’ailier marocain a réalisé un enchaînement technique qui n’est pas passé inaperçu. Dans la surface de réparation, Gessime Yassine a éliminé deux adversaires, dont un grâce à un petit pont, avant d’enchaîner avec une frappe qui n’a toutefois pas trouvé le cadre. Malgré l’absence de but sur cette action, son geste a séduit et lui a permis de décrocher cette récompense individuelle. Gessime Yassine remporte le Top Skills de @Ligue1 en septembre ▸ #LesTopsDeLaLigue1McDonalds pic.twitter.com/eWdT2lAF3C — Racing Club de Strasbourg Alsace (@RCSA) October 14, 2026 Cette nouvelle distinction vient récompenser les progrès du jeune Marocain depuis son arrivée au Racing Club de Strasbourg lors du dernier mercato hivernal. Déjà élu joueur du mois de septembre par les supporters du club alsacien, Gessime Yassine confirme sa montée en puissance. Titularisé depuis le début de la saison, l’ailier affiche des statistiques encourageantes avec deux buts et une passe décisive. Sa qualité technique, sa capacité à éliminer ses adversaires et son aisance dans les petits espaces constituent des atouts qui lui permettent de gagner progressivement en visibilité. items.title: Éthiopie : comment la désinformation sur les réseaux sociaux brouille la réalité de la guerre
items.description: En Éthiopie, la reprise des combats au Tigré s'accompagne d'une autre bataille, moins visible mais tout aussi déterminante : celle de l’information. Sur les réseaux sociaux, des vidéos détournées, des images anciennes et des contenus générés par l'intelligence artificielle alimentent la propagande et brouillent la compréhension du conflit. Alors que l’accès au terrain reste difficile pour les journalistes, comment distinguer les faits des manipulations ? Reportage.

items.title: Lifetime presidency needs NASS that cannot say no — Melaye
items.description: By John Alechenu, Abuja Former Kogi West Senator, Dino Melaye, has said Nigeria does not need another third-term controversy for a president to secure a lifetime presidency, arguing that all it takes is a National Assembly unable to assert its independence. Melaye spoke at a media briefing in Abuja on Wednesday, expressing concern over what he described as the legislature’s apparent inability to stand up to the executive. He said Nigerians and others concerned about the country’s future should be worried about the National Assembly’s seeming reluctance to exercise its constitutional independence. “A lifetime presidency does not require a president who stays forever. It requires a presidency that meets no meaningful restraint while in office,” he said. Melaye argued that the Constitution anticipated that presidents would seek political advantage, which, according to him, was why it established an independent legislature to provide checks and balances. He said recent developments had raised questions about whether the National Assembly was adequately discharging that responsibility. “The Police Act raised questions about speed and executive-initiated tenure. Rivers raised questions about supermajority. Tax law raised questions about integrity of laws passed. Electoral Act raised questions about whether procedure reflected the will of Parliament,” he said. The African Democratic Congress (ADC) chieftain also cited budget implementation, Service-Wide Votes, the proposed six-year tenure for elected officials, state police, the reported failure of oversight following the deaths of 30 miners in Niger State and what he described as legislators’ indifference to the implementation of Section 145 of the Constitution. He cautioned against treating the issues as proof of a single allegation but said they collectively warranted scrutiny of the legislature’s independence. “Don’t collapse them into one allegation. But together, they justify scrutiny of how much independence NASS still has,” he said. Melaye questioned whether the Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, and the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, had ensured that the Inspector-General of Police (IGP) was institutionally independent of the President. He said the concern was not about the competence or qualifications of the current IGP, Olatunji Disu, but whether adequate safeguards existed to protect the office from perceived political influence. According to him, the police play a critical role in election security, even though the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is responsible for conducting elections. “IGP does not count votes. But his men decide whether voting is safe,” he said. Melaye said reports on previous elections had documented allegations of partisan conduct by security agents, adding that the issue deserved particular scrutiny ahead of the 2027 general election. He pointed to the appointment of a former presidential aide as IGP following an amendment to the Police Act initiated by the President and passed by the National Assembly within a day. “President initiated it, Parliament passed it with speed, beneficiary was former CSO to President, successor is former ADC to same President. None proves rigging. But together, question cannot be dismissed,” he said. Melaye warned that the risk of a lifetime presidency did not begin with the cancellation of elections but with the weakening of institutions responsible for protecting electoral credibility. “It starts when institutions around elections depend on faith alone, without Parliament protecting that faith,” he said. He added: “No President should want a Parliament that cannot say no. Every President leaves office. Precedents remain. Every shortcut today becomes a weapon tomorrow. “We are not strengthening institutions. We are strengthening incumbents. Oath was to Constitution, not President.” The post Lifetime presidency needs NASS that cannot say no — Melaye appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Heritage Series notes: BoG promises more inclusive cedi with improved sizes, tactile features
items.description: The Bank of Ghana (BoG) has assured that the Heritage Series banknotes has been designed with improved tactile features to make the currency easier to be identified and handled by persons with disabilities. The Bank of Ghana is set to introduce a new series of banknotes from November 3, 2026, replacing the current designs with upgraded notes featuring enhanced security and durability features as the central bank seeks to strengthen currency integrity and improve cash management. Speaking during an engagement with the Federation of Disability Organizations, Head of the Currency Management Department of the Bank of Ghana, Dominic Owusu, said the Bank will continue to safeguard the integrity of the Ghana Cedi while making it accessible to all. The meeting brought together officials of the Bank of Ghana and representatives of the Federation of Person’s with disabilities to discuss concerns surrounding the identification and handling of Ghanaian banknotes. The engagement provided an opportunity for the Federation to share the practical challenges persons with disabilities face during cash transactions and make recommendations to improve accessibility under the proposed Heritage Series. Mr. Owusu said the discussions form part of the bank’s commitment to ensuring the new banknotes respond to the needs of all users, while strengthening collaboration with disability groups. “The bank remains committed to ensuring that the cedi is accessible, secure, durable and convenient to use by all segments of society, including persons with disability. In developing the heritage series of the Ghana Cedi Banknotes, the bank gave due consideration to the needs of persons with disability to ensure that your needs are adequately reflected in the design,” he said. The engagement therefore highlights the importance of sustained consultation between the central bank and disability groups to ensure their concerns translate into practical improvements in currency design and cash handling. Member of the Federation of Persons with Disabilities, Alexander Bankole Williams said the improvements in the Banknotes under the heritage series will improve cash handling experience for persons with disability. The Bank of Ghana says it will sustain engagements with disability groups to ensure their concerns inform efforts to improve the accessibility of the Ghana Cedi. The Central Bank is also calling on financial institutions, businesses and other cash handlers to ensure persons with disabilities can conduct transactions with dignity, without compromising their privacy or independence.

items.title: Airport police arraign suspect over alleged impersonation
items.description: By Dickson Omobola Airport Police Command has arraigned a 47-year-old suspect, Mark Agbor, over impersonation and unauthorized access to restricted areas. The command’s Public Relations Officer, ASP Mohammed Adeola, said the suspect, a staff member of Pathfinders International Limited, was handed over to the International Division of the Airport Police Command by the Provost Investigation Unit of the Nigerian Air Force, Ikeja, for further investigation and necessary action. Adeola, in a statement, said findings revealed that on October 7, 2026, the suspect allegedly posted a video on social media platforms in which he presented himself as the owner of two military combat helicopters and claimed that one of the aircraft was available for sale, apparently seeking interested buyers online. The statement reads: “Following the conclusion of investigations, the suspect was arraigned before a court of competent jurisdiction and the case has been adjourned to November 18, 2026. The Commissioner of Police, Airport Police Command, CP Ogunbode Olufunke, emphasised that conduct of this nature has serious security implications and could undermine the operations of security agencies. She stressed that the matter would be pursued in accordance with the law and commended the effective collaboration and coordination between the Airport Police Command and the Nigerian Air Force, noting that the successful outcome was made possible through joint efforts and inter-agency cooperation. “Olufunke further urged companies and stakeholders operating within the airport environment to strengthen employee screening, vetting and background checks to minimise the risk of security breaches and other acts capable of endangering airport operations. The Airport Police Command reiterates its firm resolve to uphold professionalism, inter-agency collaboration and the protection of lives and critical national infrastructure, while urging members of the public to remain vigilant and support efforts to maintain a safe and secure airport environment.” The post Airport police arraign suspect over alleged impersonation appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2027: Debate dodgers are ‘empty upstairs’ — Adebayo
items.description: By John Alechenu, Abuja Presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Prince Adewole Adebayo, has described politicians who avoid public debates as “empty upstairs”, saying they lack the intellectual capacity to address Nigeria’s economic and social challenges. Adebayo spoke on Tuesday night, October 13, during a live appearance on Talking It Real, hosted by Adeola Fayehun, where he challenged President Bola Tinubu and other contenders for the 2027 presidential election to an open debate. “I will meet them on any stage, under any condition,” he said. “If you are running for the presidency of a nation as complex as Nigeria, you must be ready to lay out your thesis. Those who avoid debates do so because they are empty upstairs. They have nothing to offer except recycled promises.” The SDP candidate said aspiring presidents must demonstrate intellectual transparency and engage in public scrutiny rather than rely solely on campaign rallies. He argued that candidates who avoid live debates were shielding themselves from scrutiny of their ideas and capacity to lead. “Leadership is about accountability, not shadow-boxing,” he said. Adebayo also used the programme to outline his policy document for the 2027–2031 period, titled Farewell to Poverty and Insecurity. He criticised the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) over what he described as anti-people economic policies, citing the removal of petrol subsidy and the reported 15 per cent import duty on refined petroleum products. According to him, the policies had contributed to rising inflation and increased economic hardship. Adebayo said an SDP administration would liberalise the energy sector and fully reopen government-owned refineries to boost domestic production. “Poverty in Nigeria is artificial. It can be eliminated in four years with production, accountability and ethical revolution,” he said. He added that the SDP was preparing to lead what he described as a “people’s election” aimed at replacing the current political class with purposeful leadership. The post 2027: Debate dodgers are ‘empty upstairs’ — Adebayo appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kidnapped CRIN workers regain freedom after six days
items.description: ….Rider: Kidnappers reportedly demanded N120m ransom for three victims By Adeola Badru IBADAN — Three persons abducted by gunmen at the Cocoa Research Institute of Nigeria (CRIN), Idi Ayunre, in Oluyole Local Government Area of Oyo State, have regained their freedom after six days in captivity, amid reports that a ransom was paid to secure their release. The victims reportedly returned to the institute’s premises at about 1pm on Wednesday and have since been reunited with their families. An insider, who confirmed their release to our correspondent, said the victims regained their freedom after spending six days in the kidnappers’ den. “Our members of staff who were kidnapped last Friday at the various institute locations have regained their freedom after six days in captivity. “They arrived at the institute at 1pm. They have been reunited with their respective families,” the source said. The source said a substantial ransom was reportedly paid to secure their release, although the exact amount paid was not immediately known. The development followed reports that the kidnappers had contacted the victims’ relatives and demanded N120 million for the release of the three abductees. Efforts to reach the Oyo State Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Olayinka Ayanlade, for confirmation of the victims’ release were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. The victims were identified as Mrs Eunice Babalola and Mr Kehinde Gbalajobi, both agricultural superintendents, and another man who resides in the institute’s Senior Staff Quarters but is not an employee of CRIN. Babalola and Gbalajobi were reportedly abducted while walking from the institute’s Central Nursery to the Senior Staff Quarters. A source explained that the two agricultural superintendents had gone to Babalola’s residence at the Senior Staff Quarters to collect some items, while a driver was expected to pick them up later. The source said: “Their intention was to pick something at Mrs Babalola’s residence (SS Quarters). The driver was to pick them later at SS Quarters while he would be returning with other Nursery staff from CRIN Nursery to the Main Office.” The source added that the two workers were seized on their way to the quarters, while the third victim, a resident of the Senior Staff Quarters who was not an employee of the institute, was also abducted. “The dedicated duo were picked by kidnappers on their way from Nursery to SS Quarters while another man (CRIN SS Quarters resident but not a staff of CRIN) was also kidnapped,” the source said. According to the source, the gunmen later attempted to abduct more people at the Central Nursery but were repelled by security personnel following an exchange of gunfire. “The kidnappers went to the Central Nursery to pick more victims but were repelled after a fierce exchange of gunshots with the security men on guard then,” the source said. The source further disclosed that the kidnappers subsequently contacted the victims’ relatives and demanded N120 million for the release of the three abductees. The post Kidnapped CRIN workers regain freedom after six days appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Anambra cautions commercial bus drivers against lawlessness
items.description: By Nwabueze Okonkwo ONITSHA — The Anambra State Government has cautioned commercial bus drivers against violating the rule of law and regulations governing the transport sector. The Commissioner for Transport, Hon. Edward Ibuzor, gave the warning while inaugurating the newly consolidated 20-member executive committee of the Anambra State Drivers Welfare Association (ASDWA). Ibuzor said that, in line with the state government’s policy direction, the transport sector must increasingly embrace proper identification, registration, digitalisation, accountability and effective regulation. He, however, stressed that genuine commercial drivers deserved an operating environment free from harassment, multiple taxation and unnecessary intimidation. The commissioner said the government was determined to bring all drivers’ associations in the state under one umbrella and a coordinated platform that would promote their welfare while strengthening government supervision, accountability and service delivery. He expressed concern that the commercial transport sector had, for years, been characterised by multiple associations, conflicting interests and leadership disputes, making effective coordination difficult. Ibuzor commended Governor Chukwuma Soludo for approving the inauguration of the association, following the dissolution of transport unions at the inception of his administration. He said the government’s objective was to promote unity rather than division, service rather than exploitation, and organisation rather than disorder. “Let me make it abundantly clear that this association is being inaugurated under the supervision of the Anambra State Ministry of Transport to provide an effective channel of communication between government and genuine commercial bus drivers across the state,” he said. He added that the newly inaugurated leaders must see their positions as a call to service and responsibility rather than an opportunity for personal aggrandisement or intimidation of drivers. “You must protect the welfare of your members, support road safety, discourage touting and illegal levies, maintain discipline at our parks and loading points, cooperate with government agencies, and ensure that commercial drivers contribute positively to the orderly movement of people and goods throughout the state,” Ibuzor said. Addressing the state chairman of the association, Hon. Moses Ohanebo, and other executive members, the commissioner charged them to lead with fairness, transparency and inclusiveness. “You are not leaders of a faction; you are being entrusted with the responsibility of bringing commercial bus drivers together and ensuring that every legitimate driver has a sense of belonging,” he said. Ibuzor assured the association of the ministry’s cooperation but warned that its leadership would be held accountable for its conduct and performance. He said the leadership’s success would be measured by improved unity among drivers, fewer disputes and illegal activities, and better discipline at motor parks. Some of the newly inaugurated executive members are Ohanebo, chairman; Pastor John Ogbonna, personal assistant to the chairman; Obinna Anisiobi, deputy chairman (administration); Francis Osondu, first deputy chairman (operations); Felix Asimonye, second deputy chairman (operations); and Azuka Nwabueze, third deputy chairman (logistics). Others are Ifeanyi Madukwe, general secretary; Innocent Okolie, assistant secretary; Aloy Onuh, financial secretary; Chinedu Molokwu, treasurer; Hon. Kingsley Adiele, PRO I; and Oligbo Chukwu, PRO II. Former chairmen of the association, Sir Nnamdi Okafor, Chief Paul Ejiofor, popularly known as Last Born, and Chief Emmanuel Ukatu, thanked God for the peace achieved within the association. They also commended the state government for reinstating the association and pledged their support for the government and the Ohanebo-led executive. In their acceptance speeches, Ohanebo and Adiele assured the state government and members of their determination to reposition the association and improve its operations. Ohanebo disclosed that the association had more than 40 branches across the state, identifying the removal of touts and criminals from motor parks as one of its priorities. He assured passengers that those boarding commercial vehicles across the state should expect quality transport services and improved protection for their goods and luggage. The post Anambra cautions commercial bus drivers against lawlessness appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: King Charles writes to Pope after lung cancer operation
items.description: Britain’s King Charles III is writing to Pope Leo XIV after the leader of the world’s Catholics had a cancerous tumour removed from his lung, a royal source said Wednesday. Charles, who is the head of the Church of England, would write privately to the pope to pass on his best wishes, the source said. He and Queen Camilla met with Leo last year at the Vatican shortly after he was elected as pontiff, becoming the first American pope. Part of the pope’s right lung was removed in Tuesday’s operation and the leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics is awaiting the results of tests to determine if the cancer has spread. The British monarch is also still being treated for an undisclosed cancer after being diagnosed in early 2024. As monarch, Charles is supreme governor of the Church of England, which was created in the 16th century when English king Henry VIII broke with the Roman Catholic Church. In ensuing centuries, relations have steadily improved, but in 2016, some fractures emerged, particularly over the ordination of women, which is forbidden within the Catholic Church. Last year, Charles became the first British monarch to pray publicly with a pope for 500 years in a service presided over by Leo XIV and broadcast live on Vatican media. items.title: Guinée: la BIDC signe une facilité de crédit renouvelable de 25 millions USD avec Topaz multi-industries SA pour renforcer l’industrie manufacturière
items.description: La Banque d’Investissement et de Développement de la CEDEAO (BIDC) a signé une facilité de crédit renouvelable de 25 millions USD avec Topaz Multi-Industries SA afin d’accroître la production industrielle en Guinée, de renforcer les chaînes de valeur locales et de soutenir la compétitivité du secteur manufacturier. L’accord a été signé le 13 octobre 2026. Acteur majeur du secteur manufacturier en Afrique de l’Ouest, Topaz Multi-Industries dessert une clientèle répartie dans plusieurs pays de la région, les marchés régionaux représentant une part importante de ses activités. Cette facilité permettra de soutenir et de renforcer la capacité de l’entreprise à s’approvisionner en matières premières, à maintenir sa production et à répondre à la demande croissante de produits industriels et de consommation courante. Au-delà du financement de la production industrielle, cette transaction témoigne de l’engagement de la Banque en faveur de la création de valeur ajoutée locale et de la réduction de la dépendance à l’exportation de matières premières brutes. En soutenant leur transformation en produits finis, cette facilité contribuera au développement des chaînes d’approvisionnement locales, à l’expansion de l’activité manufacturière et au renforcement de la capacité de la région à créer des emplois et à retenir une plus grande part des retombées économiques au sein de ses économies. S’exprimant lors de la cérémonie de signature, Dr George Agyekum Donkor, Président de la BIDC et de son Conseil d’Administration, a souligné l’importance d’un secteur manufacturier compétitif dans l’accélération de la transformation économique durable en Afrique de l’Ouest. Il a indiqué que l’accès au financement permet aux entreprises d’étendre leurs activités, de préserver les emplois et de renforcer la résilience économique. Il a ajouté que cette transaction illustre l’engagement de la BIDC à catalyser l’investissement du secteur privé et à soutenir le développement industriel dans la région. M. Roshan Ashok Vaswani, Directeur Général de Topaz Multi-Industries SA, a déclaré que cette facilité permettra à l’entreprise d’accroître sa capacité de production, de répondre plus efficacement à la demande du marché et de contribuer au développement industriel de la Guinée. Ce financement est aligné sur la Stratégie GRO (Croissance, Résilience et Optimisation) 2026-2030 de la BIDC, notamment à travers son accent mis sur le développement du secteur privé, la transformation industrielle et le développement des chaînes de valeur régionales. À travers ce partenariat, la BIDC réaffirme également son engagement en faveur des Objectifs de Développement Durable (ODD) des Nations Unies, en particulier l’ODD 8 relatif au travail décent et à la croissance économique, l’ODD 9 consacré à l’industrie, à l’innovation et aux infrastructures, ainsi que l’ODD 17 portant sur les partenariats pour la réalisation des objectifs. *********************************** À propos de la BIDC La Banque d'Investissement et de Développement de la CEDEAO (BIDC) est l'Institution de Financement du Développement des quinze États de l’Afrique de l’Ouest. Basée à Lomé, en République togolaise, la Banque s'engage à financer des projets et programmes de développement portant sur diverses initiatives dans les secteurs des infrastructures et des services sociaux de base, du développement rural et de l'environnement, de l'industrie ainsi que des services sociaux, à travers ses guichets dédiés aux secteurs privé et public. Les interventions de la BIDC se font sous forme de prêts à long, moyen et court terme, de prises de participation, d’octroi de lignes de crédit et mise en place d’accords-cadres de refinancement, des opérations d'ingénierie financière et services connexes. L’article Guinée: la BIDC signe une facilité de crédit renouvelable de 25 millions USD avec Topaz multi-industries SA pour renforcer l’industrie manufacturière est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: ‘We want answers’ – Family seeks probe into 14-year-old’s death 12 days after starting SHS
items.description: The family of a 14-year-old student of Abomosu STEM Senior High School in the Eastern Region is calling for a thorough investigation into his death, raising questions about his reported illness, treatment and the condition of his body. Daniel Boateng Mintah reportedly died on September 30, 2026, barely 12 days after reporting to the school to pursue his dream of becoming a computer engineer. His father, David Mintah, told JoyNews that the family received a call informing them that Daniel was unwell and needed an injection for suspected malaria. His mother, Joyce Mintah, had spoken to him earlier that day. Mrs Mintah sent GH¢50 after the caller requested money for the injection. The caller had also asked for Daniel’s health insurance details, she said. “Repeated attempts to obtain updates on his condition proved unsuccessful. At about 3:10 p.m., another caller, who identified himself as the school’s headmaster, asked us to come urgently,” Mr Mintah said. The couple set off for the school but received further calls directing them to Kwabeng Hospital, where they were told Daniel had been brought in dead. According to Mr Mintah, a doctor told them that Daniel had complained of a headache and stomachache before being brought to the hospital. The doctor reportedly advised them that a post-mortem examination would be needed to establish the cause of death. Mr Mintah said he found aspects of the explanations provided by the school and hospital inconsistent. “The following day, we requested that the body be transferred to Tafo. On October 4 and 5, we continued to receive information about its condition. “My suspicions deepened when I visited Daniel’s body at the mortuary on October 6 and observed blood coming from his nose, ears, mouth and head,” he recounted tearfully. He said the school had also told the family that Daniel left the orientation area to urinate but did not return. Mr Mintah urged the police to establish the circumstances surrounding his son’s death. “If he was murdered, the laws of Ghana must be applied to the letter. If he died a natural death, may his gentle soul rest in peace,” he said. The family appealed to the Inspector-General of Police, Christian Tetteh Yohuno, and the Minister for Education, Haruna Iddrisu, to intervene and ensure a thorough investigation. Mr Mintah also requested that Daniel’s body be transferred from the Tafo mortuary to the Police Hospital in Accra to support further investigations. He expressed concern that another family could suffer a similar loss if the circumstances remained unresolved. Mrs Mintah, who accompanied Daniel to school on the day he reported, recalled his determination to study computer science despite his father’s earlier suggestion that he consider another course. She said Daniel had repeatedly promised to make the family proud. “Having taken him with me to the market one day, he saw my daily struggles and told me, ‘Mummy, I will surprise you, okay,’” she recalled. She had looked forward to seeing him develop his interest in computers and planned to buy him ahenema, or “royal slippers”, to wear with his cloth during an upcoming Parent-Teacher Association meeting. Mrs Mintah said she had not been informed of any health problem before the call on September 30. “I’m at this point pleading with the entire country, investigative agencies, parents and everyone who feels connected to help push for justice for our son,” she said. “Wherever my Daniel Boateng Mintah is, I want him to know I love him so much,” she added, struggling to hold back tears. Daniel’s elder sister, Vivian Mintah, also recounted the family’s unsuccessful attempts to obtain updates after the request for money for an injection. She said she later questioned a teacher about her brother’s treatment. According to Vivian, the teacher said Daniel had visited the school’s sick bay complaining of a headache. She said he could not identify the injection administered and referred her to a nurse who was unavailable at the time. The family also raised questions about medication found among Daniel’s belongings returned by the school after his death. Vivian identified the medication as carbamazepine, olanzapine and multivitamins, saying the family had not purchased them for him. “My brother had never received psychiatric treatment and had not been diagnosed with a mental health condition,” she said. She called for investigators to establish the origin of the medication and why it was among his belongings. Vivian said Daniel’s last hospital visit before reporting to Abomosu STEM SHS had been for a dental appointment because he wanted braces. She described struggling to sleep and concentrate following his death. She also said she saw blood on his uniform and gauze around his head, hands and feet when she visited his body at the mortuary. Daniel’s former teacher, Ricky Kwabena Godigah, an assistant headmaster at Richenfel Academy at Dawhenya, Tema Community 25, described him as respectful, reserved and academically gifted, with a strong interest in computer science. He said Daniel had no record of indiscipline and that the school had encouraged him to pursue his ambition. “We all want answers to this unfortunate incident, and only a thorough investigation can establish the truth,” Mr Godigah said. He added that establishing the circumstances surrounding Daniel’s death was essential to preventing a similar tragedy. The reporter’s attempts to get someone from the school to speak on record have so far proved unsuccessful.
