items.title: Shettima dismisses Obi’s 2023 victory claim as ‘delusion of grandeur’
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Vice President Kashim Shettima has dismissed Peter Obi’s claim that he won the 2023 presidential election as a “delusion of grandeur,” while also slamming the former Labour Party presidential candidate’s reliance on what he called “bogus statistics” and economic prescriptions detached from Nigeria’s realities. Shettima spoke on Wednesday at the inauguration of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja, where he addressed Obi directly and questioned the evidence behind his claim about the last presidential election. “I respect Peter Obi, but he has gone beyond his mastery of philosophy to make bogus claims about winning the 2023 presidential election without producing evidence to buttress his assertion. This is called delusion of grandeur,” the Vice-President said. Furthermore, Shettima’s second line of attack focused on Obi’s economic prescriptions, which he portrayed as overly dependent on foreign comparisons and insufficiently adapted to Nigeria’s conditions. “Then comes my very good friend, Mr Peter Obi, the master of bogus statistics and incoherent economic prescriptions who seems convinced that his size 36 shirt for Bangladesh will somehow fit Nigeria’s size 52,” he said. “His fascination with foreign comparisons opens up a lot of peculiarities that distinguish one nation from another. Governance is an act that demands mastery of context, whether social, economic, or political.” The Vice President also criticised Obi’s use of statistics in making economic comparisons, while arguing that policies cannot be transferred wholesale between countries with different circumstances. “A country of over 200 million people cannot be governed through borrowed statistics and economic prescriptions detached from its peculiarities.” The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council inauguration, held at the Banquet Hall of the Presidential Villa in Abuja, formally brought the expanded campaign structure into focus as the ruling party prepared for the 2027 general election. items.title: No preacher has the right to impose beliefs on bus passengers – Kwesi Pratt Jr backs preaching ban
items.description: Veteran journalist Kwesi Pratt Jnr has defended restrictions on preaching in commercial vehicles, arguing that passengers should not be compelled to listen to religious messages during their journeys. Speaking on Accra-based Metro TV on Wednesday, October 14, amid controversy over the proposed ban on preaching and hawking in commercial vehicles, Mr Pratt Jr said the 1992 Constitution guarantees freedom of conscience, including the right to practise any religion or to have no religious belief. “I think it’s important to look at the 1992 Constitution. It governs everything. It’s the supreme law of the land. And the 1992 Constitution guarantees the freedom of conscience. Everybody is free to belong to whatever religion they choose, to believe whatever they believe, and also not to believe,” he said. Mr Pratt Jr questioned the basis for allowing preaching in public transport when passengers may belong to different religious groups or hold different beliefs. “So if you say that commercial transport should be free, for spreading the gospel, which gospel?” he asked. He gave an example of a bus travelling from Accra to Kumasi with a traditional priest, a Pentecostal Christian, a Bahá’í believer, a Hindu and a Muslim on board, each wanting to share their religious beliefs. “Can you imagine the confusion on the bus?” he asked, insisting that passengers should be able to travel without being subjected to religious messages they may not wish to hear. Mr Pratt Jr said the stress of long-distance travel was already considerable, with journeys to Kumasi sometimes taking six hours, and argued that unsolicited preaching could add to passengers’ discomfort. He also criticised preachers who, he said, board buses without paying and deliver messages that frighten passengers with descriptions of fatal road accidents and claims that prayer is the only way to prevent them. “The journey itself is stressful,” he said, describing what he considers an additional burden on both passengers and drivers. He questioned why opposition to the proposed restriction should be framed as an attack on Christianity, arguing that the issue was whether individuals had the right to impose their beliefs on others in a shared public space. “I have a right to also believe what I want to believe. Why should they be allowed to impose their beliefs on me?” he asked. Mr Pratt maintained that religious freedom should not give anyone the authority to dictate how others should live or what they should listen to while travelling. “You can’t come to my house and start telling me how to conduct my life and so on. It’s an infringement of my right,” he said, adding that “the bus station should be sanitized.”

items.title: Africa Maritime Security Forum opens in Accra with call for stronger continental cooperation
items.description: African security leaders and international partners have called for stronger continental cooperation, intelligence-sharing and sustainable investment to address evolving maritime threats, as the maiden African Maritime Security Forum opened at the Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre (KAIPTC) in Accra on Wednesday, October 14. The two-day forum, held under the theme “The African Maritime Landscape in Times of Geopolitical Uncertainty in 2026 and Onwards”, brings together maritime security practitioners, naval leaders, policymakers, academics and international partners to develop practical responses to threats affecting Africa’s coastal states and strategic shipping routes. The event has attracted 66 registered participants, with representation from Nigeria, Ghana, Côte d’Ivoire, South Africa, France, Denmark, Britain, Cameroon, Cape Verde, Togo, Madagascar, the United States, Kenya and Sierra Leone. Ghana’s Minister for Defence, Kenneth Gilbert Adjei, formally opened the forum, urging African countries to move beyond policy declarations and strengthen coordinated, intelligence-led operations to combat piracy, trafficking, illegal fishing and other forms of transnational maritime crime. He warned that maritime threats transcend national borders and require collaboration among governments, navies, law enforcement agencies, regional organisations, industry players and international partners. Mr Adjei stressed that Africa’s seas must be protected not only as strategic trade routes but also as vital sources of livelihoods, economic opportunity and sustainable development. He highlighted Ghana’s maritime security partnership with Denmark, citing training, simulation facilities and operational support for the Ghana Navy and other security institutions. KAIPTC Commandant calls for continent-wide approach The Commandant of KAIPTC, Air Vice Marshal David A. Akrong, said the expansion of maritime security discussions beyond the Gulf of Guinea reflected the increasingly interconnected nature of threats across Africa’s maritime domain. He noted that the new forum would connect security concerns affecting the Gulf of Guinea, southern African shipping routes and the western Indian Ocean, enabling countries to develop coordinated responses to shared challenges. While acknowledging significant progress in reducing piracy in the Gulf of Guinea through regional cooperation and frameworks such as the Yaoundé Architecture, Air Vice Marshal Akrong cautioned that the underlying causes of maritime insecurity remained unresolved. These include limited law enforcement capacity, weak coastal governance, youth unemployment, environmental degradation and marine pollution. He also highlighted renewed piracy concerns in the Somali Basin and western Indian Ocean, alongside smuggling, human trafficking and illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. Geopolitical instability beyond Africa’s borders was another major concern. Disruptions around the Red Sea, Bab el-Mandeb and Strait of Hormuz have contributed to changes in global shipping routes, increasing traffic around southern Africa’s Cape sea route and creating wider security and economic implications for coastal states. Air Vice Marshal Akrong called for stronger maritime domain awareness, greater use of technology, robust legal frameworks and strategies that address the root causes of insecurity. SADC identifies funding and capability gaps Professor Kula Ishmael Theletsane, Director of the Organ on Politics, Defence and Security Affairs at the Southern African Development Community (SADC) Secretariat, identified inadequate funding, fragmented policies, weak information-sharing and limited naval capabilities as major barriers to effective maritime security. He said SADC’s Integrated Maritime Security Strategy, adopted in 2022, sought to promote a broader approach to maritime governance. However, overlapping regional and continental frameworks, institutional weaknesses and differences in national priorities continued to complicate implementation. Professor Theletsane highlighted shortages of modern patrol vessels, aircraft and surveillance systems, warning that many countries lacked the capacity to monitor their exclusive economic zones effectively. He also raised concerns about maritime terrorism, drug trafficking, illegal fishing and insecurity around Mozambique’s Cabo Delgado province and the Mozambique Channel, where subsea cables and energy infrastructure face potential threats. To address these challenges, he advocated sustainable regional financing, interoperable maritime assets, harmonised legislation and improved coordination among regional bodies, including SADC, the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa and the East African Community. He cautioned that regional commitments must translate into practical action, supported by stronger institutions and consistent information-sharing. Denmark reaffirms support for African-led solutions Denmark’s Ambassador to Ghana, Jakob Linulf, called for stronger national maritime capabilities and regional cooperation to protect shipping routes amid geopolitical tensions and disruptions to global trade. He underscored the importance of maritime security to the international economy, noting that approximately 90 per cent of global trade is transported by sea. The Ambassador highlighted Denmark’s cooperation with African partners through its Peace and Stabilisation Programme, which has supported anti-piracy initiatives, maritime security training and capacity-building for military and civilian security personnel. He reaffirmed Denmark’s support for the implementation of the Yaoundé Code of Conduct in West and Central Africa and the Djibouti Code of Conduct in eastern Africa, stressing that effective cooperation is essential to safeguarding freedom of navigation. Mr Linulf also emphasised the importance of African ownership, arguing that international partnerships should strengthen local institutions and enable countries to develop lasting solutions to shared security challenges. Building on an established partnership The African Maritime Security Forum builds on collaboration among KAIPTC, the Royal Danish Defence College and the Security Institute for Governance and Leadership in Africa at Stellenbosch University in South Africa. Since 2022, the three institutions have organised annual maritime security conferences, initially focusing on the Gulf of Guinea. Discussions in Stellenbosch in 2024 and 2025 also examined developments in the Red Sea and their implications for African coastal states. The new continental platform represents an expansion of that partnership, recognising that maritime threats, shipping disruptions and criminal networks increasingly connect different regions. Participants are expected to examine the implications of geopolitical developments for African maritime governance and produce actionable recommendations to strengthen national, regional and cross-regional security policies.

items.title: La Bourse de Casablanca termine sur une note négative
items.description: La Bourse de Casablanca a fini sur une note négative mercredi, son indice principal, le MASI, cédant 0,44% à 16.967,31 points (pts). Le MASI ESG, indice des entreprises ayant la meilleure notation ESG selon Moody's ESG Solutions, a reculé de 0,84% à 1.253,32 pts, tandis que le MASI 20, qui regroupe les 20 valeurs les plus liquides, a progressé de 0,03% à 1.230,11 pts. Le MASI Mid and Small Cap, reflétant la performance des petites et moyennes entreprises cotées, a lâché 0,95% à 1.615,91 pts. Sur le plan sectoriel, les indices « Mines » (-3,02%), « Ingénieries et biens d'équipement industriels » (-2,52%) et « Chimie » (-1,47%) ont enregistré les plus fortes baisses. À l'inverse, les secteurs « Distributeurs » (+1,39%), « Sociétés de portefeuilles – Holdings » (+1,05%) et « Télécommunications » (+0,55%) ont signé les meilleures performances. Les échanges ont dépassé 183 millions de dirhams (MDH), réalisés principalement sur le marché central « Actions » et dominés par les transactions sur Sodep-Marsa Maroc (27,4 MDH), Bank of Africa (26,89 MDH) et Managem (19,34 MDH). La capitalisation boursière s'est établie à plus de 998 milliards de dirhams. Aux valeurs individuelles, les plus fortes baisses ont été accusées par Rebab Company (-4,95% à 94 DH), Aluminium du Maroc (-3,86% à 1.892 DH), Lesieur Cristal (-3,36% à 280,2 DH), SMI (-3,25% à 5.650 DH) et Managem (-3,23% à 1.500 DH). À l'opposé, Mutandis (+2,61% à 229,8 DH), Label'Vie (+2,21% à 3.935 DH), T2S Group Holding (+1,44% à 212 DH), Disway (+1,37% à 740 DH) et Cosumar (+1,09% à 176,4 DH) ont affiché les plus fortes progressions. 2027: I won’t go everywhere with you – Tinubu excuses self from APC campaign tours
items.description: Bayo Wahab President Bola Tinubu has told members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council not to expect him to accompany them to every campaign event ahead of the 2027 general election, saying he must remain focused on governance and the country’s economic responsibilities. Tinubu spoke on Wednesday at the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja, where he urged members to take the party’s message to Nigerians across the states and local government areas while he continued to attend to matters of governance. The president said he agreed with concerns that the demands of the campaign should not distract him from running the country, adding that Nigeria needed his attention at the moment. “You’ve warned me not to allow the rigour of the campaign to distract me from governance, I hear you. I am in full agreement with your decision. Nigeria needs more attention now,” Tinubu said. He told council members to excuse him from accompanying them to every campaign event, noting that his administration had bills to pay and international financial obligations to meet. “So, you will excuse me from going everywhere with you, we have bills to pay. The American creditors cannot wait,” the President said. Tinubu also said the government needed to attract investors who would commit to long-term investments in Nigeria and contribute to the future of the country’s children. “We want those investors to come in, be here to stay, to invest for the future of our children,” he said. The president, however, assured Nigerians that he would continue to engage them directly even as the campaign council took charge of mobilisation across the country. “However, I will still make time to speak directly with Nigerians, even as you lead the campaign in the states and local government areas,” he said. Tinubu described the inauguration of the council as more than a campaign activity, saying it represented a renewed commitment to Nigerians and the responsibilities of the ruling party. “We have not gathered merely to inaugurate a council. We have gathered to renew a covenant. A covenant with Nigerian people and the historic responsibility they have entrusted to us as Nigeria’s governing party,” he said. He added that the council was expected to communicate the administration’s vision, achievements and agenda to voters nationwide. “This council will carry our vision, our records and our agenda to every Nigerian, and it will carry them to victory every ward of this country,” Tinubu said. The president also commended APC members for completing the party’s congresses, recalling that some had predicted internal crises during the process. He said the party had overcome the challenges and emerged united, crediting members for participating in the process from the ward level to the national leadership. “ They said there will be implosion. We passed through it. We did not fail. You didn’t let us down. We got here together,” he said. items.title: The Rise of In-Office Remote Work
items.description: Home Depot, Instagram, Fidelity, and TikTok are just a few of the companies that have recently ordered their employees back to the office five days a week, part of a broader shift toward stricter return-to-office mandates. Such policies cut down on working from home, yet they don’t always cut down on remote work. Many employees now commute to the office only to spend each day on video calls with colleagues who are elsewhere, or even down the hall. They’re in the office but still working remotely. We are two economists who have spent years studying how remote work shapes learning, productivity, happiness, and career progression. We have been struck by how often people picture the alternative to working from home as an office where nearly everyone is together. The modern office looks very different from that ideal. Today, the alternative to working from home is often working in a sea of mostly empty cubicles. In a September survey of 1,835 college-educated American workers, we found that, on their most recent day at the office, more than 70 percent of respondents had at least one member of their team who was not in the building with them. As a result, roughly half of respondents had no fully in-person meetings. And more than a third had exclusively online meetings because their teams moved meetings entirely online whenever anyone was remote. For these workers, the commute to the office buys little more than a different background on their video calls. The commute is costly. The typical American spends 54 minutes getting to and from work in a day, which they rank among their most hated activities. Yet when colleagues are actually together, this commute can be worth it. [ Stephanie H. Murray: ‘Commuting is bad’—particularly for women ] In-person connection often unlocks the best parts of work. It sparks creativity; in an experiment published in Nature , pairs who brainstormed in person came up with about 14 percent more ideas than those brainstorming online. Face-to-face work also boosts mentorship, increasing the comments that people receive on their work by about 20 percent. Perhaps as a result, people consistently do better work when face-to-face with their colleagues and rate this work as more meaningful than work done alone. But these benefits are fragile. In our research, we find that having just one distant teammate weakens the connections among those sitting side by side, as team meetings move partially or fully online. Thus, any exposure to remote work in the office eliminates many benefits of the commute. Working remotely from the office has become so common because we have yet to shed two remnants of the pandemic era. The first is sprawl: Teams stretch across multiple locations. A typical team might have, say, a few employees who work in the same city, a couple who are fully remote, and one who works in a satellite office far away. So even if every teammate were in their office, the team meeting would still be largely online. During the lockdown, distance didn’t matter for jobs that could be done over Zoom. Many companies hired people far from their team’s central hub, and allowed existing employees to move farther away. In our analysis of data from one Fortune 500 firm, about 60 percent of corporate employees had at least one distant teammate after the pandemic, up from 20 percent before. Among small businesses, the distance between employees and the central office nearly tripled from 2019 to 2023, driven in large part by employees who live too far away to regularly commute to work. Many companies have simply accepted this geographic sprawl. If a team is already dispersed, managers may see nothing wrong with hiring a candidate in Detroit even though the team’s center of gravity is in Denver. Our analysis finds that job posts among Fortune 500 firms now list multiple possible office locations five times as often as a decade ago. Bad habits are another remnant of the lockdown. During COVID, many workers became accustomed to focusing on their own to-do list and churning through more tasks in less time. Now many still view in-office interactions with colleagues as distractions from their work. As they see it, going to the office means they spend time commuting just to lose more time chatting. That view misses the potential for these conversations to spark new ideas, propel others’ growth, and improve the quality of their work. Consequently, many stay home as much as they can get away with. Our analysis finds that the typical worker commutes in one fewer day than companies require: Ask for four and you get three. This might not sound like such a big deal, but on any given day, someone is likely staying home and causing their on-site peers to be on Zoom calls. When one person fails to show up, the office has less of a draw for the rest of the team. This is especially true for managers; if the leader stays home, the rank and file often follow suit. Pretty quickly, the people who initially followed the rules start to skip the commute too. [ Read: Revenge of the office ] Even when people do go into the office, many send out Teams or Zoom links rather than moseying over to a conference room. On their most recent day in the office, 52 percent of workers with meetings had at least one held online even though all the participants were in the same building. Skipping the schlep to the conference room can feel efficient. But this convenience cuts out the small moments that create deeper connections: the chat before the meeting starts, the debrief on the way back to your desk. Rolling back this trend of working remotely from the office feels Sisyphean. Reuniting colleagues who have scattered to the four corners of a Zoom screen seems impossible. And showing up in a conference room feels pointless when the other participants are a few doors down on their laptop. Mandating more time in an office has neither ensured that colleagues go to the same office nor that they meet in person rather than online. The result is that bringing people back to the office often relocates—rather than reduces—remote work. But an isolated workday doesn’t have to be the new norm. Companies could regather teams, by paying remote workers to relocate and refocusing hiring on each team’s central hub. When recongregating is impractical, they could hold regular off-sites. Companies could revamp performance reviews to reward the things that happen best in person: the creative breakthroughs, the mentorship moments. That way, conversations with co-workers would feel like essential parts of work rather than distractions from the solo tasks that people could do faster from home. Not every workday has to be in the office. But ensuring that in-office days are in-person days could make work feel more human.

items.title: NA speaker Sadiq issues production orders for 2 PTI lawmakers
items.description: Speaker of the National Assembly (NA) Sardar Ayaz Sadiq on Wednesday issued production orders for two PTI MNAs Sanaullah Khan Masti Khel and Dawar Khan Kundi. On Tuesday, the PTI urged Sadiq in a letter to issue production orders for its nine detained MNAs, including Khel and Kundi, ahead of the National Assembly and Senate sessions on Tuesday. In the letter, Chief Whip Amir Dogar claimed that nine PTI MNAs were “currently detained” and requested him to issue production orders for them to enable them to attend the session NA session that commenced on Tuesday. On Wednesday, Sadiq issued the production orders under the powers conferred by Rule 108 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the National Assembly, 2007. According to the production order, seen by Dawn , the speaker considered the presence of the two MNAs during the NA session, which was summoned by President Asif Ali Zardari on Oct 13, “necessary”, observing that they were currently in the custody of the Punjab police. “You are, therefore, directed to produce the aforesaid members … at the commencement of each sitting of the National Assembly before the sergeant-at-arms at the Parliament House, Islamabad, who shall, after the conclusion of the sitting, deliver them into your custody,” the order said. Copies of the order have been sent by the NA Secretariat to the secretary of the interior ministry, Punjab’s chief secretary, additional chief secretary and additional home secretary; the chief commissioner and inspector general of police of the Islamabad Capital Territory, and the sergeant-at-arms of the NA for “necessary action and coordination” to ensure the production of the named MNAs. The Centre on Sunday imposed emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, citing the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. Subsequently, several PTI leaders, including the non-functional chief minister of the province, Sohail Afridi, were taken into custody .

items.title: Turkish Government Takes Over Independent TV News Channel
items.description: Click to expand Image Halk TV general news coordinator Serhan Asker gives an interview to media after the government takeover of the channel, a police raid on the premises, and the announcement of an arrest warrant against its owner and 16 others. Halk TV, Istanbul, October 14, 2026. © 2026 Adem Altan/AFP via Getty Images Police carried out a dawn raid on the widely watched, independent news channel Halk TV on October 14, signaling its takeover by a government-appointed administrator who promptly ordered the station to end its live broadcast. Halk TV is close to the main political opposition New Party (Yeni Parti). Its journalists have reported on the imprisonment and trial of Istanbul’s mayor, Ekrem İmamoğlu, government moves to split the opposition, and persistent allegations of corruption in the ruling party. The seizure of the channel is part of a wider effort by the government of Recep Tayyip Erdoğan to restrict Turkish citizens’ access to independent news sources that has involved pulling the plug on several TV news outlets, prosecuting and jailing journalists and greatly escalating internet censorship. The Istanbul prosecutor’s office ordered the arrest of Halk TV’s owner—on accusations of bribery, money-laundering, and rigging tenders—along with 16 other people. As with other takeovers of media outlets, the financial crimes investigation provides a pretext for censorship. Halk TV will now be managed by the Savings Deposit Insurance Fund, a state body attached to the presidency, which has been used over the past ten years to manage companies under governmental administration that are subject to criminal investigations. Halk TV continued to report on matters of pressing public interest until the last moment: An anchor was conducting an interview about an investment fund scandal implicating prominent figures in Erdoğan’s party moments before the administrators cut the live broadcast, leaving viewers, instead, with a scene from an old Turkish film. The takeover of Halk TV came on the very day that İmamoğlu took to the stand to begin his defense in the main politically-motivated trial against him. The Turkish government’s steps to suppress and silence a TV station that broadcasts critical content violates not only the rights of the workers and journalists targeted but the public’s right of access to information and to freedom of expression. Most people in Türkiye rely on television over other media for news coverage. Halk TV has been a critical voice in a country where broadcast news is increasingly monotone and government aligned. The Turkish authorities should take immediate steps to reverse the takeover of the channel. A free, pluralistic media offering varied views and opinions is a cornerstone of a democratic society.

items.title: Techiman North MP fulfills promise with new CHPS Compound in Kokoago
items.description: The people of Kokoago, a farming community in the Techiman North District of the Bono East Region, are breathing a collective sigh of relief following the commissioning and handing over of a fully furnished CHPS Compound, ending years of struggle for access to basic healthcare. A Community’s Long Struggle For years, Kokoago residents faced a daunting reality: the absence of any healthcare facility in their community. The sick, particularly pregnant women, were forced to travel several kilometers to Wenchi or Techiman through what residents describe as a terrible road network. The consequences were devastating. Assemblyman for Abimagya Electoral Area, Abu Mark, recounted the harrowing experiences community members endured. “The situation has been terrible. Our pregnant women suffer the most. Some have lost their lives, and others have had to give birth in tricycles on these bumpy roads just trying to reach a hospital.” The lack of a nearby health facility meant that even minor ailments could become life-threatening emergencies, with the journey to the nearest hospital often proving more dangerous than the illness itself. A Promise Made, A Promise Kept In 2024, the community, through their traditional leaders (Nananom), placed their request before their Member of Parliament, who also serves as the Trade Minister, Elizabeth Ofosu Adjare. The plea was simple but urgent: they needed a healthcare facility close to home. DCE Adom Johnson recalled the moment the request was made. “The people, through Nananom, made their request clear to the MP in 2024. They needed a facility close to home.” Less than two years after that heartfelt appeal, the MP returned to Kokoago—not with words, but with action. A fully furnished CHPS Compound now stands as a testament to the promise fulfilled. A Facility with Added Benefits The newly commissioned facility comes equipped with more than just basic healthcare infrastructure. It includes a mechanized water system, ensuring a safe and constant supply of water—a critical component for any health facility and a brand-new motorcycle to aid the movement of staff. The MP expressed her joy at the completion of the project and her hopes for its impact on the community. “I am incredibly happy that this facility is finally here. The inclusion of the mechanized water system is a bonus. My hope is that this will drastically minimize maternal mortality in this area and bring healthcare to the doorstep of every resident,” she said. Call for Proper Maintenance The Bono East Regional Minister, Francis Owusu Antwi, who joined the commissioning ceremony, took the opportunity to advise the health personnel who will be working at the facility. He urged them “to treat the facility as your own”, emphasizing that “proper maintenance would ensure it continues to serve the community for generations to come”. Community Gratitude The mood in Kokoago was one of celebration and gratitude. Residents gathered to witness the historic moment, with traditional drumming and dancing marking the occasion. Speaking on behalf of the residents, Nana Ameyaa Tumfour II, Queen Mother of Kokoago, expressed the community’s appreciation. “We are grateful. We thank the MP and the government for this gesture. Our days of traveling long distances with sick family members are over.” A New Chapter For the people of Kokoago, the new CHPS Compound represents more than just a building. It symbolizes a promise kept, a lifeline secured, and a new chapter in their community’s health and well-being. The days of perilous journeys to Wenchi or Techiman for basic healthcare are over. Pregnant women can now receive prenatal care close to home. Children can be treated for common ailments without the risk of a dangerous journey. Families can access health services with dignity and ease. As the community celebrates this milestone, the CHPS Compound stands as a reminder of what can be achieved when leaders listen to the needs of their people and act decisively to address them.

items.title: Enterprise Trustees, Sinapi Aba launch ‘Asetenapa Plan’ to promote retirement savings among informal workers
items.description: For many Ghanaians who depend on daily sales and irregular incomes, saving towards retirement remains a challenge as immediate financial needs often take priority. To address this concern, Enterprise Trustees, in partnership with Sinapi Aba Savings and Loans, has launched the Asetenapa Plan, a pension solution aimed at helping informal-sector workers build financial security for their retirement. The initiative is designed to encourage market traders, small business owners and other self-employed workers to make regular contributions towards their future, regardless of how much they earn. Head of Advisory, New Business and Marketing at Enterprise Trustees, Ransford Mate-Kole, said the plan allows members to save daily, weekly or monthly, depending on their income and financial capacity. He noted that many informal sector workers continue working without a structured retirement arrangement, raising concerns about their financial security when they can no longer earn a living. “One day, we will have to retire. What are we retiring on? We’re urging workers to develop the habit of saving while they are still earning,” he noted. Beyond retirement savings, Mr Mate-Kole said the plan provides life cover, with a stated payment of 2,500 to beneficiaries in the event of a member’s death. Members hospitalised for more than two days at a Ghana Health Service-registered facility are also eligible for a daily payment of 50 for up to 30 days, according to the terms outlined at the launch. On the partnership, he said Enterprise Trustees would combine its pension management expertise with Sinapi Aba’s nationwide network and reach among informal sector workers to improve access to retirement planning and encourage more people to develop a savings culture. He explained that contributions are voluntary, allowing members to determine how much and how often they save, while a digital platform facilitates registration and contributions. Chief Executive Officer of Sinapi Aba, Aaron Rex Opoku-Ahene, said the success of the initiative would go beyond the number of pension accounts opened to include its impact on financial awareness, savings habits and the long-term security of beneficiaries. He stressed that every hardworking Ghanaian, irrespective of income, occupation, gender or location, deserves the opportunity to prepare for retirement. Mr Opoku-Ahene emphasised that workers in the informal sector, who often depend on daily earnings and lack regular employment benefits, deserve the same opportunity to plan for retirement as those in the formal sector.

items.title: Intégrité territoriale, stabilité et paix : l’ambassadeur du Yémen souligne le rôle du Maroc
items.description: L'ambassadeur de la République du Yémen auprès du Royaume du Maroc, Azzedine Saeed Al-Asbahi, a affirmé que la position marocaine à l’égard des évolutions de la situation au Yémen demeure constante et solidement ancrée. Il a souligné que les Yéménites gardent un souvenir positif du Maroc, estimant que, chaque fois que le Yémen a eu besoin d’un soutien marocain, celui-ci s’est toujours montré sincère et constructif. Lors d’une conférence de presse organisée mercredi au siège de l’ambassade du Yémen à Rabat, Al-Asbahi a indiqué que la République du Yémen n’avait, à ce jour, demandé aucun soutien militaire au Maroc. Cette déclaration intervient alors que se poursuit l’opération « Fajr Al-Yemen » (L’Aube du Yémen), qui vise à rétablir les institutions de l’État et à étendre l’autorité du gouvernement yéménite à l’ensemble du territoire national, dans le cadre du conflit qui l’oppose aux milices houthies. L’ambassadeur a également souligné que « le Maroc se tient aux côtés du Yémen » , comme en témoigne, selon lui, le message adressé par le roi Mohammed VI à la partie saoudienne à la suite des derniers événements. « Je n’ai pas besoin de témoignages ni de confirmations à ce sujet » , a-t-il ajouté. Le diplomate yéménite a par ailleurs estimé que le modèle marocain en matière de consolidation de la stabilité politique et du développement constitue une expérience positive. « Le Maroc s’est toujours tenu aux côtés du Yémen pour préserver son unité, garantir sa stabilité et consolider la paix. Lorsque nous avons eu besoin de lui au sein de la coalition arabe, il a été l’un des pays à s’engager sérieusement » , a-t-il déclaré. Il a également rappelé que le premier martyr de l’aviation en 2015 était un jeune Marocain. Il faisait référence au lieutenant Yassine Bahti, décédé lors du crash de son avion F-16 au Yémen, alors que les forces marocaines participaient à la coalition arabe contre les Houthis. L’ambassadeur du Yémen au Maroc a, en outre, souligné que son pays avait, de son côté, adopté une position claire et constante en faveur des causes du Maroc et de son intégrité territoriale depuis l’indépendance. « Aujourd’hui encore, le Yémen soutient l’unité du Maroc et la marocanité de son Sahara » , a-t-il affirmé. Concernant le conflit en cours contre les milices houthies, le responsable a indiqué que, depuis les accords de Stockholm de 2022, une orientation avait été privilégiée en faveur du gel de l’ensemble des opérations militaires et de l’instauration d’une trêve de longue durée, dans le but de consolider la paix dans le pays et de rétablir une situation normale. « Lorsque le lancement de l’opération “Fajr Al-Yemen” a été annoncé, le discours était clair : nous menons une guerre pour la stabilité et l’unité du Yémen, pour la stabilité de la région ainsi que pour la sécurité régionale et internationale, et pour le rétablissement des institutions de l’État », a-t-il expliqué. Évoquant les perspectives de la prochaine étape, le diplomate yéménite a déclaré que « cette question relève de la société yéménite, mais également de la responsabilité de la communauté internationale, qui doit faire face sérieusement à un groupe incontrôlé qui ne menace plus seulement la sécurité nationale du Yémen, mais constitue désormais une véritable menace à l’échelle régionale et internationale ». Le 5 octobre dernier, le président du Conseil présidentiel de direction, Rachad Mohammed Al-Alimi, avait annoncé le lancement de l’opération de libération « Fajr Al-Yemen », dont l’objectif est de rétablir les institutions de l’État, d’étendre leur autorité à l’ensemble du territoire yéménite, de libérer Sanaa et de mettre fin au contrôle exercé par le mouvement houthi. Le ministère yéménite des Affaires étrangères et des Expatriés avait alors indiqué que cette opération visait à mettre fin au coup d’État et à rétablir l’autorité de l’État sur l’ensemble du territoire national. Il avait également souligné que tout futur processus politique devait aboutir au rétablissement des institutions étatiques, à la limitation de la détention des armes, ainsi qu’à la préservation de l’unité, de la souveraineté du Yémen et de son indépendance décisionnelle. The post Intégrité territoriale, stabilité et paix : l’ambassadeur du Yémen souligne le rôle du Maroc appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Octobre Rose : AFG Bank et AFG Assurances facilitent l’accès au dépistage
items.description: © Internet AFG Bank et AFG Assurances ont organisé, ce mercredi 14 octobre 2026, une journée de sensibilisation et de dépistage gratuit des cancers du sein et du col de l’utérus dans les locaux des deux filiales du groupe AFG. Menée avec l’Office national de la santé de la reproduction (ONASR), l’initiative vise à sensibiliser et à dépister environ 400 personnes, tout en facilitant leur accès aux services de prévention. Faire du dépistage un réflexe plutôt que d’attendre l’apparition des symptômes. C’est le message porté par AFG Bank et AFG Assurances à travers cette journée organisée dans le cadre d’Octobre Rose 2026. L’opération a réuni des collaboratrices des deux institutions, des membres d’associations féminines, des partenaires ainsi que d’autres participantes. Au-delà de la sensibilisation, les organisateurs veulent permettre aux participantes d’échanger avec des professionnels de santé et de bénéficier directement de prestations de dépistage. Cette démarche s’inscrit dans la campagne nationale Octobre Rose, lancée le 1er octobre par le ministère de la Santé et du Développement social, avec un objectif annoncé de 110 000 personnes à dépister. Détecter tôt pour mieux soigner Pour les responsables d’AFG Bank et d’AFG Assurances, la prévention reste essentielle dans la lutte contre les cancers féminins. Dans son allocution d’ouverture, la directrice générale d’AFG Assurances, Cissé Adam Ba, a insisté sur l’importance du dépistage précoce, qui permet d’engager plus rapidement une prise en charge. « Détecté tôt, le cancer du sein se guérit dans neuf cas sur dix », a-t-elle soutenu. Elle a également insisté sur la nécessité de mieux informer les femmes, certaines hésitant encore à se faire dépister par peur, manque d’information ou en raison de contraintes familiales et professionnelles. Pour le cancer du col de l’utérus, la vaccination contre le papillomavirus humain (HPV), associée au dépistage, constitue également un important moyen de prévention. La sensibilisation ne concerne toutefois pas uniquement les femmes. Selon la directrice générale d’AFG Assurances, les hommes peuvent aussi être touchés par le cancer du sein et ont également un rôle à jouer dans la promotion du dépistage et l’accompagnement de leurs proches. De son côté, la directrice adjointe d’AFG Bank, Assa Deh, a estimé que chaque femme devait pouvoir accéder à une information claire et adaptée ainsi qu’au dépistage précoce. Une détection et une prise en charge rapides, a-t-elle rappelé, augmentent considérablement les chances de guérison. À travers cette initiative, les deux filiales du groupe AFG entendent aller au-delà de leurs activités bancaires et assurantielles en contribuant à des actions de prévention en matière de santé. Leur démarche repose notamment sur la proximité, la solidarité et la responsabilité sociale. La collaboration avec l’ONASR et les professionnels de santé vise ainsi à rapprocher l’information et les services de prévention des femmes. Les responsables des deux institutions ont enfin invité les participantes à ne pas laisser la peur ou les contraintes du quotidien les éloigner des structures sanitaires. Elles ont également été encouragées à sensibiliser leurs proches et à faire du suivi médical une habitude.

items.title: Le Niger sur Kalangou du 14 octobre 2026
items.description: Listen to « Culture, environnement, et tradition (Le Niger sur Kalangou) » on Spreaker. Dans l'emission de ce mercredi : Entretien avec Mounass, une slameuse nigerienne, pour echanger sur le slam, son parcours artistique et son univers musical. Dans la rubrique Environnement, direction Kournawa, dans la commune rurale de Goudoumaria, region de Diffa. Attikou Ousmane, responsable du site de recuperation des terres, explique le role de la fixation des dunes dans la lutte contre la desertification et la protection des cuvettes oasiennes, des terres agricoles et des habitations. L'echo des regions nous conduit ensuite a Ayorou, dans la region de Tillabery, a la decouverte des communautes Sorkos et Do, originaires du Mali et vivant aux cotes des populations locales. Moussa Illo Gaoudel, ancien agent de la Voix du Sahel et descendant de cette communaute, revient sur leur histoire et leurs activites au micro de Youssouf Alwali. Playlist Musicale Titre : les hommes de l'artiste Mounass Ban ga laifeinta de l'artiste Limanjah.

items.title: Gov’t working to ensure GAUA strike is called off by October 16 – Haruna Iddrisu
items.description: Education Minister, Haruna Iddrissu, said the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission (FWSC) is liaising with the Finance Ministry to resolve the issue of market premium and one-time research allowance. The allowance is the basis for the ongoing strike by the Ghana Association of University Administrators (GAUA). He expressed optimism that the industrial action would be called off by Friday for the universities to reopen, after the government reaches a consensus with the leadership of the Association. Mr Iddrissu was speaking at the 64TH Annual National Conference for the Conference of Heads of Assisted Secondary Schools (CHASS) in Ho in the Volta Region. He also announced that the government would honour its promise of paying promoted teachers their due salaries by the end of October 2026. Per his assessment, the first phase of arrears will be paid by Friday, October 16, 2026, based on the new grades of the promoted teachers.

items.title: Injures, accusations sans preuves…, Djénabou Touré met les communicants face à leurs responsabilités
items.description: En visite de travail à Kankan, ce mercredi 14 octobre 2026, la ministre de l’Administration du territoire et de la Décentralisation, Djénabou Touré, a dénoncé les injures, les attaques personnelles et les accusations non vérifiées sur les réseaux sociaux. Elle a appelé les communicants à promouvoir un débat responsable, respectueux des valeurs culturelles mandingues et des lois guinéennes. C’est à la Maison des jeunes de Kankan, devant des autorités administratives, locales et judiciaires, des responsables des services de sécurité et plusieurs citoyens, que la ministre a abordé cette question devenue récurrente dans l’espace numérique guinéen. Au cours de son intervention, Djénabou Touré a insisté sur les dérives liées à l’utilisation des réseaux sociaux, notamment les injures publiques, les attaques personnelles et la diffusion d’informations non vérifiées. Des comportements qu’elle juge incompatibles avec les valeurs culturelles mandingues et les principes de responsabilité qui doivent guider les acteurs de la communication. « Aujourd’hui, tout le monde est sur les réseaux sociaux. Les gens s’insultent de père et de mère. Cela ne relève pas de notre culture », a-t-elle déploré. Les communicants appelés à plus de responsabilité La ministre a également interpellé les responsables politiques et administratifs qui s’entourent de communicants chargés de défendre leur bilan et de relayer leurs activités. Selon elle, ces derniers ont certes pour mission de valoriser les réalisations de leurs mandants, mais aussi de relever les insuffisances, sans tomber dans les injures ni les attaques personnelles. « J’aime les communicants parce que leur rôle, c’est de dire le bon travail du groupement et de montrer aussi ce qui n’est pas bon, mais dans le respect, sans injures », a-t-elle expliqué. Pour Djénabou Touré, les responsables doivent assumer leur part de responsabilité et recadrer leurs collaborateurs lorsque ceux-ci franchissent les limites du débat public. « Si tu es ministre et que tu prends une personne comme communicant, si elle insulte une personne, tu dois la prendre et la mettre en garde ou en prison. Toi, le ministre, tu dois être la première personne à lui interdire cela », a-t-elle insisté. Elle dénonce les accusations sans preuves La ministre a par ailleurs dénoncé les publications accusant publiquement des individus de détournement de fonds ou de mauvaise gestion, sans vérification préalable des faits. Recevoir une information ou une accusation ne saurait, selon elle, justifier sa diffusion immédiate sur les réseaux sociaux. Elle a ainsi invité les communicants à mener les vérifications nécessaires avant toute publication, afin d’éviter les accusations infondées et les atteintes à la réputation des personnes mises en cause. « On t’appelle la nuit pour te dire que telle personne a mangé l’argent ou a pris l’argent. Tu te lèves pour aller sur les réseaux sociaux dire des choses sans faire l’enquête. Ce n’est pas normal », a-t-elle dénoncé. Djénabou Touré a également rappelé que certaines pratiques, notamment les injures publiques et la diffusion de photographies de personnes sans leur autorisation, peuvent, selon les circonstances et les dispositions légales applicables, exposer leurs auteurs à des poursuites judiciaires. Un appel aux parents pour l’éducation des enfants Au-delà des communicants, la ministre a exhorté les parents à mieux encadrer leurs enfants et à leur transmettre les valeurs de respect, de responsabilité et de bonne conduite, aussi bien dans la vie quotidienne que sur Internet. « Je demande aux parents de conseiller leurs enfants sur le bon chemin et le bon comportement. Si tu connais tes origines, tu ne vas pas tromper », a-t-elle déclaré, avant d’inviter l’assistance à promouvoir les bonnes pratiques et le respect mutuel. À travers cette intervention à Kankan, Djénabou Touré a rappelé que la liberté d’expression doit s’accompagner du respect des autres et des lois en vigueur. Pour les acteurs de la communication, l’enjeu est de défendre leurs convictions, de dénoncer les dysfonctionnements et d’informer les citoyens sans recourir aux injures ni relayer des accusations non vérifiées.

items.title: Nine-Inch Snails
items.description: Since September, giant snails have put one Florida neighborhood on high alert. No one in a roughly 300-acre zone in the city of Hialeah, just outside of Miami, is allowed to move yard waste or even a single brick into or out of the neighborhood without explicit permission from state authorities. Teams of scientists patrol the area in search of giant African land snails, enormous mollusks with tiny teeth, a foot bigger than a 5-year-old’s, and the tendency to spread the rat-lungworm parasite, which is exactly as delightful as it sounds. The snails, which actually grow to about eight inches in length, but can stretch—if nothing else, for headline-writing purposes—to nine inches, have worried Florida authorities since 1969. Since then, the state has spent millions of dollars fending off three infestations. One such operation took a decade to complete. Now, whenever a snail is found, inspectors from the state agriculture department’s Division of Plant Industry start patrolling. They set out bait and drench hatchling-harboring soil with anti-mollusk poison. Then they distribute mug shots to the public. (That step might seem unnecessary, given that we are talking about snails the size of chipmunks, but the experts I talked with all emphasized the importance of anti-snail awareness.) An area is considered clean only after it has been monitored and treated for three years. This time, the problem “seems to be limited to just one city block,” Paul Skelley, a main architect of the agriculture department’s crackdown, told me. But the response is full-bore. “We are serious about this snail in Florida,” Skelley said. “When you find these cancers, you don’t want to let them fester. You need to cut them out.” Skelley was part of the response to the last big infestation, which lasted from 2011 until 2021, and he sounds somewhat keyed up on the phone. Giant African land snails (also known as GALS) really are giant, and meaty and sweaty-looking, like a boxer’s fist just out of the glove. “When you see the whole body out moving around,” he said, “it’s unbelievable.” Earlier this century, the International Union for Conservation of Nature declared these snails one of the worst invasive species on Earth. GALS are prevalent across a thick belt of the globe, centered on the equator, and their slime trail is widening: After expanding their range from East Africa through Madagascar, India, and the Pacific Islands, they have lately been spotted in Argentina, Beijing, and, somehow, the Italian Alps. And as climate change makes more of the world warmer and wetter, they could conquer even more territory. Skelley considers his state a firewall. If the snails spread through Florida, “they could get quite a distance up the East Coast and inland” by hitching rides with humans, he said. Once they arrive somewhere new, GALS quickly multiply, and then make trouble just by being themselves. They love eating—beans, melons, ornamental flowers, shrubs—which is why they’re a hazard to agriculture. When cars run them over, the snails’ pointy shells can puncture tires. In search of minerals needed to grow their shells, they target stucco, eating our houses to build theirs. All of this can happen at a scale difficult to imagine. In the past, in Hawaii, brigades of the snails have blocked roads after rainstorms, eventually creating “a sort of mush of snail bodies and slime,” Robert Cowie, a snail researcher at the University of Hawaii at Mānoa, told me. “Cars were skidding.” In Keralam, in India, where recent monsoons created the wet, humid conditions in which the snails thrive, teachers clear them daily from schools and playgrounds. In Florida, during the most recent big outbreak, Skelley’s team would purge a yard the size of a couple of parking spaces and end up pulling out maybe 2,000 snails. On their own, the African snails move as one would expect, but Skelley jokes that they can go up to 70 miles an hour—“as fast as humans can move them.” And humans—whether they’re taken in by the snails’ charisma and impressive bulk, or just unaware of the threat—like to move them. Florida’s first brush with GALS began in 1966, when a young boy brought three home from a vacation in Hawaii. His grandmother found them, the story goes, and put them out in her North Miami garden. By 1973, those three snails had become 18,000, which the state located and destroyed. Harboring the snails anywhere in the United States without a permit is illegal. Still, federal, state, and customs inspectors continue to confiscate GALS from pet owners and breeders, from schools, and from the occasional religious practitioner who (allegedly) drinks their mucus . So far, Florida’s giant-snail infestations have all been in cities and suburbs, far from farmland or protected ecosystems. But “we’re scared to death that it’s going to be found in the Everglades, some national park,” Skelley said. “That’s the worst case.” Brazil is already there. An agronomist brought the snails into the country in 1988, most likely from Indonesia, in an ill-advised attempt to create a market for giant escargot. He sold snail-rearing kits to hundreds of hopefuls, who raised GALS in their backyards. “He had a very good intention,” Silvana Thiengo, the head of the Malacology Laboratory at the Oswaldo Cruz Institute in Rio de Janeiro, told me. But unfortunately, “Brazilians are not used to eating escargot.” The snails were soon discarded on streets and in rivers. Now Thiengo receives snail specimens from around the country, and most of them are giants. They’re in urban gardens, tempting dogs to play with them; in croplands, eating bananas, beans, and soy; in the middle of the Amazon and in the country’s massive tropical wetland, the Pantanal. She and her colleagues worry about how large numbers of giant snails might compete with native species “for food, for space, for everything.” A particular worry is the rat-lungworm parasite, which can infect humans, pets, livestock, and wildlife. In humans, the worms burrow into the brain and can cause coma and death. Although the disease is quite rare, Thiengo and her colleagues have found that human cases of it have been ticking up in Brazil. But at this point, the snails are so widespread in the country that little can be done about them. Although Brazil once ran national anti-snail campaigns, all have been phased out. In some cases, trying to get rid of these snails has caused more problems than it has solved—and again, not through any fault of the snails. In Hawaii, where GALS were originally introduced by a gardener who thought they would make a fun yard ornament, the Hawaii Department of Agriculture tried to control the giant-snail population by introducing more than a dozen new carnivorous snails to the islands in the 1950s. One of the new species, the rosy wolf snail, developed a taste for Hawaii’s hundreds of species of endemic land snails, or kāhuli . It ate so many that more than half of those species are now extinct. Still, once GALS have settled into the places they’ve invaded, something mysterious tends to happen, Cowie, the University of Hawaii snail researcher, told me. Their numbers die down. And the snails themselves get smaller. Hawaii’s snails are now at “a handleable level,” he said. “Maybe not acceptable, but you can deal with it.” The state has given up fighting them. Cowie hasn’t. After it rains, he goes out into his garden with a pair of tongs and a garbage bag. He picks them up, giant out-of-place snail after giant out-of-place snail. He can’t stop the forces—globalization, ignorance, human folly—that ferry snails from place to place. But he can stop the snails in his own yard. He considers it his responsibility to move them one last time—into his freezer, and then into the trash.

items.title: Le gouvernement français réduit le budget du Louvre, qui envisage de nouveaux tarifs
items.description: Le Louvre pourrait de nouveau faire payer plus cher ses visiteurs. Dans un entretien au Figaro publie le 14 octobre, son president-directeur, Christophe Leribault, a evoque une hausse des tarifs et une reduction du programme d'expositions face aux coupes prevues dans le budget francais pour 2027. Le gouvernement envisage ainsi de reduire les moyens d'un musee deja confronte a de graves problemes d'entretien. Le patrimoine francais soumis aux restrictions Le projet de budget prevoit une diminution de trois millions d'euros de la subvention de fonctionnement du Louvre. Le ministere de la Culture est lui aussi mis a contribution : ses credits reculeraient de 0,6 %, selon les chiffres rapportes par Le Monde . Pour justifier ces choix, la ministre de la Culture, Catherine Pegard, affirme que la culture « doit participer comme les autres a l'effort global ». L'etat entend donc economiser sur une institution qui abrite une part majeure du patrimoine francais. Dix millions d'euros resteraient affectes aux travaux du musee, sans compenser la baisse de ses moyens de fonctionnement. Les visiteurs appeles a payer davantage Le prix des billets a deja augmente. Passe de 17 a 22 euros en 2024, le tarif d'entree atteint, depuis janvier 2026, 32 euros pour les visiteurs qui ne beneficient pas du tarif reserve aux ressortissants et residents de l'Espace economique europeen. Selon Le Monde , le ministere mise desormais sur ces recettes supplementaires pour attenuer la baisse de sa subvention. Or, les revenus issus de cette tarification differenciee devaient initialement servir a financer des travaux. Le Louvre pourrait donc devoir puiser dans l'argent destine a sa renovation pour maintenir son fonctionnement, tout en reduisant ses expositions. Pour le public, la perspective est celle de billets plus chers et d'une offre culturelle moins riche. Un musee deja en quete de moyens Les restrictions surviennent dans un contexte preoccupant. Le vol des bijoux de la Couronne en octobre 2025 a mis en lumiere les defaillances de la securite du Louvre, tandis que ses infrastructures necessitent de lourds investissements. Devant le Senat, le 17 juin, Christophe Leribault avait deja prevenu : « Accumuler des œuvres dans un musee que l'on ne pourrait plus ouvrir au public serait un non-sens absolu. » Il insistait sur l'urgence des renovations. Alors que le Louvre a besoin de fonds pour preserver ses collections et accueillir le public, l'executif francais choisit de reduire son soutien au fonctionnement du musee. Une politique d'economies qui risque de se faire sentir aussi bien sur sa programmation que sur le portefeuille des visiteurs.

items.title: KAIPTC Commandant calls for continent-wide strategy to tackle Africa’s maritime security threats
items.description: The Commandant of the Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre (KAIPTC), Air Vice Marshal David A. Akrong, has called for a continent-wide approach to maritime security, warning that geopolitical tensions, organised crime and shifting global shipping routes pose growing challenges to Africa’s coastal states. Speaking at the maiden African Maritime Security Forum in Accra on Wednesday, October 14, Air Vice Marshal Akrong said the forum’s expansion beyond the Gulf of Guinea reflected the reality that maritime threats no longer respected regional boundaries. He said the new platform would connect security discussions covering the Gulf of Guinea, southern African sea routes and the western Indian Ocean, enabling countries to develop coordinated responses to shared challenges. The inaugural forum, held under the theme “The African Maritime Landscape in Times of Geopolitical Uncertainty in 2026 and Onwards”, brings together African maritime security practitioners, naval leaders, scholars and international partners to examine emerging threats and develop practical policy recommendations. Air Vice Marshal Akrong acknowledged that piracy in the Gulf of Guinea had declined significantly, attributing the progress to regional frameworks and cooperation, including the Yaoundé Architecture, which supports information-sharing and coordinated maritime patrols. However, he warned that the underlying causes of maritime insecurity remained persistent, citing limited law enforcement capacity, weak coastal governance, youth unemployment, environmental degradation and marine pollution. He also highlighted renewed piracy threats in the Somali Basin and western Indian Ocean, alongside transnational organised crime, including smuggling, trafficking and illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. According to the KAIPTC Commandant, these activities continue to undermine maritime security and threaten economic stability in coastal states. He further warned that geopolitical tensions and insecurity beyond Africa’s immediate borders were having direct consequences for the continent’s maritime environment. In particular, he noted that disruptions around strategic international shipping chokepoints, including the Red Sea, Bab el-Mandeb and the Strait of Hormuz, were contributing to the rerouting of global shipping traffic towards southern Africa’s Cape sea route. These developments, he said, demonstrated the need for stronger maritime domain awareness and greater cooperation to anticipate and respond to the wider security and economic consequences of global crises. Air Vice Marshal Akrong called for innovative strategies, greater adoption of technology and robust legal frameworks to address evolving maritime threats, stressing that responses must tackle the underlying drivers of insecurity rather than merely its symptoms. The two-day forum is expected to examine the implications of geopolitical changes for African maritime security governance and develop actionable recommendations to strengthen regional and cross-regional policies. The Commandant expressed appreciation to the Government of Denmark for its support and commended the Royal Danish Defence College (RDDC) and the Security Institute for Governance and Leadership in Africa (SIGLA) at Stellenbosch University for their partnership in organising the forum. Since 2022, the three institutions have collaborated under a maritime security programme supported by Denmark to convene annual conferences, initially focused on the Gulf of Guinea. Meetings in Stellenbosch, South Africa, in 2024 and 2025 also addressed developments in the Red Sea and their implications for African coastal states. The decision to establish the African Maritime Security Forum marks a broader ambition to promote safer seas and a prosperous blue economy across the continent. Air Vice Marshal Akrong urged participants to engage in open and constructive discussions, expressing confidence that stronger partnerships and practical solutions would help secure Africa’s maritime spaces and support sustainable economic growth.

items.title: Pilgrims caught up in Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia
items.description: By Timour Azhari RIYADH, Oct 14 (Reuters) - Pilgrims in Saudi Arabia to visit Islam's holiest sites may not have anticipated being caught up in an air war, but some experienced an attack by Yemen's Houthis first hand and others have been forced to change their plans. Footage of the massive blast that killed 13 people and wounded 300 in a Riyadh airport departure terminal struck by a Houthi missile on Saturday showed many passengers attired in the simple white clothes of Muslim pilgrims travelling to Mecca.

items.title: GRIDCo investigates Mallam substation fire as power restoration continues in Accra
items.description: The Ghana Grid Company Limited (GRIDCo) is investigating a fire outbreak at its Mallam substation after a fault affected one of the facility’s transformers in the early hours of Wednesday, October 14, disrupting electricity supply to parts of Accra. In a press statement issued on Wednesday, October 14, GRIDCo said the incident occurred at approximately 2.36 am, affecting power supply to areas served by the substation. The Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) responded promptly and successfully contained and extinguished the fire. READ ALSO: Fire at GRIDCo Mallam substation disrupts power in parts of Accra GRIDCo said electricity supply had been restored to some affected areas, while efforts were ongoing to reconnect customers in the remaining areas as quickly as possible. The company’s engineers are investigating the cause of the fire, and arrangements have been initiated to replace the affected transformer as soon as possible. GRIDCo apologised to affected customers and stakeholders for the inconvenience caused, thanking them for their patience and understanding as work continues to restore normal electricity supply. The company said it remained focused on restoring power to the outstanding affected areas as quickly as possible.

items.title: Dialogue AES-CEDEAO : Les experts de la Confédération peaufinent leur stratégie commune
items.description: Le Secrétaire général du Ministère des Affaires étrangères, Hermann Toé, a ouvert, ce mercredi 14 octobre 2026, à Ouagadougou, deux jours de travaux réunissant des experts de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES). Cette rencontre vise à préparer les prochaines négociations formelles entre l’AES et la Communauté économique des États de l’Afrique de l’Ouest (CEDEAO), prévues à Dakar. En prélude aux premières négociations formelles avec la CEDEAO, les experts des trois pays membres de l’AES se concertent afin de définir une position commune et de parvenir à un cadre de relations respectueux et profitable à leurs peuples. Selon le Secrétaire général du Ministère des Affaires étrangères, Hermann Toé, Chef de la délégation burkinabè à ses échanges, le rendez-vous de Dakar engage l’avenir des relations entre deux espaces que l’histoire, la géographie, les échanges et les peuples continueront de relier. « Notre responsabilité est donc de préparer une position rigoureuse, cohérente et pleinement conforme aux orientations du Collège des chefs d’État », a-t-il dit. La délégation des experts du Mali A l'en croire, ces deux jours de travaux porteront sur l’harmonisation de la lecture des enjeux et de la compréhension des dispositions soumises à négociation. Les participants devront également identifier clairement les lignes rouges, les marges de flexibilité ainsi que les points nécessitant un arbitrage politique. Enfin, ils s’attacheront à définir une stratégie, une méthode et une discipline communes de négociation. Le chef de la délégation des Hauts fonctionnaires du Niger, l'Ambassadeur Ousmane Alhassane, a pour sa part, salué la mise en place de l’architecture de négociation de la Confédération, notamment la création des groupes de travail (Task Forces) appelés à contribuer au processus. « L’objectif est de mieux préparer la feuille de route des négociations prévues à Dakar, ainsi qu’à la détermination des thématiques et des modalités devant encadrer les discussions entre les deux parties », a-t-il affirmé. La délégation des experts du Niger De son côté, le chef de la délégation des Hauts fonctionnaires du Mali, Mahamane Amadou Maïga a souligné l’importance de préserver les acquis de plusieurs décennies d’intégration régionale et de privilégier les intérêts des populations Ouest-africaines, notamment en matière de libre circulation des personnes et des biens. Cette réunion constitue ainsi une étape de concertation pour harmoniser les positions des trois pays membres et préparer les prochaines échéances diplomatiques entre la Confédération AES et la CEDEAO. Nadège KINDA Minute.bf

items.title: El Rey, en Melilla: “Estamos preparados para defender nuestros valores y libertades”
items.description: El Rey ya lo advirtió ayer en Ceuta y lo ha vuelto a hacer este miércoles en Melilla: ambas ciudades autónomas son parte innegociable de España. Es un mensaje recurrente desde que los pasados 30 y 31 de julio entraran más de 80.000 personas desde Marruecos por la frontera del Tarajal tensionando la convivencia en Ceuta y poniendo a la vecina Melilla en guardia ante entradas masivas u otro tipo de acciones desde el país magrebí. Seguir leyendo Sin pronunciamientos de entidad en Marruecos En Marruecos, la continuación de la visita real en Melilla apenas ha tenido eco este miércoles en algunos artículos de opinión en la prensa de bajo perfil crítico. En el plano oficial no se produjeron pronunciamientos de entidad,. Tan solo la Alianza de Izquierda, coalición que obtuvo ocho escaños en las recientes elecciones legislativas, emitió un comunicado cuestionando la presencia del monarca español en las “ciudades ocupadas” de Ceuta y Melilla, al tiempo que expresaba su “asombro” ante el silencio oficial del Gobierno marroquí frente a un “acto provocador” desde España. Tampoco se han registrado finalmente ninguna de las protestas anunciadas contra la visita de los Reyes cerca de las ciudades autónomas. Las fuerzas de seguridad marroquíes se desplegaron masivamente este miércoles en torno a la frontera de Ceuta para impedir una concentración convocada al mediodía, según informaron fuentes locales en Fnideq (Castillejos). En el paseo marítimo urbano, los agentes jalonaban cada 200 metros el recorrido hasta la frontera. El mismo despliegue era patente en las colinas que flanquean la ruta. Los accesos al cruce internacional se hallaban sellados con puestos de control, en los que se habían destacado tres camiones con cañones de agua a presión y vehículos dotados de protección antidisturbios.

items.title: 20% digital tax is not E-Levy – GRA boss
items.description: The Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) has assured the public that the 20% digital tax collection is not a reintroduction of the Electronic Transfer Levy (E-Levy), insisting that it is not introducing any new tax. The Commissioner-General of the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA), Anthony Kwasi Sarpong, made the remarks while appearing before Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee on Wednesday, October 14, 2026 Mr Sarpong said the data being received reflects payments made by Ghanaians to the government to support infrastructure development and the provision of social services. He explained that the authority’s focus is on improving revenue collection and ensuring that the government receives the revenue due to it. “The data we are receiving reflects accurately what Ghanaians have paid and that is coming to their government to support infrastructure and social services, as the tax is intended to be. “We would like to assure Ghanaians and citizens that this is in no way close to E-Levy. GRA is not introducing any tax. Parliament itself has not passed any tax close to that,” he said. The GRA boss said the authority is instead working to improve collection and ensure that the revenue is remitted to the government. His comments follow a report that commercial banks are preparing to apply a 20 per cent Value Added Tax (VAT) to payments for cross-border digital services and e-commerce transactions made with cards issued in Ghana.
